dervis-irab:1-9.t:
* Vocabulary:
(نُطْفَةٍ): in al-Miṣbāḥ: "نطف الماء ينطف, of the pattern of قتل: [the water] flowed. Abū Zayd said: نطفت القربة تنطف and تنطِف, نطفانا, when the water-skin dripped. And «النقطة» [Translator's note: so in the source; evidently «النطفة»] is the fluid of the man and the woman; its plural is نطف and نطاف, like برمة and برام. النطفة is also clear water, whether little or much. There is no verb for النطفة, i.e. no verb from its root-form is used for it." In al-Mukhtār, نطف is of the two patterns of قتل and ضرب.
(خَصِيمٌ): intensely contentious. There are two meanings in it. One is that he is an adversary of his Lord, denying his Creator, saying «من يحيي العظام وهي رميم» ("Who will give life to bones when they have decayed?"). The second is that he then becomes eloquent, arguing on his own behalf, combating opponents with obstinacy, disputation, sophistry and other kinds of impudence and malice. More of this will come in the Rhetoric section.
(دِفْءٌ): in al-Mukhtār: "الدفء is the offspring of camels, their milk, and what is benefited from them. Allah the Exalted said: «لكم فيها دفء». In the hadith: «لنا من دفئهم ما سلموا بالميثاق» ('ours is of their livestock as long as they keep to the covenant'). It is also warmth, a noun from دفئ الرجل, of the pattern of طرب and سلم; the masculine is دفآن and the feminine دفأى, like غضبان and غضبى; and one says رجل دفئ with the short form and رجل دفيء with the long form." In al-Miṣbāḥ: "دفئ البيت يدفأ, with hamza, of the pattern of تعب. They said: one does not say for the active participle دفيء on the pattern of كريم, but on the pattern of تعِب. And دفئ الشخص, the masculine being دفآن and the feminine دفأى, like غضبان and غضبى, when he puts on what warms him; and دفؤ اليوم like قرب [the day became warm]; and الدفء, on the pattern of حمل, is the opposite of cold." In al-Qāmūs: "الدفء, with kasra, and also with fatḥa on the second letter, is the opposite of the sharpness of cold, like الدفاءة; the plural is أدفاء. دفئ like فرح and كرم, and تدفأ, استدفأ and ادّفأ; أدفأه: he clothed him in warmth; الدفآن is the one seeking warmth, like الدفئ; and الدفء with kasra is the offspring of camels and their fur, the benefit from them, and what warms of wool and fur." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "الدفء is the name of that by which one is warmed, just as الملء is the name of that with which something is filled; it is الدفاء, clothing made of wool, camel-hair or goat-hair." So in summary الدفء has three meanings:
1- the opposite of coldness, i.e. warmth;
2- the garments with which one warms oneself;
3- what is obtained from camels by way of offspring, milk and benefits.
(تُرِيحُونَ): you bring them back to their resting-place in the evening.
(تَسْرَحُونَ): you take them out to pasture in the morning. Further discussion of al-irāḥa and al-tasrīḥ will come in the Rhetoric section. In al-Miṣbāḥ: سرحت الإبل سرحا, of the pattern of نفع, and سروحا: [the camels] grazed by themselves; and سرحتها: it is transitive and intransitive; and سرّحتها with doubling is for intensity and frequency.
(بِشِقِّ الْأَنْفُسِ): with their exertion; with kasra and fatḥa on the shīn, two dialect forms meaning hardship. There is a difference between them: the form with kasra means "half", as if half his strength goes because of the exertion he suffers; while the form with fatḥa is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of شق عليه الأمر شقا ("the matter was hard on him"), and its literal meaning goes back to الشق, which is a split. In al-Mukhtār: "الشق with kasra is half of a thing; الشق is also hardship, and from it is the saying of the Exalted «إلا بشق الأنفس»; this may be given a fatḥa."
(قَصْدُ السَّبِيلِ): القصد is a maṣdar in the sense of the agent, which is القاصد. One says سبيل قصد and قاصد, i.e. straight, as if it aims for the direction the traveller is heading for and does not deviate from it.
(جائِرٌ): deviating from straightness.

* I'rab:
(أَتى أَمْرُ اللَّهِ فَلا تَسْتَعْجِلُوهُ): (أتى) is a past verb and (أمر الله) its fāʿil (agent). The future is expressed with the past because it is like an accomplished fact from which there is no escape. The fāʾ is a conjunction; (لا) is prohibitive; (تستعجلوه) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive (لا); the wāw is the fāʿil and the hāʾ the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (سُبْحانَهُ وَتَعالى عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ): (سبحانه) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb; (تعالى) is a past verb; (عما) is contended for (tanāzaʿahu) by both (سبحانه) and (تعالى). (ما) may be maṣdarī, in which case it needs no resumptive pronoun, or relative, in which case a resumptive pronoun must be supplied; the clause (يشركون) has no grammatical position in either case. (يُنَزِّلُ الْمَلائِكَةَ بِالرُّوحِ مِنْ أَمْرِهِ عَلى مَنْ يَشاءُ مِنْ عِبادِهِ): (ينزل الملائكة) is a verb, a latent agent and a direct object; (بالروح) is attached to (ينزل), or to something omitted as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. accompanied by the Spirit; (من أمره) is attached to something omitted as a ḥāl; (على من يشاء) is attached to (ينزل); (من عباده) is a ḥāl. (أَنْ أَنْذِرُوا أَنَّهُ لا إِلهَ إِلَّا أَنَا فَاتَّقُونِ): (أن) is lightened [from أنّ], and it together with what falls within its scope is a badal (substitute) for His words (بالروح), i.e. He sends down the angels with "warn!", its implied form being «بأنه أنذروا»; the noun of (أن) is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the clause (أنذروا) is the content of an omitted verb of saying, i.e. «بأن الشأن أقول لكم أنذروا» ("with [the message] that the matter is: I say to you, warn"). You may also make (أن) explicative (mufassira), because الروح means revelation, which has the meaning of saying without its letters. (أنه) together with what falls within its scope stands in place of the object of (أنذروا), because it includes the sense of «أعلموا الناس» ("inform people"); or (أنذروا) has its original meaning and (أنه) is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. «أنذروا بأنه». The clause (لا إله إلا أنا) is the khabar (predicate) of (أنه); a detailed discussion of «لا إله إلا الله» has preceded. (فاتقون): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that implies an omitted condition), i.e. since the matter is as mentioned — His custom, Exalted is He, being to send down angels to the prophets and command them to warn people that He has no partner in divinity — then fear Me lest you fall short of its content. (اتقون) is an imperative verb and its agent; the nūn is for protection (nūn al-wiqāya), and the yāʾ of the speaker has been omitted out of regard for the verse-endings. (خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بِالْحَقِّ تَعالى عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ): (خلق السموات والأرض) is a verb and a latent agent; (السموات) is the mafʿūl bihi; (الأرض) is conjoined to (السموات); (بالحق) is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. "rightly"; (تعالى) is a past verb, its agent latent, implied as "He"; (عما) is attached to (تعالى); the clause (يشركون) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (ما). (خَلَقَ الْإِنْسانَ مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ فَإِذا هُوَ خَصِيمٌ مُبِينٌ): (خلق الإنسان) is a verb, a latent agent and a direct object; (من نطفة) is attached to (خلق), and (من) is for the starting point; in (فإذا), the fāʾ is a conjunction and (إذا) is the [particle] of surprise (al-fujāʾiyya); (هو) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (خصيم) is the khabar; (مبين) is a naʿt (adjective). (وَالْأَنْعامَ خَلَقَها لَكُمْ فِيها دِفْءٌ وَمَنافِعُ وَمِنْها تَأْكُلُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (الأنعام) is accusative by an omitted verb explained by what follows; (خلقها) is a verb, a latent agent and a direct object, and the clause is explicative; (لكم) is a fronted khabar; (فيها) is a ḥāl; (دفء) is a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is circumstantial; it may also be resumptive; and it is possible that (لكم) is a ḥāl from (دفء) and (فيها) the khabar. The noun from which [the verb] is diverted (al-ism al-mushtaghal ʿanhu), namely (الأنعام), occurs after a conjunction, not separated from the noun by «أمّا», and preceded by a verb, namely (خلق الإنسان من نطفة); so its accusative is preferred, because the one who uses the accusative conjoins a verbal clause to a verbal clause, while the one who uses the nominative conjoins a nominal clause to a verbal clause, and the matching of the two clauses is better than their mismatch. It might be said: in the nominative there is relief from supplying a governor, so each has something in its favour, and they ought to be equal rather than the accusative being preferred. The answer is that regard for matching is stronger than what was mentioned. (منافع) is conjoined to (دفء); (منها) is attached to (تأكلون); (تأكلون) is an imperfect verb and its agent. The fronting of the preposition and its genitive noun, which is governed by the verb, necessitates restricting it to it. (وَلَكُمْ فِيها جَمالٌ حِينَ تُرِيحُونَ وَحِينَ تَسْرَحُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (لكم) is a fronted khabar; (فيها) is a ḥāl; (جمال) is a postponed mubtadaʾ; (حين) is an adverb attached to something omitted as an adjective; the clause (تريحون) is the muḍāf ilayhi of [the adverb], and likewise His words (وحين تسرحون). Further discussion of al-irāḥa and al-tasrīḥ will come in the Rhetoric section. (وَتَحْمِلُ أَثْقالَكُمْ إِلى بَلَدٍ لَمْ تَكُونُوا بالِغِيهِ إِلَّا بِشِقِّ الْأَنْفُسِ): the wāw is a conjunction; (تحمل أثقالكم) is an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a direct object; (إلى بلد) is attached to (تحمل); the clause (لم تكونوا بالغيه) is an adjective of (بلد); (بالغيه) is the khabar of (تكونوا); (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (بشق الأنفس) is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the nominative pronoun in (بالغيه), i.e. with hardship upon you. (إِنَّ رَبَّكُمْ لَرَؤُفٌ رَحِيمٌ): inna and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (رءوف رحيم) are two khabars. (وَالْخَيْلَ وَالْبِغالَ وَالْحَمِيرَ لِتَرْكَبُوها وَزِينَةً): (والخيل) and what follows it is conjoined to (الأنعام), i.e. and He created these for riding and adornment. (لتركبوها) is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied «أن» after the lām of causation, and the preposition with its genitive noun is in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). (زينة) is conjoined to the position of (لتركبوها). The first was put in the genitive «بالجر» [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably "with the lām" is meant] because of the difference of agent, since riding is the act of those addressed, while the agent of creating is Allah the Exalted; as for (زينة), it is of His act, the Exalted, and therefore it is accusative, for the one who adorns and creates is Allah. It may also be parsed as accusative as a ḥāl from the hāʾ in (تركبوها). (وَيَخْلُقُ ما لا تَعْلَمُونَ): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, brought to show His all-encompassing knowledge and power, the Exalted, and that what their knowledge has reached is reckoned extremely slight compared to His vast knowledge. (وَعَلَى اللَّهِ قَصْدُ السَّبِيلِ وَمِنْها جائِرٌ): (على الله) is a fronted khabar; (قصد السبيل) is a postponed mubtadaʾ; (منها) is a fronted khabar; (جائر) is an adjective of a qualified noun which is the postponed mubtadaʾ, i.e. a deviating path (سبيل جائر), deviating from straightness. (وَلَوْ شاءَ لَهَداكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (لو) is conditional, of impossibility (imtināʿiyya); the object of (شاء) is omitted, i.e. had He willed your guidance; the lām connects the apodosis (jawāb) of (لو); (هداكم) is a verb, a latent agent and a direct object; (أجمعين) is a tawkīd (emphasis).

* Rhetoric:
1- Concision (ījāz) in His words «حين تريحون وحين تسرحون»: the two words «تريحون» and «تسرحون» enfold many meanings and images, which bestow on the owners of these livestock a beauty, splendour and grandeur beyond what one could picture. For when the herdsmen bring the livestock back in the evening to their resting-place, i.e. their shelter for the night, or send them out in the morning to the grassy pastures, and turn aside by the courtyards and houses, the camels grumble, the cattle low and the sheep bleat, and all of this echoes together with the shouting of the children and the talk of the noble women and maidens as they sway along, strutting and lively; joy embraces everyone, blessing dances and happiness flutters. He put the bringing back (al-irāḥa) before the sending out (al-tasrīḥ) because the beauty in the bringing back is greater: they come in with full bellies, brimming udders and honey-sweet milk.
2- The majāz mursal (metonymic trope) in His words «فإذا هو خصيم مبين»: because the fāʾ indicates immediate succession, yet his being a manifest adversary does not come immediately after his creation from a drop; rather it points to what his state will lead to. So it is a majāz mursal, the relation being consideration of what will be, as in the words of the Exalted «إني أراني أعصر خمرا» ("I see myself pressing wine"), i.e. grapes that will turn into wine.

dervis-irab:10-17.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تُسِيمُونَ): you pasture your animals; from سامت الماشية, when the livestock grazed, so they are سائمة, and their owner أسامها (sent them to graze). It is from السومة, which is a mark, because by grazing they leave marks on the ground.
Al-Suyūṭī said: the passive participle of أفعل never comes on the pattern فاعل except in a single word, namely the saying of the Arabs: أسمت الماشية من المرعى, so they are سائمة; they did not say مسامة. And His words, the Exalted, «فيه تسيمون» are from أسام يسيم «واجب» [Translator's note: so in the source; the word appears corrupt, perhaps «وأجيب» "and it has been answered"]: what is meant is "I sent them to graze, so they grazed, so they are grazing (sāʾima)", as you say: "I made him enter the house, so he entered, so he is entering (dākhil)".
(ذَرَأَ): He created. ذرأنا الأرض and ذروناها: we sowed it. ذرأ الله الخلق وبرأ ("Allah created and brought into being the creation"); among [His names] is al-Dhāriʾ, al-Bāriʾ, besides Him [Translator's note: the phrase «ومن الذارىء البارئ سواه» is obscure in the source; perhaps "and who is the Creator, the Maker, besides Him?"]. "O Allah, Yours is creation and bringing forth, and from You come sickness and recovery." And ذرأة has come upon him: the whiteness of grey hair when it first appears on the temples; ذرئ رأسه ذرءا; a man أذرأ and a woman ذرءاء: white-headed or white-faced. The poet said:
فمرّ ولما تسخن الشمس غدوة ... بذرءاء تدري كيف تمشي المنائح
(He passed, before the sun had warmed the morning, with a white-faced [she-camel] that knows how milk-loaned camels walk.)
i.e. she has been loaned out for milking many times and has grown used to it, so she walks along compliantly and does not refuse.
(طَرِيًّا): الطراوة is the opposite of dryness, i.e. tender and fresh. One says طرّيت كذا, i.e. "I renewed it". In al-Miṣbāḥ: طرو الشيء, on the pattern of قرب, so it is طري, i.e. tender, of evident freshness; and طرئ with hamza, on the pattern of تعب, is a dialect form, so it is طريء, of evident freshness. طرأ فلان علينا يطرأ, with hamza and two fatḥas, طروءا: he came upon us, so he is طارئ; and طرأ الشيء يطرأ also طرآنا, with hamza: it happened suddenly, so it is طارئ. أطريت العسل, with yāʾ: I thickened the honey; أطريت فلانا: I praised him with the best that is in him. The subtle point in describing the meat as fresh will come in the Rhetoric section.
(حِلْيَةً): in al-Miṣbāḥ: "حلي الشيء بعيني وبصدري يحلى, of the pattern of تعب: it seemed fine to me and pleased me. حليت المرأة حليا, with sukūn on the lām: she wore ornaments; its plural is حُلي, the base being on the pattern فعول, like فلس and فلوس. الحلية with kasra is the description, and the plural is حلى, with short alif, the ḥāʾ taking ḍamma or kasra. حلية السيف is its adornment. Ibn Fāris said: it is not pluralised. تحلت المرأة: she wore ornaments or acquired them; حلّيتها with doubling: I put ornaments on her or acquired them for her to wear. حليت السويق: I put something sweet in it until it became sweet." In al-Qāmūs and its commentary and others: الحلي, plural حُلي and حِليّ, and الحلية, plural حليّ and حلى against the rule: that with which one is adorned of wrought metals or precious stones. The statement of some commentators that [the ornaments are] pearls and coral is an explanation of the meaning of حلية, not a lexical explanation. What is meant by their wearing is the wearing by their women, because they are among them and because they only adorn themselves for their sake, so it is as though it were their adornment and their clothing.
(مَواخِرَ): sailing; المخر is [a ship's] splitting the water with its breast. From al-Farrāʾ: it is the sound of ships running before the winds. In al-Mukhtār: "مخرت السفينة, of the patterns of قطع and دخل: it ran, splitting the water with a sound; and from it is the saying of the Exalted «وترى الفلك مواخر فيه», i.e. sailing." In al-Asās: "فلك مواخر: they cut the water, splitting it with a sound. بنات مخر arose: they are summer clouds that cleave the air. استمخرت الريح: I faced the wind with my nose; and I went out أتمخر الريح, inhaling it. مخرت الأرض مخرا: I watered the land so that it would become good."
(تَمِيدَ): sway with you. In al-Mukhtār: "ماد الشيء يميد ميدا, of the pattern of باع; مادت الأغصان والأشجار: [the branches and trees] swayed; ماد الرجل: he strutted." In al-Qāmūs: "ماد يميد ميدا وميدانا: it moved and veered; [of] the mirage: it shimmered; [of] the man: he strutted, and he was struck by nausea and dizziness from drunkenness or sea-travel; and from it is المائدة: food, and the table with food on it, like الميدة in both senses."
(عَلاماتٍ): plural of علامة. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "أعلمت على كذا, with alif, of a book or something else: I put a mark on it. أعلمت الثوب: I gave it a border of embroidery or the like, which is the mark. The plural of العلم is أعلام and the plural of العلامة is علامات. علّمت له علامة, with doubling: I set for him a sign by which he would know it."

* I'rab:
(هُوَ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً لَكُمْ مِنْهُ شَرابٌ وَمِنْهُ شَجَرٌ فِيهِ تُسِيمُونَ): (هو) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (الذي) its khabar (predicate); the clause (أنزل) is the ṣila (relative clause); (من السماء) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أنزل); (ماء) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (لكم) is a fronted khabar; (منه) is attached to something omitted as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (شراب); (شراب) is a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of (ماء). (ومنه شراب) is a resumptive clause composed of a fronted khabar and a postponed mubtadaʾ [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably the second clause, «ومنه شجر», is meant]. (فيه) is attached to (تسيمون); the clause (تسيمون) is an adjective of (شجر); the bāʾ [sic; the preposition in فيه] is causal, i.e. because of it the trees grow. (يُنْبِتُ لَكُمْ بِهِ الزَّرْعَ وَالزَّيْتُونَ وَالنَّخِيلَ وَالْأَعْنابَ وَمِنْ كُلِّ الثَّمَراتِ): (ينبت) is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), implied as "He"; (لكم) is attached to (ينبت), and (به) is also attached to (ينبت), the bāʾ being causal; (الزرع) is a mafʿūl bihi; (الزيتون), (النخيل) and (الأعناب) are conjoined to (الزرع); (من كل الثمرات) is also conjoined to what preceded, (من) being partitive, i.e. "and some of all fruits".
(إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآيَةً لِقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ): (إنّ) is a particle resembling the verb; (في ذلك) is its fronted khabar; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (آية) is the postponed noun of (إنّ); (لقوم) is an adjective of (آية); the clause (يتفكرون) is an adjective of (قوم). (وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهارَ وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ): (وسخر لكم الليل) is a verb, a latent agent and a direct object; (لكم) is attached to (سخر); (الشمس) and (القمر) are conjoined to (الليل والنهار). (وَالنُّجُومُ مُسَخَّراتٌ بِأَمْرِهِ): the wāw is a conjunction; (النجوم) is a mubtadaʾ and (مسخرات) a khabar, and the clause is conjoined to the previous clause; (بأمره) is attached to (مسخرات). (إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآياتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ): the i'rab of its parallel has preceded. (وَما ذَرَأَ لَكُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ مُخْتَلِفاً أَلْوانُهُ): the wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is conjoined to (الليل والنهار), meaning what He created in it of animals, plants and inanimate things; you may also make it accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. "and He created and caused to grow", the meaning being the same. (لكم) is attached to (ذرأ), and (في الأرض) is also attached to (ذرأ); (مختلفا) is a ḥāl, and (ألوانه) is the agent of (مختلفا). (إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآيَةً لِقَوْمٍ يَذَّكَّرُونَ): its i'rab has preceded.
(وَهُوَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ الْبَحْرَ لِتَأْكُلُوا مِنْهُ لَحْماً طَرِيًّا): the wāw is a conjunction; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and (الذي) a khabar; the clause (سخر) is the ṣila; (البحر) is a mafʿūl bihi; in (لتأكلوا) the lām is for causation, and (تأكلوا) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied «أن» after the lām of causation, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (سخر); (منه) is attached to (تأكلوا); (لحما) is a mafʿūl bihi; (طريا) is an adjective. (وَتَسْتَخْرِجُوا مِنْهُ حِلْيَةً تَلْبَسُونَها): (تستخرجوا) is conjoined to (لتأكلوا); (منه) is attached to (تستخرجوا); (حلية) is a mafʿūl bihi; the clause (تلبسونها) is an adjective of (حلية). (وَتَرَى الْفُلْكَ مَواخِرَ فِيهِ وَلِتَبْتَغُوا مِنْ فَضْلِهِ وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ): the wāw is parenthetical; (ترى الفلك) is a verb, a latent agent and a direct object, and the clause is parenthetical; (مواخر) is a ḥāl, because the seeing is visual; (فيه) is attached to (مواخر); (لتبتغوا) is conjoined to (لتأكلوا); laʿalla and its noun; the clause (تشكرون) is its khabar.
(وَأَلْقى فِي الْأَرْضِ رَواسِيَ أَنْ تَمِيدَ بِكُمْ): (ألقى) is conjoined to (سخر); (في الأرض) is attached to (ألقى); (رواسي) is an adjective of an omitted direct object, i.e. "firm mountains"; (أن) together with what falls within its scope is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. out of aversion that it should sway with you and quake, like the one seized by dizziness, whose head spins when he sails the sea; (بكم) is attached to (تميد).
(وَأَنْهاراً وَسُبُلًا لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ): (أنهارا) and (سبلا) are conjoined to (رواسي), or are the object of an omitted verb, the implied form being «وجعل فيها» ("and He made in it"), because (ألقى) contains the meaning of «جعل»; the Exalted said: «ألم نجعل الأرض مهادا والجبال أوتادا». Laʿalla and its noun; the clause (تهتدون) is its khabar. (وَعَلاماتٍ وَبِالنَّجْمِ هُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ): (علامات) is conjoined to (أنهارا وسبلا); (بالنجم) is attached to (يهتدون); (هم) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (يهتدون) its khabar. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: (علامات) is accusative like a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. He did these things so that you might take lessons from them, and as signs, i.e. a lesson and an indicator in every course of travel, for one may be guided by mountains, rivers and paths. This is unintelligible speech; perhaps Abū al-Baqāʾ was right when he parsed it as the object of an omitted verb, i.e. "and He placed in it signs".
(أَفَمَنْ يَخْلُقُ كَمَنْ لا يَخْلُقُ أَفَلا تَذَكَّرُونَ): the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (al-istifhām al-inkārī); the fāʾ conjoins to something omitted; (من) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (يخلق) is the ṣila; the kāf is the khabar of (من); the clause (لا يخلق) is the ṣila of the second (من); the hamza is a second disapproval; the fāʾ is a conjunction; (لا) is negative; (تذكرون) is originally «تتذكرون», and one of the two tāʾs was dropped.

* Rhetoric:
1- Completion (al-tatmīm):
In the words of the Exalted «لتأكلوا منه لحما طريا» there is a tatmīm of precaution. It has preceded that tatmīm is a device consisting of a word which, if removed from the speech, would diminish its meaning; and also that it is of three kinds: tatmīm of deficiency, tatmīm of precaution and tatmīm of hyperbole; examples of it have preceded. We say here that He, Glorified is He, knew that if He did not describe the meat as fresh, it would not be thought liable to spoil; but it is well known that spoilage comes to fresh meat more than to anything else, so it was necessary to describe it thus, so that one would hasten to eat it for fear of its spoiling. The jurists have discussions about the flesh of fish that show intelligence and acumen, which we shall indicate briefly in the Benefits section. This «التميم» [Translator's note: so in the source, for «التتميم»] has a general benefit, namely teaching and guiding that meat should only be eaten fresh; physicians say that eating it after its freshness has gone is the most harmful thing there can be.

2- Shift of address (al-iltifāt):
In the words of the Exalted «وبالنجم هم يهتدون» there is a shift from the second person to the third. Its benefit is that, since guidance from the stars is the most useful and clearest of indications on land and sea, He drew attention to its greatness by shifting to the third person, to convey generality and so that it should not be thought that the one addressed is singled out for it; and He increased the emphasis by fronting the preposition and its genitive noun, as though hinting subtly that the guidance of anything other than the stars is slight and of no account.

3- The inverted simile (al-tashbīh al-maqlūb):
That is in the words of the Exalted «أفمن يخلق كمن لا يخلق», since the obvious requirement would be the reverse, because the address is to the idol-worshippers, inasmuch as they called them gods, likening them to Him, the Exalted; so they made what is not the Creator like the Creator. Hence the contrariety in the address: it is as if, because of their excess in worshipping them, and consequently their abasement and the regression of their minds, these had become for them like the original, and the true Creator had become the derivative; so the disapproval came accordingly. The inverted simile has many secrets, among them this one we have alluded to; and among them is that a person forgets that the thing compared-to is what should come first, out of his intense infatuation with the thing compared, and so he inverts the simile, as al-Buḥturī did in describing the pool built by al-Mutawakkil ʿalā Allāh, when he said:
كأنها حين لجت في تدفقها ... يد الخليفة لمّا سال واديها
(As it surged on in its outpouring, it was like the hand of the Caliph when its valley flowed.)
whereas what is customary is to liken the hand of the Caliph, in its outpouring of generosity, to the pool when it pours forth water.
The poets have followed the method of inversion often; some of them hit the mark, as Abū ʿUbāda al-Buḥturī did, and some erred and went astray. Abū Bakr al-Ṣūlī claimed that Abū Tammām erred in his inversion when he said:
طلل الجميع لقد عفوت حميدا ... وكفى على رزئي بذاك شهيدا
(O ruin of the assembled tribe, you have been effaced as one praised; and that suffices as witness to my bereavement.)
Abū Bakr said: "He meant: its having passed away praised suffices as a witness that I was bereaved. The proper way of putting it would have been: my bereavement suffices as a witness that it passed away praised; because the praiseworthiness of the ruin's affair is past and is neither a witness nor known, whereas his bereavement, through the grief he displays, is a known witness. That the present should be witness to the absent is more fitting than that the absent should be witness to the present." Al-Ṣūlī went on in his critique, denying that inversion occurs in the Qur'an, and [holding] that the inversion in the Qur'an which Abū Tammām's partisans cited in support of the inversion in his verse is not sound, despite what the commentators say, and that therefore analogy with it is not valid, so the inversion in Abū Tammām's verse is not valid.
This is an arbitrary and prejudiced stance on al-Ṣūlī's part, which drove him to deny what consensus has settled and logic indicates. We shall return to discussing him elsewhere in this book.

4- Predominance (al-taghlīb):
Also in the words of the Exalted «أفمن يخلق كمن لا يخلق», since what is meant by «من لا يخلق» is the idols, yet He used «من», which is for rational beings possessed of knowledge. That is because, when they worshipped them and called them gods, they treated them as beings possessed of knowledge; so «من» was used according to their belief and in accordance with what was ingrained in their natures. It is also for the sake of correspondence (al-mushākala) between them and the true Creator, who is referred to in His words «أفمن يخلق كمن لا يخلق». Al-ʿIzz ibn ʿAbd al-Salām said: this verse is problematic, because the rule of simile requires one to say «أفمن لا يخلق كمن يخلق»; and it cannot be said that they venerated the idols more than Allah, because they did not say that; they only said: "We worship them only that they may bring us nearer to Allah." [This is] unlike the words of the Exalted «أفنجعل المسلمين كالمجرمين» and His words «أم نجعل المتقين كالفجار»: since they used to say, "We shall be masters in the Hereafter as we were masters in this world", the answer came in accordance with their belief that they were higher and the believers lower.
Shaykh al-Islām Zakariyyā answered in Fatḥ al-Raḥmān: "The address is to the idol-worshippers; they went to excess in worshipping them until for them these became the original in worship and the Creator the derivative; so the disapproval came accordingly, so that they would understand what was meant on the terms of their own belief."

* Benefits:
Fresh meat and the flesh of fish:
Among the curiosities of the jurists is that they say: if a man swears not to eat meat and then eats fish, he has not broken his oath. If someone objects to them that Allah the Exalted called it meat, they say the matter rests on custom, and by people's custom, when meat is mentioned unqualified, fish is not understood by it. They said: do you not see that if he swore not to ride a beast (dābba) and then rode a disbeliever, he would not break his oath, even though Allah called him a beast in His words «إن شر الدواب عند الله الذين كفروا» ("the worst of beasts in the sight of Allah are those who disbelieve")? Likewise, if he destroyed a spider's house (bayt), he would not break his oath not to destroy a house. Likewise, the fat of the tail and the fat of the belly are not meat, because they are not used as meat is used, what is made from meat is not made from them, and they are not customarily called meat — and so on with these discussions, which may be consulted in the extensive works of jurisprudence.

dervis-irab:18-23.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِنْ تَعُدُّوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ لا تُحْصُوها): a resumptive clause, brought as a summary reminder of Allah's favours and bounties. (إن) is conditional; (تعدوا) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (نعمة الله) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (لا) is negative; (تحصوها) is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), the wāw being the agent and the hāʾ the direct object. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَغَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): inna and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis; (غفور) is the first khabar (predicate) of (إنّ) and (رحيم) its second khabar. (وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ ما تُسِرُّونَ وَما تُعْلِنُونَ): (الله) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (يعلم) is the khabar, and the agent of (يعلم) is latent (mustatir), implied as "He"; (ما) is a mafʿūl bihi; the clause (تسرون) is the ṣila (relative clause); (وما تعلنون) is conjoined to (ما تسرون). (وَالَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ لا يَخْلُقُونَ شَيْئاً وَهُمْ يُخْلَقُونَ): (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (يدعون) is the ṣila; (من دون الله) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause (لا يخلقون) is the khabar of (الذين); (شيئا) is a mafʿūl bihi; the wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (يخلقون) the khabar, it being passive. (أَمْواتٌ غَيْرُ أَحْياءٍ وَما يَشْعُرُونَ أَيَّانَ يُبْعَثُونَ): i.e. "they are dead", so it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; this is preferable to making it a second khabar of (الذين), though that is not impossible. (غير أحياء) is a naʿt (adjective) of (أموات), intended for emphasis. (وما يشعرون) is conjoined to (أموات), so it is like the second part [of the predicate] of the implied «هم», or it is a third khabar of (الذين). (أيان) is an adverb of (يبعثون), so it is attached to it. There is disagreement about the pronoun of (يبعثون): it is said to refer to the idols, the meaning being "and these gods do not know when the living will be resurrected" — and how much mockery there is in that! This is the most preferable of what has been said about it, and for this reason we have confined ourselves to it and been content with it. (إِلهُكُمْ إِلهٌ واحِدٌ فَالَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ قُلُوبُهُمْ مُنْكِرَةٌ وَهُمْ مُسْتَكْبِرُونَ): (إلهكم) is a mubtadaʾ, (إله) the khabar and (واحد) an adjective; the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that implies an omitted condition); (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (لا يؤمنون بالآخرة) is the ṣila; (قلوبهم) is a mubtadaʾ and (منكرة) the khabar of (قلوبهم), and the nominal clause is the khabar of (الذين). In (وهم), the wāw is circumstantial; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ and (مستكبرون) the khabar, and the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. (لا جَرَمَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ ما يُسِرُّونَ وَما يُعْلِنُونَ): (لا جرم) was discussed in Sūrat Hūd. We add here that (لا) is negative and (جرم) means «بدّ» ("escape/avoidance"); this is according to the origin. Here, however, (لا) has been compounded with (جرم) like the compounding of «خمسة عشر», and the two have been made to mean a verb whose meaning is "it is true and established"; (أنّ) together with what falls within its scope is its fāʿil. The clause (يعلم) is the khabar of (أنّ); the clause (يسرون) is the ṣila; (وما يعلنون) is conjoined to (ما يسرون). (إِنَّهُ لا يُحِبُّ الْمُسْتَكْبِرِينَ): inna and its noun; the clause (لا يحب) is its khabar; (المستكبرين) is the object of (يحب).

* Benefits:
(أَيَّانَ): a conditional noun of time that puts two verbs in the jussive, whether joined to «ما» or not, as in the words of the poet:
أيان نؤمنك تأمن غيرنا وإذا ... لم تدرك الأمن منا لم تزل حذرا
(Whenever we grant you safety, you are safe from others; and if you do not attain safety from us, you will remain on your guard.)
and the words of another, who joined to it the redundant «ما» for emphasis:
إذا النعجة الأدماء باتت بقفره ... فأيان ما تعدل به الريح تنزل
(When the tawny wild ewe spends the night in a desert, then wherever the wind turns it, there it alights.)
It is also an interrogative noun about time, like «متى». Its origin is «أي آن»: it is a compound of «أي», which contains the meaning of condition, and «آن» in the sense of "time"; after compounding they became a noun of condition or interrogation, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative as an adverb of time.

dervis-irab:24-29.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أَساطِيرُ): plural of أسطورة, like أحاديث, أضاحيك and أعاجيب, plurals of أحدوثة, أضحوكة and أعجوبة. In al-Qāmūs and al-Tāj: الإسطار, الأسطار, الأسطور, الأساطير, and also all of them with the hāʾ: what is written; the plural is أساطير; and [it means] a tale that has no basis.
(أَوْزارَهُمْ): plural of وزر, which is sin.

* I'rab:
(وَإِذا قِيلَ لَهُمْ: ماذا أَنْزَلَ رَبُّكُمْ قالُوا أَساطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ): (إذا) is an adverb for future time; the clause (قيل لهم) is the muḍāf ilayhi of the adverb; the clause (ماذا أنزل ربكم) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of (قيل). The statement is resumptive, brought to begin mentioning examples of the vices of the polytheists. (ماذا): it has preceded that two possibilities are allowed in it: either the whole of it is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a fronted object of (أنزل), or (ما) alone is an interrogative noun and (ذا) a relative noun in the position of nominative as a khabar (predicate). (أنزل ربكم) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause (قالوا) has no grammatical position; (أساطير الأولين) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. «هي أساطير الأولين» ("they are tales of the ancients") or «المنزل أساطير الأولين» ("what was sent down is tales of the ancients"). Supplying «المنزل» carries added eloquence, because it is then mockery, i.e. on the assumption that it was sent down, it is tales with nothing of value in them. (لِيَحْمِلُوا أَوْزارَهُمْ كامِلَةً يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ): the lām is for causation; (يحملوا) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied «أن» after the lām of causation; the wāw is the fāʿil; (أوزارهم) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (كاملة) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); (يوم القيامة) is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يحملوا). You may also make the lām [the lām] of consequence (lām al-ʿāqiba). In either case it is attached to His words (قالوا أساطير الأولين). So either the meaning is that they wronged themselves with their own hands and said what would cause them to bear the burdens, or that they did that ignorant and heedless, so that its consequence for them was that they bear their burdens, meaning the sins of their own selves which they committed. The secret of His saying «كاملة» will come in the Rhetoric section. (وَمِنْ أَوْزارِ الَّذِينَ يُضِلُّونَهُمْ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ أَلا ساءَ ما يَزِرُونَ): (ومن أوزار) is conjoined to «أوازرهم» [Translator's note: so in the source, for «أوزارهم»], so the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (يحملوا); (من) is partitive, i.e. and some of the burdens of those who go astray through their misguidance. This is the view of a group of commentators, headed by al-Zamakhsharī, al-Bayḍāwī and al-Jalāl. Al-Wāḥidī said: "The word (من) in His words «ومن أوزار الذين يضلونهم» is not partitive, because if it were partitive, some of the burdens would be reduced from the followers, and that is not permissible, because of his saying, upon him be blessing and peace: «لا ينقص ذلك من آثامهم شيئا» ('that does not reduce anything of their sins'). Rather it is for the genus, i.e. that they may bear [burdens] of the genus of the burdens of the disbelievers." This too is fine speech. The clause (يضلونهم) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (الذين); (بغير علم) is a ḥāl from the direct object, i.e. they mislead those who do not know that they are astray; it may also be from the agent to whom the misleading is attributed, the meaning being that they undertake misleading out of ignorance of the severe punishment that will follow for them. (ألا) is a particle of alerting; (ساء) is a past verb for expressing blame; (ما) is a tamyīz (specification), i.e. "a thing", or the fāʿil of (ساء); the clause (يزرون) is an adjective of (ما) on the first view, or its ṣila on the second. In either case the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bil-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being «وزرهم» ("their burden"). (قَدْ مَكَرَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ فَأَتَى اللَّهُ بُنْيانَهُمْ مِنَ الْقَواعِدِ): a resumptive clause, brought to console the Prophet ﷺ for what he endured of their obstinacy and scheming. (قد) is a particle of verification; (مكر الذين) is a verb and its agent; (من قبلهم) is the ṣila of (الذين); (فأتى الله بنيانهم) is conjoined to what preceded, being a verb, an agent and a direct object; (من القواعد) is a ḥāl, or a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أتى). (فَخَرَّ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّقْفُ مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ وَأَتاهُمُ الْعَذابُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لا يَشْعُرُونَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (خر) is a past verb; (عليهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (خر); (السقف) is the agent; (من فوقهم) is a ḥāl; (أتاهم العذاب) is a past verb, a fronted direct object and a postponed agent; (من حيث) is attached to (أتاهم); the clause (لا يشعرون) is annexed to the adverb. (ثُمَّ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ يُخْزِيهِمْ): (ثم) is a conjunction; (يوم) is an adverb attached to (يخزيهم); (القيامة) is the muḍāf ilayhi; (يخزيهم) is an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a direct object. (وَيَقُولُ أَيْنَ شُرَكائِيَ الَّذِينَ كُنْتُمْ تُشَاقُّونَ فِيهِمْ): (أين) is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as an adverb of place, attached to something omitted that is a fronted khabar; (شركائي) is a postponed mubtadaʾ; (الذين) is an adjective of (شركائي); the clause (كنتم) is the ṣila; the clause (تشاقون) is the khabar of (كنتم); (فيهم) is attached to (تشاقون). (قالَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ إِنَّ الْخِزْيَ الْيَوْمَ وَالسُّوءَ عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ): (قال الذين) is a verb and its agent; the clause (أوتوا) is the ṣila; the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil; (العلم) is the second object; inna and its noun; (اليوم) is an adverb attached to (الخزي), because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) that operates like the verb; (السوء) is conjoined to (الخزي); (على الكافرين) is the khabar of (إنّ). (الَّذِينَ تَتَوَفَّاهُمُ الْمَلائِكَةُ ظالِمِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ): (الذين) is a naʿt (adjective) of (الكافرين) or a badal (substitute) for it; the clause (تتوفاهم الملائكة) is the ṣila, the clause being a verb, a direct object and an agent; (ظالمي أنفسهم) is a ḥāl from the object of (تتوفاهم); (أنفسهم) is the muḍāf ilayhi; (تتوفاهم) is an imperfect in the sense of the past.
(فَأَلْقَوُا السَّلَمَ ما كُنَّا نَعْمَلُ مِنْ سُوءٍ): the fāʾ may be a conjunction, with (ألقوا) conjoined to (توفاهم), because it means «توفتهم» ("[the angels] took them"); or (ألقوا) may be conjoined to (قال الذين أوتوا العلم); or it may be resumptive. (ألقوا) is a verb and its agent; (السلم) is a mafʿūl bihi — السلم is making peace and humble submission; the clause (ما كنا) is the content of an omitted verb of saying, i.e. "saying"; (ما) is negative; (كنا) is kāna and its noun; the clause (نعمل) is the khabar of (كنا); (من) is redundant (zāʾida); (سوء) is genitive in form and accusative in position as a mafʿūl bihi.
(بَلى إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ بِما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ): (بلى) is a particle of answer; inna, its noun and its khabar; (بما) is attached to (عليم); the clause (كنتم تعملون) is the ṣila of (ما), and the clause (تعملون) is the khabar of (كنتم). (فَادْخُلُوا أَبْوابَ جَهَنَّمَ خالِدِينَ فِيها فَلَبِئْسَ مَثْوَى الْمُتَكَبِّرِينَ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that implies an omitted condition); (ادخلوا) is an imperative verb and its agent; (أبواب) is a mafʿūl bihi by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa); (جهنم) is the muḍāf ilayhi; (خالدين) is a ḥāl from the agent of (ادخلوا); (فيها) is attached to (خالدين); the fāʾ is resumptive; the lām is for commencement (lām al-ibtidāʾ); (بئس) is a past verb for expressing blame; (مثوى المتكبرين) is the fāʿil; and the one specified for blame is omitted, i.e. «هي» ("it").

* Rhetoric:
1- In the words of the Exalted «قد مكر الذين من قبلهم فأتى الله بنيانهم من القواعد فخر عليهم السقف من فوقهم» there is a representational metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya). He likened the state of all the false schemers who devise plots and conspiracies, who try to inflict harm and guile on the believers and set snares for them, to the state of a people who built a lofty building and supported it with the pillars and foundations of construction, and then the building collapsed from the pillars themselves, in that they weakened and were not strong enough to hold what had been raised upon them, so the roof fell in and came down upon them.
The scholars of rhetoric have mentioned that representation (al-tamthīl) has two manifestations. One is that the meaning appears from the outset in the form of a representation; the second is what comes after the meanings, to clarify them and fix them in souls. In both cases it clothes meanings with grandeur, raises their worth and doubles their power to move souls towards them and summon hearts to them. Consider the words of Abū al-Ṭayyib [al-Mutanabbī]:
ومن يك ذا فم مر مريض ... يجد مرا به الماء الزلالا
(Whoever has a bitter, sick mouth finds even sweet, limpid water bitter in it.)
Had he expressed the meaning by saying, for example: "The ignorant man, because of the corruption of his nature, conceives the meaning in other than its true form and imagines what is right to be wrong" — would you find this splendour? Would it have reached, in disparaging the ignorant and exposing his deficiency, what the representation in the verse reached? However much you exaggerate in depicting the false conspiracies that falsifiers devise and weave from behind a curtain, until, when they imagine they have been perfected and are able to make their opponents fall into their snares, they suddenly come to nothing — would that reach in your soul what is reached by the scene of the building that has risen high, soared and towered, which its builder has made so firm that he imagined it had guaranteed him permanence, and then, before long, its supports and bastions were shaken and it collapsed with and upon those within it? Below is a selection of verses of representation for you to measure by:
Ibn Lankak said, satirising a people whose appearance was fine and whose inner character was ugly:
في شجر السرو منهم مثل ... له رواء وما له ثمر
(In the cypress tree there is a likeness of them: it has fine looks but no fruit.)
And Ibn al-Rūmī said on the same theme:
فغدا كالخلاف يورق للعي ... ين ويأبى الإثمار كل الإباء
(So he became like the willow, putting out leaves for the eye but utterly refusing to bear fruit.)
Consider likewise the words of Abū Tammām:
وإذا أراد الله نشر فضيلة ... طويت أتاح لها لسان حسود
(When Allah wishes to spread a virtue that has been folded away, He provides for it the tongue of an envier.)
cut off from the verse that follows it — although the verse is clear in meaning — and then follow it with the next verse:
لولا اشتعال النار فيما جاورت ... ما كان يعرف طيب عرف العود
(Were it not for the fire blazing in what is near it, the sweetness of the scent of aloeswood would not be known.)
and see whether the meaning unfolded its full garment, revealed the hidden part of its ornament and adornment, and earned full precedence, except through the last verse and the representation and imagery in it.
There will come, among the marvels of representation in our book, what will astonish minds.

Return to the verse:
The verse with which we are concerned is among the highest that representation reaches, and it is enduring, not changing with the change of times and places. Building was and still is a symbol of strength, novelty and wealth, and its crumbling and toppling represents, in ancient and modern times alike, the disappearance and passing away of all that. That is because the representational metaphor is based on simile, so it is no wonder that tastes differ «فبها» [Translator's note: so in the source, for «فيها»] with the difference of times, just as they differed in appreciating simile. Here we are today, unable to relish many of the metaphors inspired by past environments, which remain frozen clichés whose wording dazzles us more than their meaning illuminates our souls. As for the metaphor that transcends the circumstances of time and place and secures for itself a freshness lasting as long as time, it is the metaphor that achieves the speaker's aim, in which the image compared-to is clear and familiar, depicting what it wants to depict with clarity, effect and concision, and to which tributaries are added — like this verse, when He said «فخر عليهم السقف من فوقهم». He reinforced the representation with His words «من فوقهم», since a roof only falls from above, because by its falling above them He conveyed that they were beneath it, thus removing the possibility that they were not present beneath it; and He emphasised the nullification of their conspiracies by their dying under the effect of what they had set up for others, as the proverb says: "Whoever digs a pit for his brother falls into it."
2- Precaution (al-iḥtirās):
In the words of the Exalted «فخر عليهم السقف من فوقهم». Someone might say: a roof can only be from above, so what is the point of mentioning «من فوقهم»? The answer is that it is a precaution against the possibility that the roof might be a floor relative to others, for many roofs are a floor for one people and a roof for another people. So Allah the Exalted removed this possibility with two expressions, namely His word «عليهم» and His word «خر», because it is only used of what descends or falls from high to low.
Some critics have cited a verse among the examples of faults, namely:
زياد بن عين عينه تحت حاجبه ... وبيض الثنايا تحت خضرة شاربه
(Ziyād ibn ʿAyn: his eye is beneath his eyebrow, and his white front teeth are beneath the darkness of his moustache.)
He said: the fault in it is that the eye is never anywhere but beneath the eyebrow, and the front teeth beneath the moustache. It was said in reply to this fault-finder: the poet meant that the one praised was created in the finest form and was born so; he was not born misshapen or of defective appearance, and nothing befell him while an embryo to diminish or disfigure his form.
Ibn al-Aʿrābī said: "He only said «من فوقهم» to let you know that they were located beneath it. The Arabs say: 'A roof fell on us' and 'A wall collapsed on us' when one owns it, even if it did not fall on him. So He brought His words «من فوقهم» to remove this doubt that exists in the speech of the Arabs." This is acceptable speech.

dervis-irab:30-34.t:
* I'rab:
(وَقِيلَ لِلَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا ماذا أَنْزَلَ رَبُّكُمْ قالُوا خَيْراً): in (وقيل للذين), (قيل) is a past verb, passive. There is disagreement about its [implied] subject; the nearest of the views is that they are the delegations of the Arabs whom the tribes used to send to Mecca. (للذين) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (قيل); the clause (اتقوا) is the ṣila (relative clause); (ماذا) has been discussed many times before; (أنزل ربكم) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (خيرا) is the object of an omitted verb, i.e. «أنزل خيرا» ("He sent down good"). Al-Zamakhsharī's wording: "If you say: why was the first put in the nominative and this one in the accusative? I say: to distinguish between the answer of the one who affirms and the answer of the one who denies. That is, when these were asked they did not hesitate, and they fitted the answer to the question, clear and plain, as an object of the sending down, so they said «خيرا», i.e. He sent down good; whereas those others turned the answer away from the question and said: it is tales of the ancients, which is not a matter of sending down at all." (لِلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا فِي هذِهِ الدُّنْيا حَسَنَةٌ وَلَدارُ الْآخِرَةِ خَيْرٌ وَلَنِعْمَ دارُ الْمُتَّقِينَ): (للذين) is a fronted khabar (predicate); the clause (أحسنوا) is the ṣila; (في هذه) is attached to (أحسنوا); (الدنيا) is a badal (substitute); (حسنة) is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive, and it may also be explicative of His word «خيرا». In (ولدار الآخرة), the lām is for commencement (lām al-ibtidāʾ); (دار الآخرة) is a mubtadaʾ and (خير) a khabar. In (ولنعم دار المتقين), the lām is also for commencement; (نعم) is a past verb for expressing praise; (دار المتقين) is the fāʿil; and the one specified for praise (al-makhṣūṣ bil-madḥ) is omitted, i.e. «هي» ("it"). (جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ يَدْخُلُونَها): (جنات) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. It may also be the one specified for praise, in which case it is parsed as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause (نعم دار المتقين), or as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; the first is preferable and less strained. The clause (يدخلونها) is circumstantial.
(تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ لَهُمْ فِيها ما يَشاؤُنَ): the clause «تجري من تحتهم الأنهار» [Translator's note: so in the source; the Qur'anic text here is «من تحتها»] is also a ḥāl (circumstantial); (لهم) is a fronted khabar; (فيها) is a ḥāl; (ما) is a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause (يشاءون) is the ṣila; and the clause (لهم فيها …) is a third ḥāl. (كَذلِكَ يَجْزِي اللَّهُ الْمُتَّقِينَ): the kāf is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), and it may also be parsed as a ḥāl; this has been established many times before. (يجزي الله المتقين) is a verb, an agent and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (الَّذِينَ تَتَوَفَّاهُمُ الْمَلائِكَةُ طَيِّبِينَ): (الذين) is an adjective of (المتقين) or a badal for it; the clause (تتوفاهم) is the ṣila; the hāʾ is the direct object and (الملائكة) the agent; (طيبين) is a ḥāl from the object in (تتوفاهم), i.e. pure of blemishes. (يَقُولُونَ سَلامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ ادْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ بِما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ): the clause (يقولون) is a ḥāl from (الملائكة), either concurrent (muqārina) or anticipated (muqaddara); their definitions will come in the Benefits section. (سلام) is a mubtadaʾ and (عليكم) a khabar; (ادخلوا الجنة) is an imperative verb, its agent and a direct object; (بما) is attached to (ادخلوا); the clause (كنتم) is the ṣila; the clause (تعملون) is the khabar of (كنتم). (ما) may also be maṣdarī, with the same i'rab.
(هَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَّا أَنْ تَأْتِيَهُمُ الْمَلائِكَةُ أَوْ يَأْتِيَ أَمْرُ رَبِّكَ): (هل) is an interrogative particle whose meaning is negation; (ينظرون) is an imperfect verb and its agent; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (أن) together with what falls within its scope is an interpreted maṣdar, the object of (ينظرون); (أو) is a conjunction; (يأتي أمر ربك) is conjoined to (تأتيهم الملائكة), i.e. [the command is] the punishment. (كَذلِكَ فَعَلَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ): the i'rab of (كذلك) was given recently, so refresh your memory of it; (فعل الذين) is a verb and its agent; (من قبلهم) is the ṣila of the relative. (وَما ظَلَمَهُمُ اللَّهُ وَلكِنْ كانُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is negative; (ظلمهم الله) is a verb, a direct object and an agent; the wāw is circumstantial or parenthetical; (لكن) is lightened and inoperative; kāna and its noun; the clause (يظلمون) is its khabar; (أنفسهم) is a fronted object of His word (يظلمون). (فَأَصابَهُمْ سَيِّئاتُ ما عَمِلُوا): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (أصابهم) is a verb and a fronted direct object; (سيئات) is the agent; (ما) is relative or maṣdarī, and in either case it is the muḍāf ilayhi of (سيئات). (وَحاقَ بِهِمْ ما كانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِؤُنَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (بهم) is attached to (حاق); (ما) is the agent; the clause (كانوا) is the ṣila; (به) is attached to (يستهزئون); the clause (يستهزئون) is the khabar of (كانوا).

* Benefits:
The ḥāl in relation to time:
The ḥāl in relation to time is of three kinds: 1- concurrent (muqārina), which is the most common, as in «هذا بعلي شيخا» ("this is my husband, an old man").
2- anticipated (muqaddara), which is future, as in «ادخلوها خالدين» ("enter it, to abide forever").
3- narrated (maḥkiyya), which is past, as in «جاء زيد أمس راكبا» ("Zayd came yesterday riding").
In the verse with which we are concerned, namely «يقولون سلام عليكم», it may be concurrent if the saying is uttered by them in this world, and anticipated if the saying is uttered by them in the Hereafter.

dervis-irab:35-36.t:
* I'rab:
(وَقالَ الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا لَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ ما عَبَدْنا مِنْ دُونِهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ نَحْنُ وَلا آباؤُنا): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, [brought] to establish their sophistry — their saying is a word of truth by which falsehood is intended — and their arguing against Allah the Exalted by His will, in which they have no argument, given the choice of the two paths and the taking of one of the two ways that was created for it [i.e. for human will].
(وقال الذين) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause (أشركوا) is the ṣila (relative clause); (لو) is conditional, of impossibility (imtināʿiyya); (شاء الله) is a verb and its agent, and the object is omitted, i.e. had He willed other than our way and what issues from us. Further discussion of the omission of the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) will come in the Rhetoric section. (ما) is negative; (عبدنا) is a verb and its agent; (من دونه) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); (من) is redundant (zāʾida); (شيء) is genitive in form and the object of (عبدنا) in position; (نحن) is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the agent of (عبدنا). The meaning is: we would not have worshipped anything other than Him. In (ولا), the wāw is a conjunction and (لا) is negative; (آباؤنا) is conjoined to (نحن). (وَلا حَرَّمْنا مِنْ دُونِهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ): the wāw is a conjunction; (حرمنا) is a verb and its agent; (من دونه) is a ḥāl from (شيء); (من) is a redundant preposition; (شيء) is genitive in form, a direct object accusative in position.
(كَذلِكَ فَعَلَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ): (كذلك) is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun) that is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); (فعل الذين) is a verb and its agent; (من قبلهم) is the ṣila. (فَهَلْ عَلَى الرُّسُلِ إِلَّا الْبَلاغُ الْمُبِينُ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (هل) is an interrogative particle meaning negation; (على الرسل) is a fronted khabar (predicate); (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (البلاغ) is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject) and (المبين) its adjective. (وَلَقَدْ بَعَثْنا فِي كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ رَسُولًا): the wāw is a conjunction; the lām prepares for the oath (mūṭṭiʾa lil-qasam); (قد) is a particle of verification; (بعثنا) is a verb and its agent; (في كل أمة) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (بعثنا); (رسولا) is a direct object.
(أَنِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ وَاجْتَنِبُوا الطَّاغُوتَ): (أن) may be maṣdarī, and together with what it governs it is accusative by removal of the preposition, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (بعثنا); it may also be explicative (mufassira), because sending contains the meaning of saying. (اعبدوا) is an imperative verb and its agent; the Name of Majesty is the direct object; (اجتنبوا الطاغوت) is an imperative verb, its agent and a direct object.
(فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ هَدَى اللَّهُ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ حَقَّتْ عَلَيْهِ الضَّلالَةُ): the fāʾ is for consequence (tafrīʿiyya) and resumptive; (منهم) is a fronted khabar; (من) is a postponed mubtadaʾ, and it is an indefinite noun that is qualified; the clause (هدى الله) is an adjective of (من). (ومنهم من حقت عليه الضلالة) is conjoined to the preceding one and is like it in i'rab. (فَسِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَانْظُرُوا كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ الْمُكَذِّبِينَ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that implies an omitted condition), i.e. if you want guidance and indication of the ideal way, then travel; (في الأرض) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (سيروا); in (فانظروا), the fāʾ is a conjunction and (انظروا) an imperative verb and its agent; (كيف) is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as the fronted khabar of (كان); (عاقبة المكذبين) is its postponed noun.

* Rhetoric:
Concision by omission (ījāz al-ḥadhf):
Omission for the sake of concision: the object of (شاء) has been omitted in His words «لو شاء الله ما عبدنا من دونه», i.e. had He willed our guidance. The omission of the direct object has subtleties too many to be mentioned. That is because people's purposes differ in mentioning transitive verbs. Sometimes they mention them intending only to affirm, for the agents, the meanings from which they are derived, without touching on mention of the objects; in that case the transitive verb is like the intransitive. An example of that is people's saying: "So-and-so loosens and binds, commands and forbids, harms and benefits." The second category is that the verb has an intended object, but it is omitted from the wording because of an indication that points to it. That may be obvious, with no artistry in it, as in their saying «أصغيت إليه» ("I listened to him"), i.e. with my ear. The hidden kind is that into which artistry enters. Among the hidden kind is that you mention the verb having in mind a specific object for it, but you forget it and hide it from yourself and give the impression that you mention the verb only to affirm its meaning itself without making it pass to an object, as in the words of al-Buḥturī:
شجو حساده وغيظ عداه ... أن يرى مبصر ويسمع واع
(The grief of those who envy him and the rage of his enemies is that one who sees should see and one who listens should hear.)
The meaning is: that one who sees should see his merits and one who listens should hear reports of him. Also among the hidden kind is that you have a known, intended object, it being known that the verb you mentioned has no object other than it, by the evidence of the situation or of the preceding speech, yet you discard it and feign forgetting it so that attention may be fully devoted to affirming the act for the agent, being devoted to it alone and wholly directed to it. Ṭufayl al-Ghanawī said of Banū Jaʿfar ibn Kilāb:
جزى الله عنا جعفرا حين أزلقت ... بنا نعلنا في الواطئين فزلت
أبو أن يملونا ولو أن أمّنا ... تلاقي الذي يلقون منا لملّت
هم خلطونا بالنفوس وألجئوا ... إلى حجرات أدفأت وأظلت
(May Allah reward Jaʿfar on our behalf when our sandals slipped with us among those treading, and we fell; they refused to grow weary of us, though had our mother met what they met from us she would have grown weary; they mingled us with their own selves and gave shelter in chambers that warmed and shaded.)
He omitted the object in four places: «لملت», «ألجئوا», «أدفأت» and «أظلت», because the original is «لملتنا» ("she would have grown weary of us"), «ألجئونا إلى حجرات أدفأتنا وأظلتنا» ("they sheltered us in chambers that warmed us and shaded us"). The poet's words «ولو أن أمنا تلاقي الذي لاقوه منا لملت» imply that what they met from us had reached such intensity as to make any mother weary and fed up, and that the hardship had reached such a degree as would make a mother weary of her son and annoyed with him, despite the patience in hardship for the good of their children that is in the nature of mothers. That is because, even though he said «أمنا» ("our mother"), the meaning is that this is the judgement of every mother with her children; had he said «لملتنا» it would not be fitting, because the meaning of generality is intended, i.e. such that every mother would grow weary of every son. Among this is the omission of the object after the verb of willing, as in the poet's words:
لو شئت لم تفسد سماحة حاتم ... كرما ولم تهدم مآثر خالد
(Had you willed, you would not have spoiled Ḥātim's magnanimity in generosity, nor demolished the glorious deeds of Khālid.)
The original is: "Had you willed to spoil Ḥātim's magnanimity, you would not have spoiled it"; then that was omitted from the first [part], dispensing with it because of the indication of it in the second. Moreover, it has the beauty and rarity that you see, because what is required by the rule of eloquence is that the omitted element not be uttered; for it is not hidden that, were you to revert to the original, you would arrive at insipid speech and something the ear spits out and the soul loathes.
ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī explains the beauty of omitting the object after the verb of willing by [saying] that in clarification after vagueness, and after stirring the soul to know it, there is a subtlety and nobility that does not exist when nothing stirring precedes. When you say «لو شئت» ("had you willed"), the listener knows that you have tied this willing, in meaning, to something, so he settles in his mind that there is something here that the willing requires; then when you say «لم تفسد سماحة حاتم», he knows that thing.

dervis-irab:37-42.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنْ تَحْرِصْ عَلى هُداهُمْ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَهْدِي مَنْ يُضِلُّ): (إن) is conditional; (تحرص) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (على هداهم) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تحرص), i.e. you desire it. In (فإن), the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); inna and its noun; the clause (لا يهدي) is its khabar (predicate); (من) is a relative noun, the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (يضل) is the ṣila (relative clause). It is also said that the apodosis is omitted and that the clause (فإن الله لا يهدي) gives the reason for the apodosis, the implied form being: neither you nor anyone else is able to guide them. (وَما لَهُمْ مِنْ ناصِرِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is the negative mā of the Ḥijāzī usage; (لهم) is the fronted khabar of (ما); (من) is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (ناصرين) is the noun of (ما) in position, or a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), and genitive in form. (وَأَقْسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمانِهِمْ): (وأقسموا) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (بالله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أقسموا); (جهد أيمانهم) is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) [i.e. as a mafʿūl muṭlaq]; it is also said that it is a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "striving". The clause is conjoined to (وقال الذين أشركوا), or it is resumptive and informative. (لا يَبْعَثُ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَمُوتُ بَلى وَعْداً عَلَيْهِ حَقًّا): (لا) is negative; (يبعث الله من يموت) is a verb, an agent and an object, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath. The swearing is called قسم because it takes place when people are divided (inqisām) into those who believe and those who deny. (بلى) is a particle of answer, i.e. "yes, He will resurrect them", because it affirms what comes after a negation. (وعدا عليه حقا) are two maṣdars emphasising what (بلى) indicates. It is also said that (حقا) is an adjective of (وعدا), and likewise (عليه); and (عليه) is attached to (حقا). (وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لا يَعْلَمُونَ): the clause is circumstantial; lākinna and its noun; the clause (لا يعلمون) is its khabar. (لِيُبَيِّنَ لَهُمُ الَّذِي يَخْتَلِفُونَ فِيهِ): the lām is for causation; (يبين) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied «أن» after the lām of causation, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to what (بلى) indicates, i.e. He will resurrect them in order to make clear. (لهم) is attached to (يبين); (الذي) is a mafʿūl bihi; the clause (يختلفون) is the ṣila; (فيه) is attached to (يختلفون). (وَلِيَعْلَمَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَنَّهُمْ كانُوا كاذِبِينَ): (وليعلم) is conjoined to (ليبين); (الذين) is the agent; the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila; anna together with what falls within its scope stands in place of the two objects of (يعلم); anna and its noun; the clause (كانوا) is its khabar; (كاذبين) is the khabar of (كانوا). (إِنَّما قَوْلُنا لِشَيْءٍ إِذا أَرَدْناهُ أَنْ نَقُولَ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ): (إنما) is a restraining [mā] and a restrained [inna] (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (قولنا) is a mubtadaʾ; (لشيء) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (قولنا); (إذا) is an adverb attached to (قولنا); the clause (أردناه) is annexed to the adverb; (أن) and what it governs is an interpreted maṣdar, the khabar of (قولنا); (له) is attached to (نقول); (كن) is an imperative verb from the complete kāna (kāna al-tāmma), and the clause (كن) is the content of the saying. (فيكون): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and (يكون) is conjoined to something implied, which the fāʾ discloses and over which the speech extends, i.e. "so We say that to it, and it is". Or else it is the apodosis of an omitted condition, so it is a fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that implies an omitted condition), i.e. "so when We say that, it comes to be". Further discussion of this saying and what is said, the command and the commanded, will come in the Rhetoric section. The clause is resumptive, brought to establish the power to resurrect, or the manner of bringing into being absolutely, both originating and restoring. (وَالَّذِينَ هاجَرُوا فِي اللَّهِ مِنْ بَعْدِ ما ظُلِمُوا): (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (هاجروا) is the ṣila, i.e. they moved from Mecca to Medina — and among them were some who had emigrated to Abyssinia, so they combined the two emigrations; (في الله) is attached to (هاجروا), and (في) is for causation, i.e. for the establishment of Allah's religion; (من بعد) is a ḥāl; (ما) is maṣdarī, interpreted together with what it governs as a maṣdar that is the muḍāf ilayhi of (بعد), i.e. after their being wronged by harm from the people of Mecca. (لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ فِي الدُّنْيا حَسَنَةً): the lām prepares for the oath (mūṭṭiʾa lil-qasam); the clause (نبوئنهم) is the khabar of (الذين); (في الدنيا) is a ḥāl; (حسنة) is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. «تبوئة حسنة» ("a good settling"), so it stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). You may also parse it as the second object of (نبوئنهم), because it includes the meaning of «نعطينهم» ("We will surely give them"), in which case it is an adjective of something omitted, i.e. «دارا حسنة» ("a good abode"). (وَلَأَجْرُ الْآخِرَةِ أَكْبَرُ لَوْ كانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ): the wāw is circumstantial; the lām is for commencement (lām al-ibtidāʾ); (أجر الآخرة) is a mubtadaʾ and (أكبر) a khabar; (لو) is conditional; kāna, its noun and its khabar. (الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا وَعَلى رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ): (الذين) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. «هم الذين صبروا» ("they are those who were patient"), so its position is nominative; or it is accusative by way of praise, i.e. «أعني الذين صبروا» ("I mean those who were patient"), so its position is accusative. The clause (صبروا) is the ṣila; (على ربهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يتوكلون); (يتوكلون) is an imperfect verb and its agent.

* Rhetoric:
1- إنما:
«إنما قولنا لشيء إذا أردناه أن نقول له كن فيكون». Imam ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī devoted an enjoyable chapter on «إنما» in his book Dalāʾil al-Iʿjāz, the gist of which we transmit. He paused to draw out the meanings of «إنما», and held that stopping, with regard to it, at the grammarians' statement that the joining of «ما» to «إنّ» has no benefit beyond cancelling its operation is a clear error. The basic use of «إنما» is that it comes for information the addressee is not ignorant of and does not deny the truth of, or for what is put in that position. Of the first is the saying of the Exalted «انما يستجيب الذين يسمعون» ("only those who hear respond"), for every rational person knows that there can be no response except from one who understands what is said to him and what he is called to. An example of what is put in that position is the words of Ibn al-Ruqayyāt:
انما مصعب شهاب من الله تجلّت عن وجهه الظلماء
(Muṣʿab is but a blazing flame from Allah, from whose face darkness is dispelled.)
In the speech that follows it, «إنما» conveys affirming the action for one thing and negating it of others, and it makes the matter evident. When you say «إنما جاءني زيد» ("only Zayd came to me"), it is understood from it that you meant [to deny] that the one who came was someone else; so the meaning of the speech with it resembles the meaning of your saying «جاءني زيد لا عمرو» ("Zayd came to me, not ʿAmr"), except that it has an advantage, namely that with it you understand the affirmation of the action for one thing and its negation of another all at once, and it makes it evident that the one who came was Zayd.
2- The representational metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya): in His words «كن فيكون». It is a metaphor for coming into being, representing the speed of bringing into existence when the will is attached [to something]. There is in reality no command there, no kāf and no nūn. Otherwise, had there been a command there, it would be in order to say: if the address is to the thing in its state of non-existence, that is not intelligible, because addressing the non-existent is not intelligible; and if it is after its existence, then it is bringing about what has already come about. Rather, its purpose is to depict the speed of origination by something whose duration does not exceed the uttering of the word «كن» — and how easy that is!
3- Reporting about the past with the future is more eloquent than reporting with the past verb. That is in the words of the Exalted «وعلى ربهم يتوكلون»: apparently the meaning is past, and the expression with the imperfect is to evoke that wonderful image, until it is as if the listener witnesses it. Its discussion has preceded.

dervis-irab:43-47.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الزُّبُرِ): books; plural of زبور in the sense of مزبور ("written").
(تَخَوُّفٍ): gradual diminishing; it is from your saying تخوّفته and تخوّنته when you diminished it bit by bit. Zuhayr ibn Abī Sulmā said — and it is said to be by Abū Kabīr al-Hudhalī —:
تخوف الرحل منها تامكا قردا ... كما تخوف عود النبعة السبفن
(The saddle wore down her high, compact hump, as the rasp wears down the wood of the nabʿ tree.)
[Translator's note: «السبفن» is so in the source; the word is «السَّفَن», "the rasp".]
The meaning is: He seizes them by diminishing them little by little in their persons and their wealth until they perish. It is reported of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb that he asked about the meaning of التخوف in the words of the Exalted «أو يأخذهم على تخوف», and a man of Hudhayl stood up and said: "This is our dialect: التخوف is gradual diminishing." ʿUmar said: "Do the Arabs know that in their poetry?" He said: "Yes," and recited the aforementioned verse. ʿUmar said: "Hold to your dīwān and you will not go astray." They said: "What is our dīwān?" He said: "The poetry of the Jāhiliyya, for in it is the explanation of your Book."

The Companions and the rare words (al-gharīb) in the Qur'an:
The school of the Messenger ﷺ began to follow his footsteps in exegesis, to preserve and transmit what was reported from him, and at times to add to it by explaining a rare word. Despite this, we do not lack some rare words in the verses of the Book at which they «توفقوا» [Translator's note: so in the source, for «توقفوا», "paused / refrained"]. Among that is what Abū ʿUbayda [Translator's note: so in the source; the Faḍāʾil is by Abū ʿUbayd] narrated in al-Faḍāʾil from Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, that Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq was asked about the words of the Exalted «وفاكهة وأبّا», and he said: "What sky would shade me and what earth would carry me if I said about the Book of Allah what I do not know?" And it is reported from Anas that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb recited on the pulpit «وفاكهة وأبّا» and said: "This fruit we know; so what is al-abb?" Then he turned back to himself and said: "This is indeed affectation, O ʿUmar." In the early period of Islam the Companions were divided into two groups. [First,] those who were wary of speaking about the Qur'an; among them were Abū Bakr, ʿUmar and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, and ʿAbd Allāh [ibn ʿUmar] used to fault ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās for interpreting the Qur'an by poetry. The second group were those who were not wary and interpreted the Qur'an according to what they had understood from the Messenger, or according to their own understanding by comparison with Arabic poetry and the speech of the Arabs; among them were ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās and those who took from them. Ibn ʿAbbās stood at the head of the commentators by opinion (al-raʾy) who took the poetry of the Arabs as a means to uncover the meanings of the Qur'an. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib used to praise ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās and say: "It is as if he looks at the unseen through a thin veil." Among them too were Ibn Masʿūd, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb and others; and they were followed by al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, Mujāhid, ʿIkrima, Qatāda, al-Suddī and others. Aḥmad Amīn says in his enjoyable book Fajr al-Islām, in summary, that these commentators among the Companions and the Successors followed a method which may be summed up as being guided by the hadith of the Messenger of Allah, by the spirit of the Qur'an, and by Arabic poetry and pre-Islamic literature in general; then by the customs of the Arabs in their Jāhiliyya and early Islam, the events they faced, and the enmity, disputes, emigration and wars the Messenger of Allah encountered.

A glimpse of Ibn ʿAbbās and his school:
Ibn ʿAbbās made his way among all of these, leading a school of his own that came to dominate exegesis and stamped it with its character. Al-Suyūṭī in al-Itqān cited the hundred questions of Ibn al-Azraq on the Qur'an and Ibn ʿAbbās's answer to them with poetry, explaining the rare word of each verse with a verse of poetry. Ibn ʿAbbās says about interpreting the Qur'an by poetry: "If something of the Qur'an is obscure, look into poetry, for poetry is Arabic." And he says: "If you ask about something of the rare words of the Qur'an, seek it in poetry, for poetry is the register (dīwān) of the Arabs." Ibn ʿAbbās's command of the language and meanings of the Qur'an was wide, so much so that he said: "I know all of the Qur'an except four: غسلين, حنانا, الأواه and الرقيم."
With Ibn ʿAbbās's endeavours there began a new school of exegesis that uncovered the style and meanings of the Qur'an by comparing it with Arabic literature, its poetry and its prose. This school paved the way for the rise of a broad movement to collect language and poetry from the tent-encampments and deserts of the Arabs, in order to deal with the rare words in the Qur'an that became remote [to people] as the distance grew from the Ḥijāz and the heart of the Arabian Peninsula, in Iraq, Persia, Syria and the other Islamic garrison-cities. Scholars gathered up whatever the tongues of the Bedouin yielded of examples matching what occurs in the verses of the Qur'an, and this great movement was a cause of preserving Arabic from being lost.

* I'rab:
(وَما أَرْسَلْنا مِنْ قَبْلِكَ إِلَّا رِجالًا نُوحِي إِلَيْهِمْ): the wāw is a conjunction, so that the speech is coherent; it brings up another aspect of their obstinacy and their insistence on saying: Allah is too great for His messenger to be a human being, so why did He not send us an angel? You may also make it resumptive and self-standing, the clause being brought for what we have mentioned. (ما) is negative; (أرسلنا) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (من قبلك) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (رجالا) is the object of (أرسلنا); the clause (نوحي إليهم) is a naʿt (adjective). (فَسْئَلُوا أَهْلَ الذِّكْرِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ لا تَعْلَمُونَ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that implies an omitted condition), i.e. if you doubt what has been mentioned, then ask; (اسألوا) is an imperative verb and its agent; (أهل الذكر) is its object; (إن) is conditional; (كنتم) is a deficient past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the apodosis (jawāb) is omitted, indicated by (فاسألوا); kāna and its noun; the clause (لا تعلمون) is its khabar (predicate). (بِالْبَيِّناتِ وَالزُّبُرِ وَأَنْزَلْنا إِلَيْكَ الذِّكْرَ لِتُبَيِّنَ لِلنَّاسِ): (بالبينات) admits various attachments. Either they [the preposition and its noun] are attached to (أرسلنا), falling under the scope of the exception together with (رجالا), i.e. "We sent only men with the clear proofs" — al-Zamakhsharī illustrated this with the saying "I struck none but Zayd with the whip", since its origin is "I struck Zayd with the whip"; or they are attached to something omitted as an adjective of (رجالا), i.e. men invested with the clear proofs, accompanied by them; or to (أرسلنا) implied, as if it were asked "With what were they sent?" and answered "With the clear proofs"; or to (نوحي), i.e. We reveal to them with the clear proofs. There are other possibilities which we have passed over. (أنزلنا) is conjoined to (أرسلنا); (إليك) is attached to (أنزلنا); (الذكر) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); in (لتبين) the lām is for causation and (تبين) is accusative (manṣūb) by an implied «أن», and it is attached to (أنزلنا); (للناس) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (تبين).
(ما نُزِّلَ إِلَيْهِمْ وَلَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ): (ما) is the object of (تبين); the clause (نزل إليهم) is the ṣila (relative clause); (لعلهم) is laʿalla and its noun; the clause (يتفكرون) is its khabar. (أَفَأَمِنَ الَّذِينَ مَكَرُوا السَّيِّئاتِ أَنْ يَخْسِفَ اللَّهُ بِهِمُ الْأَرْضَ): the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval and rebuke; the fāʾ conjoins to something omitted — as has preceded — to which the arrangement points, i.e. We sent down to you the Reminder so that you may make its content clear to them, and they did not reflect on that; so it is as if it were said: "Did they not reflect, and so have those who schemed evil deeds felt secure?" (أمن الذين) is a verb and its agent; the clause (مكروا) is the ṣila; (السيئات) is an adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. «المكرات السيئات» ("the evil schemes"); it may also be a mafʿūl bihi of (أمن), i.e. they felt secure from the evil punishments; or accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. they schemed with evil deeds.
