In (أن يخسف), anna [sic; أن] together with what falls within its scope is a maṣdar (verbal noun), the object of (أمن) on the first view regarding (السيئات), and a badal (substitute) for (السيئات) on the second view. (الله) is the agent of (يخسف); (بهم) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يخسف); (الأرض) is a mafʿūl bihi. (أَوْ يَأْتِيَهُمُ الْعَذابُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لا يَشْعُرُونَ): conjoined to (أن يخسف); (من حيث) is a ḥāl; the clause (لا يشعرون) is annexed to the adverb.
(أَوْ يَأْخُذَهُمْ فِي تَقَلُّبِهِمْ فَما هُمْ بِمُعْجِزِينَ): also conjoined to (أن يخسف); (في تقلبهم) is a ḥāl from the object, i.e. while they are moving about in journeys, trade and the means of this world; the fāʾ is a conjunction; (ما) is the negative mā of the Ḥijāzī usage; (هم) is its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (معجزين) is genitive by the bāʾ in form and accusative in position as the khabar of (ما).
(أَوْ يَأْخُذَهُمْ عَلى تَخَوُّفٍ فَإِنَّ رَبَّكُمْ لَرَؤُفٌ رَحِيمٌ): a third conjunction to (أن يخسف); (على تخوف) is also a ḥāl, from the agent or the object, i.e. He seizes them diminishing them little by little, or while they are in fear; the fāʾ gives the reason for what preceded; inna and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (رؤوف) is the first khabar of (إنّ) and (رحيم) the second.

dervis-irab:48-52.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَتَفَيَّؤُا ظِلالُهُ): تفيّأ الظل: the shade shifted and moved from one side to another. The maṣdar (verbal noun) is التفيّؤ, from فاء يفيء when it returned. فاء is intransitive; when it is meant to be made transitive, it is made transitive by the hamza, as in the words of the Exalted «ما أفاء الله على رسوله», or by doubling, as in «فيّأ الله الظل فتفيّأ» ("Allah made the shade shift, so it shifted"); تفيّأ is the reflexive (muṭāwiʿ) of فيّأ, so it is intransitive. There is disagreement about الفيء. It is said to be shade in general, whether before or after the sun's decline, and this fits the verse. It is said that what is before the decline is shade (ẓill) only, and what is after it is both shade and fayʾ, so ẓill is more general. And it is said that rather ẓill is specific to what is before the decline and fayʾ to what is after it, so fayʾ is only in the afternoon/evening, being what the sun has turned away from, while ẓill is what is in the morning, being what the sun has not reached. In al-Qāmūs, al-Tāj and others: الظل is الفيء; the plural is ظلال, أظلال and ظلول; ظل الليل is its blackness; one says "he came to us in the shade of the night". Dhū al-Rumma said:
قد أسعف النازح المجهول مسعفه ... في ظل أخضر يدعو هامة البوم
(The one who aids the distant, unknown traveller has aided him in the shade of a dark [night] in which the owl's head calls out.)
This is a metaphor, because shade in reality is only the light of the sun's rays without the rays [themselves]; where there is no light it is darkness, not shade. The people of [natural] science said: shade in general is the second light. The meaning of this is that when the luminary rises above the horizon, the air is lit by the presence of rays in it, and this is the first light; when something screens this light, what lies behind that screen is a second light relative to the first light, because it is derived from it; and this second light is the shade. The shadow-play (khayāl al-ẓill) inspired the poets with wonderful curiosities; among them is the saying of al-Munāwī about a dancing girl:
إذا ما تغنت قلت: سكرى صبابة ... وإن رقصت قلنا احتكام مدام
أرتنا خيال الظل والستر دونها ... فأبدت خيال الشمس وهو غمام
(When she sang, I said: drunk with passion; and when she danced, we said: the wine has taken hold. She showed us the shadow-play with the curtain before her, and revealed the image of the sun, while it was [behind] a cloud.)
Ibn Qutayba mentioned in his book Adab al-Kātib the following text: "People hold that ẓill and fayʾ are one, but it is not so, because ẓill exists from the beginning of the day to its end, and the meaning of ẓill is covering; while fayʾ is only after the sun's decline, and what is before the decline is not called fayʾ. It was only called fayʾ because it is shade that has returned (fāʾa) from one side to another, i.e. it returned from the western side to the eastern side; and الفيء is returning. Allah the Exalted said: «حتى تفيء إلى أمر الله», i.e. until it returns."
(الشَّمائِلِ): plural of شمال (left), i.e. on their two sides at the beginning and end of the day. The scholars said: when the sun rises in the east and you are facing the qibla, your shadow is on your right; when the sun rises high and stands in the middle of the sky, your shadow is behind you; and when the sun inclines towards setting, your shadow is on your left.
(داخِرُونَ): submissive, humbled.

* I'rab:
(أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا إِلى ما خَلَقَ اللَّهُ مِنْ شَيْءٍ يَتَفَيَّؤُا ظِلالُهُ عَنِ الْيَمِينِ وَالشَّمائِلِ سُجَّداً لِلَّهِ وَهُمْ داخِرُونَ): the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval and rebuke; the wāw conjoins to something omitted and implied, which the context requires, i.e. "did they not look, and did they not see, turning towards what Allah created?" (إلى ما) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يروا). Since this seeing is in the sense of looking, it is connected with (إلى), because what is meant by it is taking heed, and that taking heed can only come about through the seeing itself, accompanied by looking at the thing to ponder it, to perceive [its truth] and to contemplate «بمغابه» [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably «بمغابّه», "its outcomes"] and its consequences. The clause (خلق الله) is the ṣila (relative clause); (من شيء) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (ما خلق الله), and it is valid for it to be «مبنية» [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably «مبيِّنة», "explicative"] for its description, even though the word «شيء» is vague. The clause (يتفيأ ظلاله) is a naʿt (adjective) of (شيء); (ظلاله) is the fāʿil (agent) of (يتفيأ); (عن اليمين) is a ḥāl, and (عن الشمائل) is conjoined. It is also valid for «عن» to be a noun meaning "side", in which case it is accusative as an adverb; and it is valid for it to be attached to «تتفيأ», its meaning being "passing beyond", i.e. the shades pass from the right to the left. A question remains here: why is اليمين singular and الشمال plural? The scholars gave many answers, the closest to logic being that the beginning takes place from the right, and it is one thing, so the right is made singular; then [the shade] diminishes little by little and state after state, so it has the meaning of a plural, and the word الشمائل fits each state, being multiplied as the states multiply. Al-Farrāʾ has an interesting view; he said: it is as though, when He made it singular, He had in mind one of the things that have shade, and when He made it plural, He had in mind all of them, because His words «ما خلق الله من شيء» are singular in wording and plural in meaning; so He expressed one of them with the singular wording, as in the words of the Exalted «وجعل الظلمات والنور». Ibn al-Ṣāʾigh said: "He made [one] singular and [the other] plural with a view to the two extremes, because the morning shade dwindles until only a little of it remains, so it is as if it were in one direction, while in the evening it is the reverse, because it takes over all directions; so the two extremes are taken into account in the verse. This is from the side of meaning. From the side of wording there is correspondence in it, because «سجّدا» is plural, so the plural «الشمائل» corresponds to it because of its being adjacent to it. Thus in the verse there is correspondence of wording to meaning and regard for both together, and that is the summit of inimitability." It is also said that He made اليمين singular in regard to the wording of «ما» and the second plural in regard to its meaning. Al-Suhaylī devoted a fine treatise to this verse.
(سجّدا) is a ḥāl from (ظلاله); the wāw is circumstantial; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (داخرون) a khabar (predicate); the clause is a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in (سجدا), so it is an overlapping (mutadākhila) ḥāl. (وَلِلَّهِ يَسْجُدُ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ مِنْ دابَّةٍ وَالْمَلائِكَةُ): (لله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يسجد); (ما) is the agent of (يسجد); (في السموات) is the ṣila; (وما في الأرض) is conjoined to (ما في السموات); (من دابة) is in the position of accusative as an explicative ḥāl (al-ḥāl al-mubayyina) [Translator's note: the source again has «المبنية»]; (الملائكة) is conjoined to (ما). He singled them out for mention after the general [statement] to extol their excellence.
(وَهُمْ لا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (لا يستكبرون) a khabar. (يَخافُونَ رَبَّهُمْ مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ وَيَفْعَلُونَ ما يُؤْمَرُونَ): the clause (يخافون) is accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun of (يستكبرون), or a badal (substitute) for the clause (لا يستكبرون), because whoever fears Allah is not too proud to worship Him. (يخافون ربهم) is an imperfect verb, an agent and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (من فوقهم) is a ḥāl from (ربهم), i.e. they fear their Lord, Who is high above them in rank, in the manner of His words «وهو القاهر فوق عباده». (يفعلون) is conjoined to (يخافون); (ما) is a mafʿūl bihi; the clause (يؤمرون) is the ṣila. (وَقالَ اللَّهُ لا تَتَّخِذُوا إِلهَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ): the wāw is resumptive; (قال الله) is a verb and its agent; (لا) is prohibitive; (تتخذوا) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لا); the wāw is the agent; (إلهين) is a mafʿūl bihi; (اثنين) is an adjective of (إلهين). Among the curious paradoxes is that almost all the commentators parse it as a tawkīd (emphasis) of (إلهين), though «اثنين» is not one of the words of semantic emphasis, nor does it belong to verbal emphasis. It appears that their parsing it thus rests on the meaning, because the meaning of the description is emphasis; you will see an interesting discussion of that in the Rhetoric section. Some were compelled to say that the word «اثنين» is an emphasis of the duality understood from «إلهين»; and it is said that there is fronting and postponement in the speech, the implied form being «لا تتخذوا اثنين إلهين» ("do not take two as gods"). It is only one God. (إِنَّما هُوَ إِلهٌ واحِدٌ فَإِيَّايَ فَارْهَبُونِ): (إنما) is a restraining [mā] and a restrained [inna] (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (هو) is a mubtadaʾ; (إله) is a khabar; (واحد) is an adjective, also for emphasis. (فإياي): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that implies an omitted condition); (إياي) is the mafʿūl bihi of an implied verb explained by what follows, i.e. by His word (ارهبون). (ارهبون) is an imperative verb; the wāw is the agent; the nūn is for protection (nūn al-wiqāya); and the yāʾ, omitted out of regard for the verse-endings, is its object.
(وَلَهُ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ): you may make the wāw a conjunction, with the clause conjoined to His words (إنما هو إله واحد), or you may make it resumptive, with the clause resumptive. (له) is a fronted khabar; (ما) is a postponed mubtadaʾ; (في السموات) is the ṣila; (الأرض) is conjoined to (ما في السموات) [sic]. (وَلَهُ الدِّينُ واصِباً): the wāw is a conjunction; (له) is a fronted khabar; (الدين) is a postponed mubtadaʾ; (واصبا) is a ḥāl from the pronoun latent in the preposition and its genitive noun, the implied form being "and the religion is established for Him, being wāṣib". There are two views on the meaning of الوصب: one is permanence, i.e. to Him belongs religion, established perpetually; the second is hardship and burden, i.e. to Him belongs religion, entailing burden and hardship. (أَفَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ تَتَّقُونَ): the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval; the fāʾ conjoins to something omitted, the implied form being: after what has been established of Allah's oneness, and after you have known that everything besides Him is in need of Him, how is it conceivable that you should fear other than Him and dread other than Him? (غير الله) is a fronted object of (تتقون); (تتقون) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn; the wāw is its agent.

* Rhetoric:
These verses, for all their concision, comprise devices of rhetoric that would fill volumes. We shall try to summarise them in the following statements: 1- Predominance (al-taghlīb):
In the words of the Exalted «ولله يسجد ما في السموات وما في الأرض …»: He used the relative word «ما» in His words «ما في السموات وما في الأرض» by way of predominance, because the non-rational outnumbers the rational, and the ruling goes with the majority. The relative «ما» in its original assignment is for the non-rational, just as «من» is originally assigned to the rational, but they may be interchanged. Among uses of «من» for the non-rational in poetry is the saying of al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Aḥnaf:
أسرب القطا هل من يعير جناحه ... لعلّي إلى من قد هويت أطير
(O flock of sandgrouse, is there one who will lend his wing, so that perhaps I may fly to the one I love?)
He applied «من» to the flock of sandgrouse, which is non-rational. And the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
ألا عم صباحا أيها الطلل البالي ... وهل يعمن من كان في العصر الخالي
(Good morning, O decayed ruin! But can one who belongs to bygone times fare well in the morning?)
He applied «من» to the ruin, which is non-rational.
Below is an important rule, which we summarise «فبما يلي» [Translator's note: so in the source, for «فيما يلي», "in what follows"]:
- «من» may be used for non-rational beings in three cases:
a- When the non-rational is treated as rational, as in the words of the Exalted «ومن أضل ممن يدعو من دون الله من لا يستجيب له إلى يوم القيامة», and the aforementioned saying of Imruʾ al-Qays, and likewise the aforementioned saying of al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Aḥnaf. The calling upon idols that do not answer the call in the noble verse, and the addressing of the ruin and the sandgrouse in the two verses, justified treating them as rational, since only rational beings are addressed.
b- When the non-rational is merged with the rational in one ruling, as in the words of the Exalted «أفمن يخلق كمن لا يخلق» and His words «ألم تر أن الله يسجد له من في السموات ومن في الأرض».
c- When the non-rational is coupled with the rational in a generality that is then detailed, as in the words of the Exalted «والله خلق كل دابة من ماء فمنهم من يمشي على بطنه ومنهم من يمشي على رجلين ومنهم من يمشي على أربع». «الدابة» covers the kinds of whatever creeps on the face of the earth, and He detailed it into three types.
- And «ما» may be used for the rational when the rational is coupled with the non-rational in one ruling, as in the verse cited above.

2- Precaution (al-iḥtirās):
That is in the words of the Exalted «وقال الله لا تتخذوا إلهين اثنين إنما هو إله واحد». It is well known that number and the thing counted are combined only for what is beyond one and two. They say «عندي رجال ثلاثة ونساء ثلاث» ("I have three men and three women"), because the counted noun is devoid of indicating the specific number, so if you did not accompany it with its descriptor, the intended number would not be understood. As for «رجل», «امرأة», «رجلان» and «امرأتان», they are counted nouns in which there is an indication of number, so there is no need to say «رجل واحد», «امرأة واحدة», «رجلان اثنان» and «امرأتان اثنتان». In the verse, however, the noun carrying the meaning of singular and dual — «إله» and «إلهان» — indicates two things: the genus and the specific number. So when it is meant to indicate that what the discourse is directed at is the number, it must be accompanied by what emphasises it. Do you not see that if you said «إله» and did not emphasise it with «واحد», it would not be good, and it would seem to you that you were affirming divinity, not oneness? So precaution was necessary. This is among the marvels of eloquence before which necks are cut short [i.e. which none can match].

3- Shift of address (al-iltifāt):
From the third person to the first: He said «وقال الله لا تتخذوا إلهين اثنين …», then turned to the speaker's presence, namely His words «وإياي فارهبون» [Translator's note: so in the source; the Qur'anic wording is «فَإِيَّايَ فَارْهَبُونِ»], because that is more effective in inspiring dread than saying, following the context, «فإياه فارهبون» ("so dread Him").

dervis-irab:94-97.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلا تَتَّخِذُوا أَيْمانَكُمْ دَخَلًا بَيْنَكُمْ) He repeated it for emphasis, stating the prohibition explicitly, to stress how ugly the act is. (فَتَزِلَّ قَدَمٌ بَعْدَ ثُبُوتِها) The فاء is the fāʾ of causation (sababiyya) preceded by a prohibition; تزل is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن; قدم is the fāʿil (agent); بعد is an adverbial attached to تزل; and ثبوتها is the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (وَتَذُوقُوا السُّوءَ بِما صَدَدْتُمْ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَلَكُمْ عَذابٌ عَظِيمٌ) وتذوقوا is conjoined to تزل; السوء is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the ب is a preposition, here of causation; ما is a maṣdar (verbal-noun) particle, which together with what follows is in the position of a genitive after the ب; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تذوقوا; عن سبيل الله is attached to صددتم; ولكم is a predicate placed first; عذاب is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); and عظيم is its adjective.
(وَلا تَشْتَرُوا بِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ ثَمَناً قَلِيلًا) The و is a conjunction; لا is a prohibitive particle; تشتروا is an imperfect verb jussive by لا; بعهد الله is attached to تشتروا, the ب entering upon the thing given up; ثمنا is the mafʿūl bihi; and قليلا is an adjective. (إِنَّما عِنْدَ اللَّهِ هُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ) inna and its noun; the adverbial is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما; هو is a mubtadaʾ and خير the khabar (predicate); and the sentence is the khabar of inna; ولكم is attached to it. إن is conditional, and كنتم is in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the ت is the noun of كان and the clause تعلمون is its predicate. The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then do not break (your covenant)". (ما عِنْدَكُمْ يَنْفَدُ وَما عِنْدَ اللَّهِ باقٍ) ما is a relative noun and mubtadaʾ; عندكم is an adverbial attached to the ṣila; and the clause ينفد is the khabar of ما. Likewise وما عند الله باق. (وَلَنَجْزِيَنَّ الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا أَجْرَهُمْ بِأَحْسَنِ ما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ) The lām is the one that prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam); نجزين is an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is emphasised with the doubled nūn; the fāʿil is a latent pronoun (mustatir), its implied form being "we"; الذين صبروا is its mafʿūl bihi; أجرهم is a second object of نجزين; and بأحسن, a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to نجزين. It is an adjective of an omitted noun, i.e. "with a reward better than…"; ما is a maṣdar particle; كان with its noun, and the clause يعملون is its predicate. You may also take ما as a relative noun, the implied meaning being "with a reward better than their deed which they used to do in this world", or we may make the reward commensurate with the best of their deeds. (مَنْ عَمِلَ صالِحاً مِنْ ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنْثى وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَلَنُحْيِيَنَّهُ حَياةً طَيِّبَةً) من is a conditional noun, jussive-governing, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ; عمل is a past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis; من ذكر is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of عمل; أو is a conjunction and أنثى is conjoined to ذكر; وهو مؤمن: the و is the circumstantial wāw (ḥāliyya), هو is a mubtadaʾ and مؤمن the khabar, and the clause is a ḥāl. In فلنحيينه the فاء is the connecting fāʾ (rābiṭa) and the lām prepares for the oath; نحيينه is an imperfect verb indeclinable on the fatḥa because of its contact with the heavy nūn of emphasis, and the هاء is the mafʿūl bihi; حياة is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and طيبة an adjective. The clause فلنحيينه is the apodosis; the protasis and its apodosis together are the khabar of من. You may also take من as a relative noun, the entering فاء being due to the scent of a condition in what is described, so that the clause فلنحيينه would be its khabar.
(وَلَنَجْزِيَنَّهُمْ أَجْرَهُمْ بِأَحْسَنِ ما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ) Its i'rab has already been given, and further explanation of these verses will come in the section on rhetoric.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying, Exalted is He, «مَنْ عَمِلَ صالِحاً مِنْ ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنْثى وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ» up to the end of the verse, there are various arts, the most prominent being tatmīm (completion), which has been discussed before. It occurs twice in this verse. The first is in His saying "of male or female": since من, whether conditional or relative, conveys generality, it had to be completed with this, for emphasis and to remove the notion of restriction, in keeping with the ancient beliefs of the Arabs, who preferred the male over the female and favoured him with everything good. The second is in His saying "while he is a believer". Opinions differ about this completion and about what is meant by the good life that one in this position receives. The best of them that we choose is the saying of al-Zamakhsharī, which we quote verbatim for its benefit. He said, and excelled:
"That is because the believer who does righteous deeds, whether wealthy or poor, lives a good life. If he is wealthy, there is nothing to say; and if he is poor, he has with him what makes his life pleasant, namely contentment and satisfaction with Allah's apportioning. As for the wicked man, his case is the reverse. If he is poor, there is no difficulty about his case, in the words of Abū Dulāma:
ما أحسن الدين والدنيا إذا اجتمعا ... وأقبح الكفر والإفلاس في الرجل
(How fine are religion and the world when they come together, and how ugly are unbelief and bankruptcy in a man.)
And if he is wealthy, greed does not let him enjoy his life." What supports this is what we see of mankind's absorption in devising means of destruction and ruin in order to dominate, exploit and rule the world, and how far off that is! 2- In His saying «فتزل قدم بعد ثبوتها» there is an istiʿāra tamthīliyya (extended metaphor) for one whose condition is upright falling into a great evil and dropping into it, because when a foot slips it carries a person from a state of good to a state of evil. One who errs in something is told "his foot slipped with him", and from this is the saying of Zuhayr:
تداركتما عبسا وقد ثل عرشها ... وذبيان قد زلت بأقدامها النعل
(You two rescued ʿAbs when its throne had been toppled, and Dhubyān, whose sandals had slipped from under their feet.)
3- In His saying «فتزل قدم بعد ثبوتها إلخ» the foot is singular and indefinite. The secret of this is to regard it as grave that even a single foot should slip from the path of truth after its ground has been levelled for it and it had stood firm upon it, so how much more so many feet; and it also diminishes the number of those who take heed of what calls for sound judgement and uprightness. Of the same kind as this indefiniteness's conveying paucity is its conveying it in His saying, Exalted is He: «وتعيها اذن واعية» and in His saying «اتقوا الله ولتنظر نفس ما قدمت لغد»; so He made اذن and نفس indefinite to show how few of the people take heed of what calls for soundness.

dervis-irab:65-69.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْأَنْعامِ): Its explanation was given earlier in Sūrat al-Anʿām. Sībawayh mentioned al-anʿām in the chapter on nouns that are not declined fully (diptotes) among the nouns that come on the pattern of afʿāl, and for that reason the pronoun referring back to it is singular. The pronoun refers back to it in the feminine in Sūrat al-Muʾminūn, because its meaning is plural. It may be said of al-anʿām that it has two aspects: either it is a broken plural of naʿam, like ajbāl from jabal, or it is a singular noun carrying the sense of a plural. When it is treated as masculine, it is as naʿam is treated as masculine in the poet's line:
في كل عام نعم تحوونه ... يلقحه قوم وتنتجونه
(Every year there are cattle that you gather in; one people makes them conceive and you bring forth their young.)
And when it is treated as feminine there are two aspects: that it is a broken plural of naʿam, and that it has the meaning of a plural. Sībawayh has an interesting discussion, as we said, for he counted the singular words built on the pattern of afʿāl, such as akhlāq and amshāj, which are treated now as masculine in regard to their form and now as feminine in regard to their meaning. It was also said that it is a plural of naʿam like asbāb from sabab.
Ibn Yaʿīsh said: «Know that the patterns of the small plural (jamʿ al-qilla) are closer to the singular than the patterns of the large plural (jamʿ al-kathra), and for that reason many of the rulings of the singular apply to them. Among these is the permissibility of forming the diminutive of them on their own form, unlike the large plural; and among them is the permissibility of describing a singular with them:
غرب ثوب أسمال وبرمة اكسار
(a ghirb [bucket], a garment of tatters, and a pot of fragments)
and among them is the permissibility of the pronoun referring back to them in the singular form, as in the saying of the Exalted: «وإن لكم في الانعام لعبرة نسقيكم مما في بطونه».»
(عبرة): A lesson, that is, a sign by which one crosses over from ignorance to knowledge. It is a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning "crossing" (ʿubūr), applied by way of hyperbole to that by which one crosses over to knowledge, because it is a cause of the crossing.
(فَرْثٍ): al-Farth is dung, and the foods that have been partly digested in the stomach (kirsh).
al-Ḥarīrī said in Durrat al-Ghawwāṣ: «They say farth for what comes out of the stomach, and that is an error, because it is only called that while it is still inside it; when it comes out it is called sirjīn. Among the proverbs of the Arabs about one who guards the paltry and wastes the precious: "So-and-so guards the farth and ruins the ḥarth (tilled land)".» The answer to this is that the saying is made in regard to what it had been, and the like is frequent and regular.
(سائِغاً): Easy to pass down the throat, one does not choke on it.
(سَكَراً): al-Sakar, with two fatḥas, is wine; it was named by the maṣdar of sakira sakaran and sukran, like rashada rashadan and rushdan. The poet said:
فجاءونا لهم سكر علينا ... فأجلى اليوم والسكران صاح
(They came to us with intoxication upon us; today it cleared, and the drunken man is sober.)
In al-Qāmūs and al-Tāj: sakira yaskaru (of the pattern taʿiba) sakaran with two fatḥas, sukran with a ḍamma then sukūn, sukuran with two ḍammas, sakran with a fatḥa then sukūn, and sakarānan with two fatḥas, from drink, the opposite of being sober; so he is sakir and sakrān, and she is sakra, sakrā and sakrāna, and the plural is sakrā and sakārā with fatḥa on the sīn, and sukārā with ḍamma. Elsewhere it is reported: «There are four sayings about al-sakar: first, that it is one of the names of wine; second, that it is originally a maṣdar and then wine was named by it; third, that it is the name of vinegar in the Abyssinian language; and fourth, that it is the name of the juice for as long as it is sweet, as if it were named figuratively for what it would become if left.»
(يَعْرِشُونَ): They build. Its verb pattern is ḍaraba and naṣara, as in al-Mukhtār; and in al-Qāmūs: ʿarasha yaʿrishu means he built an ʿarīsh (trellis, booth), like aʿrasha, and also ʿarrasha with doubling.

* I'rab:
(وَاللَّهُ أَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً فَأَحْيا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِها) الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause أنزل is the khabar (predicate). من السماء: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أنزل. ماء is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). فأحيا is conjoined to أنزل. به: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أحيا. والأرض is an object. بعد موتها: the adverbial is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآيَةً لِقَوْمٍ يَسْمَعُونَ) إن and its fronted khabar, then the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and آية is the noun of inna; لقوم is an adjective of آية, and the clause يسمعون is an adjective of قوم. (وَإِنَّ لَكُمْ فِي الْأَنْعامِ لَعِبْرَةً) The wāw is a conjunction; إن is a particle resembling the verb; لكم is its fronted khabar; في الأنعام is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of عبرة; then the shifted lām, and عبرة is its delayed noun. (نُسْقِيكُمْ مِمَّا فِي بُطُونِهِ مِنْ بَيْنِ فَرْثٍ وَدَمٍ لَبَناً خالِصاً سائِغاً لِلشَّارِبِينَ) نسقيكم: a verb with a latent agent, and a direct object; مما: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نسقيكم; في بطونه is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. The clause نسقيكم is explicative of عبرة, or is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, like the saying «تسمع بالمعيدي خير من أن تراه» ("that you hear of al-Muʿaydī is better than that you see him"), as if it were said: "the lesson is: we give you to drink". And من بين فرث ودم is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of لبنا and was put before it; and you may make it a ḥāl of the preceding ما. The meaning of the first من is partitive, because the milk is part of what is in their bellies, and the second is of beginning, because the place between the dung and the blood is the place of the giving to drink, from which it begins. لبنا is a second object of نسقيكم, and سائغا is an adjective, and للشاربين is attached to سائغا. (وَمِنْ ثَمَراتِ النَّخِيلِ وَالْأَعْنابِ تَتَّخِذُونَ مِنْهُ سَكَراً وَرِزْقاً حَسَناً) ومن ثمرات النخيل is a fronted khabar, and the clause تتخذون is an adjective of an omitted described noun which is the delayed mubtadaʾ, that is, "fruit from which they used to take intoxicant and goodly provision", because they used to eat some of it and take the intoxicant from another part of it. You may also attach it to an omitted element indicated by نسقيكم, that is, "we give you to drink from the juice of the date palms and grapes"; in that case the clause تتخذون is a ḥāl. Abū Ḥayyān said: «The apparent view is that من ثمرات is attached to تتخذون, and من was repeated for emphasis; the pronoun is singular, taking into account an omitted element, that is, "from the juice of the fruits", or following the meaning of ثمرات, which is al-thamar. It was also said that it is attached to نسقيكم, so that it is conjoined to مما في بطونه; or to an omitted نسقيكم indicated by the preceding نسقيكم, so that it is a conjoining of clauses, whereas the former is a conjoining of single words, when both share the same governor. It was also said that it is conjoined to الأنعام, that is, "and from the fruits of the date palms and grapes there is a lesson", and then he explained the lesson by his saying تتخذون.» Al-Zamakhsharī said: «It is permissible that تتخذون be an adjective of an omitted described noun, as in his saying "بكفي كان من أرمى البشر" ("by my hands there was one of the best archers of mankind"); its implied form is "and from the fruits of the date palms and grapes, fruit from which you take". The pronoun in منه refers back to the implied juice, but the first is more precise.» سكرا is the object of تتخذون, and رزقا is conjoined to سكرا, and حسنا is an adjective. It is not hidden what is produced from grapes and dates, of vinegar, raisins and dibs (grape syrup); and in al-Mukhtār: al-dibs is what flows from ripe dates. (إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآيَةً لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ)
إن and its fronted khabar, the shifted lām, and آية is its delayed noun, and the clause يعقلون is an adjective of قوم. (وَأَوْحى رَبُّكَ إِلَى النَّحْلِ أَنِ اتَّخِذِي مِنَ الْجِبالِ بُيُوتاً وَمِنَ الشَّجَرِ وَمِمَّا يَعْرِشُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction on what precedes, so that the proofs of the wonders of His making and the marvels of His power may proceed in succession; you may also make it resumptive, introduced for what was mentioned. وأوحى ربك: a verb and an agent; والى النحل: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أوحى; and أن is the explicative one (an al-mufassira), because in the inspiration there is the meaning of speech without its letters, and that is the condition set for the explicative أن. You may also make it maṣdar (verbal-noun forming), and it with what follows it is accusative by removal of the preposition, with the preposition and its genitive noun attached to أوحينا, that is, "with: take up (for yourself)"; further explanation of this will come in the section on Benefits, so pay attention to it. من الجبال is attached to اتخذي, and من is partitive, because bees do not build their houses in every mountain, tree and every thing that is trellised; بيوتا is the object of اتخذي; ومن الشجر is conjoined to من الجبال, and likewise مما يعرشون.
(ثُمَّ كُلِي مِنْ كُلِّ الثَّمَراتِ فَاسْلُكِي سُبُلَ رَبِّكِ ذُلُلًا) ثم is a conjunction of delay (tarākhī), and the secret in it is that her seeking of provision comes after her taking of houses, so that she dwells in them and then, after that, seeks provision where it is to be found. كلّيّ is an imperative verb and an agent; من كل الثمرات is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to كلّيّ. فاسلكي: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and اسلكي is conjoined to كلّيّ. سبل ربك is a direct object, and ذللا is a ḥāl from السبل, because Allah made them easy for her and smoothed for her their ground and paths; or from the agent of اسلكي, that is, "while you are compliant with what you were commanded and prepared for". (يَخْرُجُ مِنْ بُطُونِها شَرابٌ مُخْتَلِفٌ أَلْوانُهُ فِيهِ شِفاءٌ لِلنَّاسِ) In the speech there is an iltifāt (shift of address) from the second person to the third, of which we shall speak in the section on Rhetoric. يخرج is an imperfect verb; من بطونها is attached to يخرج; شراب is the agent of يخرج; مختلف is an adjective of شراب; ألوانه is the agent of مختلف, because it is an active participle; فيه is a fronted khabar, شفاء a delayed mubtadaʾ, and للناس is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to شفاء, and the clause is a second adjective of شراب. (إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآيَةً لِقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ) The i'rab of its counterpart was given just before, so renew your acquaintance with it.

* Rhetoric:
1- Iltifāt (shift of address):
In His saying, Exalted is He, «يخرج من بطونها شراب مختلف ألوانه» to the end of the verse, there is a shift from the second person to the third. Had the speech come in the first pattern, it would have said "from your bellies". The speech was turned here from address to the third person for a benefit, namely that He mentioned honey to mankind, its qualities and its different colours, and informed them that it contains varied benefits for them, so as to draw their attention to it. Had He said "from your bellies", that benefit which the third-person address produced would have been lost, and this is not hidden from the critics of speech.

2- Indefiniteness (tankīr):
He made «فيه شفاء» indefinite and did not say "in it is the cure (al-shifāʾ) for all people", and so the objection was repelled that many people eat honey and are not cured of what has afflicted them. One notes that an indefinite noun in an affirmative context does not give generality. Al-Bukhārī, Muslim and others reported from the ḥadīth of Abū Saʿīd that a man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, my brother's belly is loose." He said: "Give him honey to drink." So he gave him honey to drink. Then he came and said: "I gave him honey to drink and it only increased his looseness." He said: "Go and give him honey to drink." So he went and gave him to drink. Then he came and said: "It has only increased his looseness." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah has spoken the truth, and your brother's belly has lied. Go and give him honey to drink." So he went and gave him honey to drink, and he recovered.

3- Tanqīt (the fine point of precision):
In His saying, Exalted is He: «أن اتخذي من الجبال بيوتا» — reference to it has already been made — and it is here in His saying من الجبال, since the meaning of من here is partitive, and He did not say "in the mountains", because bees do not build their houses in every mountain, in every tree and in every thing that is trellised. So He did not leave them freedom in building houses and did not entrust the matter to their desires, as He entrusted it to them in "then eat from the fruits". Rather this was made different, and they were restricted in dwelling but not restricted in food, because the benefit of eating is attained absolutely, since they find wholesome what they desire of it, whereas the benefit of houses is not attained in every place. For this very meaning, ثم was brought in, because of the difference between the two matters and their distance: restriction on them in taking houses, and freedom for them in taking the fruits.

* Benefits:
The explicative أن:
The discussion of the "explicative أن" has been given earlier: it is the one that occurs after a sentence which has the meaning of speech without its letters. It occurs here after the inspiration, because it has in it the meaning of speech, so what follows it has no grammatical position. Among the interesting disputes is that Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Rāzī, the famous Fakhr (al-Dīn), forbade this and said: "We do not concede that it is explicative; how could it be, when the condition of explication is lacking, because the waḥy here is inspiration (ilhām) by agreement, and in inspiration there is no meaning of speech?" He said: "Rather it is maṣdar-forming, that is, 'by taking the mountains as houses'." But al-Fakhr al-Rāzī's imagination carried him away this time, and he did not hit upon the right, since what is meant by speech is informing, and inspiration is an act of Allah which includes informing, such that the one inspired knows what he has been inspired with; and Allah's inspiring the bee is of this kind.

dervis-irab:98-102.t:
* I'rab:
(فَإِذا قَرَأْتَ الْقُرْآنَ فَاسْتَعِذْ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطانِ الرَّجِيمِ) The فاء is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); إذا is an adverbial of future time attached to استعذ; the clause قرأت is the muḍāf ilayhi of the adverbial; and القرآن is the mafʿūl bihi, i.e. "when you intend to recite the Qur'an". The فاء is the connecting fāʾ (rābiṭa) of the apodosis; استعذ is an imperative verb whose fāʿil is "you"; and بالله is attached to استعذ, as is من الشيطان; and الرجيم is an adjective. (إِنَّهُ لَيْسَ لَهُ سُلْطانٌ عَلَى الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَلى رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ) The sentence gives the reason for the command. inna and its noun; the clause ليس is its khabar; وله is a predicate of ليس placed first; سلطان is its delayed noun; على الذين, a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to سلطان because it is a maṣdar meaning "domination", i.e. mastery, subjugation and power; آمنوا is a ṣila; and وعلى ربهم is attached to يتوكلون.
(إِنَّما سُلْطانُهُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ يَتَوَلَّوْنَهُ وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ بِهِ مُشْرِكُونَ) إنما is a restrictive particle (kāffa) and the thing restricted (makfūfa); سلطانه is a mubtadaʾ and على الذين the khabar; the clause يتولونه, made of verb, agent and direct object, is the ṣila of the relative noun and its returning pronoun; والذين is conjoined to the first الذين; the clause هم مشركون is a ṣila, with هم a mubtadaʾ, به attached to مشركون, and مشركون their khabar. (وَإِذا بَدَّلْنا آيَةً مَكانَ آيَةٍ) The و is a conjunction; إذا is an adverbial of the future; بدلنا is verb and agent; آية is the mafʿūl bihi; and مكان is a second object of بدلنا, or an adverbial of place attached to بدلنا; and آية is its muḍāf ilayhi. (وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِما يُنَزِّلُ قالُوا) The و is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya), and the clause is a parenthesis between the condition of إذا and its apodosis, with no grammatical position; الله is a mubtadaʾ and أعلم the khabar; وبما is attached to أعلم; ينزل is a ṣila; and the clause قالوا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of إذا. (إِنَّما أَنْتَ مُفْتَرٍ بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لا يَعْلَمُونَ) The sentence is the content of what was said (maqūl al-qawl); إنما is a restrictive particle and the thing restricted; أنت is a mubtadaʾ and مفتر the khabar; بل is a particle of turning away (iḍrāb); أكثرهم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause لا يعلمون its khabar. The object of يعلمون is omitted because it is known, i.e. the reality of replacement and abrogation and their benefit. (قُلْ نَزَّلَهُ رُوحُ الْقُدُسِ مِنْ رَبِّكَ بِالْحَقِّ لِيُثَبِّتَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا)
The clause نزله is the content of قل: it is a verb with a direct object placed first, and روح is a delayed fāʿil; القدس is its muḍāf ilayhi, a construct of a noun to its attribute, i.e. "the sanctified spirit", who is Jibrīl; ومن ربك is attached to نزله; and بالحق is a ḥāl, i.e. "connected with the truth". In ليثبت the lām is the lām of reason (taʿlīl), and يثبت is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after the lām of reason, its fāʿil being "he"; الذين is the mafʿūl bihi; آمنوا is a ṣila; and ليثبت is in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and genitive through the lām because the maṣdar is not one of the heart, and because the verb differs, since the one who sent down is Jibrīl while the one who confirms is the Qur'an. (وَهُدىً وَبُشْرى لِلْمُسْلِمِينَ) These two maṣdars are conjoined to the position of ليثبت, i.e. "for confirming, guidance and glad tidings".

dervis-irab:103-106.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يُلْحِدُونَ): They incline. One says لحدت القبر and ألحدته; "they buried him in a laḥd" and "mulḥūd"; laḥada li-l-mayyit and alḥada lahu: he dug a laḥd for him; laḥada al-mayyit and alḥadahu: he placed him in the laḥd; laḥada al-sahmu ʿan al-hadaf and alḥada: the arrow swerved from the target; alḥada fī dīn Allāh and laḥada ʿan al-qaṣd: he deviated from it; alḥada fī al-ḥaram; laḥada ilayhi: he inclined to him; iltaḥada ilayhi: he sought refuge with him, and "mālī dūnahu multaḥad" (I have no refuge besides him). Dhū al-Rumma said:
إذا استوسجت آذانها استأنست لها ... أناسيّ ملحود لها في الحواجب
(When their ears pricked up, there took fright at them the pupils, set deep within the brows.) «[Translator's note: the verse is rendered as it stands in the source; its wording and sense are obscure.]»

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ نَعْلَمُ أَنَّهُمْ يَقُولُونَ) The و is a conjunction; the lām prepares for the oath; قد is a particle meant here to convey frequency; نعلم is an imperfect verb with a latent fāʿil; and أن with what is in its scope takes the place of the two objects of نعلم; أن and its noun, and the clause يقولون is its khabar.
(إِنَّما يُعَلِّمُهُ بَشَرٌ) The sentence is the content of their saying; إنما is a restrictive particle and the thing restricted; يعلمه is a verb with its direct object placed first, and بشر is a delayed fāʿil. He is a smith (qayn), that is a Roman blacksmith whose name was Jabr (with fatḥa on the jīm and sukūn on the single-dotted bāʾ), the slave of ʿĀmir ibn al-Ḥaḍramī. It is also said that they meant Jabr and Yasār, who used to make swords in Mecca and read the Torah and the Gospel, and the Messenger ﷺ used to pass by them and hear what they were reading. Other things are said as well, none of which departs from the subject. (لِسانُ الَّذِي يُلْحِدُونَ إِلَيْهِ أَعْجَمِيٌّ وَهذا لِسانٌ عَرَبِيٌّ مُبِينٌ) لسان is a mubtadaʾ and الذي its muḍāf ilayhi; the clause يلحدون إليه is a ṣila; أعجمي is the khabar of لسان, i.e. not clear; هذا is a mubtadaʾ, عربي the khabar, and مبين an adjective. This is an emphasis on the Arabic nature of the language of the Qur'an. The point of the reply is that the man to whom they attribute teaching the Qur'an to the Prophet is a non-Arab with a thickness and foreignness in his tongue which prevent him from speaking out and expressing clearly, whereas Muḥammad ﷺ is the one who brought you this clear Qur'an, of the like of one sūra of which you were unable to produce. (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِآياتِ اللَّهِ لا يَهْدِيهِمُ اللَّهُ وَلَهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ) inna and its noun; the clause لا يؤمنون is a ṣila; بآيات الله is attached to يؤمنون; the clause لا يهديهم الله is the khabar of inna; the و is a conjunction; ولهم is a predicate placed first, عذاب a delayed mubtadaʾ, and أليم its adjective. (إِنَّما يَفْتَرِي الْكَذِبَ الَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِآياتِ اللَّهِ) إنما is a restrictive particle and the thing restricted; يفتري is an imperfect verb; الكذب is the mafʿūl bihi placed first; الذين is a delayed fāʿil; and the clause لا يؤمنون بآيات الله is a ṣila. (وَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْكاذِبُونَ) The و is parenthetical; أولئك is a mubtadaʾ; هم is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) or a second mubtadaʾ; and الكاذبون is the khabar of أولئك or of هم, the sentence then being the khabar of أولئك; and the clause أولئك هم الكاذبون is parenthetical.
(مَنْ كَفَرَ بِاللَّهِ مِنْ بَعْدِ إِيمانِهِ إِلَّا مَنْ أُكْرِهَ وَقَلْبُهُ مُطْمَئِنٌّ بِالْإِيمانِ) The best of the analyses which the i'rab scholars have given for من is that it is a badal (substitute) for الذين لا يؤمنون بآيات الله, with the clause وأولئك هم الكاذبون a parenthesis between the substitute and what it substitutes for, the meaning being "only those who disbelieve in Allah after their belief invent falsehood". It is also possible, though remote, to analyse it as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause فعليهم, the فاء being added because the relative noun includes the sense of a condition, and the clause كفر بالله being a ṣila; it is likewise possible to analyse من as conditional. بالله, a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to كفر; ومن بعد إيمانه is a ḥāl; إلا is a particle of exception; and من is an excepted noun, connected (muttaṣil), because disbelief can be by word without belief. It is also said that it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), because disbelief is a conviction, while the one compelled to speak without conviction is like one who is forced. The clause أكره is the ṣila of the relative noun; وقلبه: the و is circumstantial, قلبه is a mubtadaʾ and مطمئن the khabar; and بالإيمان is attached to مطمئن. (وَلكِنْ مَنْ شَرَحَ بِالْكُفْرِ صَدْراً فَعَلَيْهِمْ غَضَبٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَلَهُمْ عَذابٌ عَظِيمٌ) ولكن: the و is resumptive and لكن is a particle resembling the verb, its noun being the pronoun of the situation (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); من is a mubtadaʾ; شرح is the protasis if you make من conditional, and a ṣila if you make it relative; الله is the fāʿil, and صدرا is a tamyīz (specification), i.e. his soul was at ease with it and he held it as belief. فعليهم: the فاء is the connecting fāʾ; عليهم is a predicate placed first and غضب a delayed mubtadaʾ; ومن الله is an adjective; ولهم is a predicate placed first and عذاب a delayed mubtadaʾ; and عظيم is an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
Compelling (al-iljāʾ):
In His saying, Exalted is He: «وَلَقَدْ نَعْلَمُ أَنَّهُمْ يَقُولُونَ إِنَّما يُعَلِّمُهُ بَشَرٌ إلخ» and Allah's saying, Exalted is He, in reply to this statement: «لِسانُ الَّذِي يُلْحِدُونَ إِلَيْهِ أَعْجَمِيٌّ وَهذا لِسانٌ عَرَبِيٌّ مُبِينٌ». Al-iljāʾ is an art which the scholars of badīʿ have not often mentioned. Usāma ibn Munqidh spoke of it in his Badīʿ under the name al-iltijāʾ and al-mughālaṭa. It is that the soundness of a flawed speech appears to depend on bringing into it something which the opponent hastens to reject by means of something that compels him to admit its soundness; or, to put it more plainly: for every speech in which a flawed answer is given to the objector, if the opponent enters into it he is driven to affirm the answer, as in the verse just mentioned. The opponent may say: "We meant the stories and reports, and we know that when a non-Arab delivers speech to an Arab it does not take it out of being something whose meanings he learned from the non-Arab; so the apparent speech cannot be a reply to the polytheists." To them it is said: Suppose the non-Arab taught him the meanings; who then taught him this formidable expression, which cut off your hopes of producing its like? If he brought it from himself, then you have admitted that one man among you brought this quantity of speech, which is a hundred and fourteen sūras, while all of you, and all whom you call upon besides Allah, were unable to bring the shortest of its sūras. And if you say that the non-Arab taught him the meanings and the words, this is harder on you, for it is an admission that a non-Arab man was able to produce verses embodying reports and stories while you were unable to produce three verses of them. That compels them to admit that it is from Allah.

* Benefits:
The story of ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir:
History relates that some people of Mecca were put to trial and apostatised from Islam after entering it, and among them were some who were compelled and let a word of disbelief run on their tongue while holding to faith. Among them were ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir and his parents Yāsir and Sumayya, Ṣuhayb, Bilāl, Khabbāb and Sālim, who were tortured. As for Sumayya, the mother of ʿAmmār, they tied her between two camels and Abū Jahl struck her in the heart with a spear, and she died; her husband Yāsir was killed, and they were the first two killed in Islam. As for ʿAmmār, he gave them part of what they wanted with his tongue under compulsion. It was said, "O Messenger of Allah, ʿAmmār has disbelieved." He said: "Never! ʿAmmār is filled with faith from the crown of his head to his foot, and faith is mingled with his flesh and blood." ʿAmmār came to the Messenger of Allah weeping, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "What is behind you?" He said: "Evil, O Messenger of Allah; I harmed you and mentioned them." The Prophet ﷺ began to wipe his eyes and said: "If they return to it, say to them what you said", up to the end of this delightful story, to which one refers in the longer works.

dervis-irab:70-72.t:
* Vocabulary:
(حَفَدَةً): al-Ḥafada is the plural of ḥāfid, and he is the one who yaḥfidu, that is, hastens in obedience and service. The poet said:
حفد الولائد بينهن وأسلمت ... بأكفهنّ أزمة الأجمال
(The young slave-girls hastened among them, and the reins of the camels were handed over into their palms.)
In al-Ṣiḥāḥ: «al-Ḥafada are the helpers, and also the servants.» And in al-Mukhtār: «al-Ḥafd is haste, and its verb pattern is ḍaraba, and also ḥafdan with fatḥa on the fāʾ; from it is their saying in the supplication "wa-ilayka nasʿā wa-naḥfidu" (to You we strive and hasten); aḥfadahu means he made him hasten. Some make aḥfada intransitive. And al-ḥafad, with two fatḥas, are the helpers and servants; it was also said to be the child of the child, and the singular of them is ḥāfid.» And in al-Qāmūs and al-Tāj: «ḥafada yaḥfidu, of the pattern ḍaraba, ḥafdan with sukūn on the fāʾ, ḥufūdan and ḥafadānan; iḥtafada fī l-ʿamal means he hastened in the work; ḥafadahu means he served him; aḥfada l-ẓalīm means the male ostrich hastened; and aḥfadahu means he made him hasten, that is, hurry. And al-ḥafīd is the child of the child, its plural being ḥufadāʾ; and al-ḥāfid is the servant, the follower, the helper and the child of the child, its plural being ḥafada and ḥufad. And al-ḥafada are also the makers of embroidered cloth (washy).» The exegetes have a long discussion about who is meant by them, and the word allows for all of them, since al-ḥafada includes many meanings, as preceded.

* I'rab:
(وَاللَّهُ خَلَقَكُمْ ثُمَّ يَتَوَفَّاكُمْ وَمِنْكُمْ مَنْ يُرَدُّ إِلى أَرْذَلِ الْعُمُرِ) الله is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause خلقكم is the khabar. ثم is a conjunction of delay, as preceded. ومنكم: the wāw is a conjunction, and منكم is a fronted khabar, conjoined to an implied element, that is, "so among you is one who remains keeping the strength of his body and mind, and among you...". من is a delayed mubtadaʾ, and the clause يرد is a ṣila, with the deputy agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he". إلى أرذل العمر is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يرد; and أرذل العمر is senility, where the eyes sink in, movements weaken, the joints tremble, frailty creeps into all parts of the body and dotage overcomes it.
(لِكَيْ لا يَعْلَمَ بَعْدَ عِلْمٍ شَيْئاً إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ قَدِيرٌ) The lām is the lām of cause; كي is a maṣdar-forming particle that governs the accusative; لا is a negative; يعلم is accusative by كي; the lām and what follows it are attached to يرد. It is also permissible that the lām be the lām of consequence (ṣayrūra), that is, "the end result of it was that he returned to the state of childhood, in forgetfulness and lack of perception". بعد علم is an adverbial attached to يعلم, and شيئا is the direct object of يعلم. You may also make the matter one of tanāzuʿ (competition of two governors for one object), so that you put شيئا in the accusative by al-ʿilm, which is a maṣdar. إن and its noun; عليم is its first khabar and قدير its second khabar. (وَاللَّهُ فَضَّلَ بَعْضَكُمْ عَلى بَعْضٍ فِي الرِّزْقِ) الله is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause فضل is the khabar; بعضكم is a direct object; على بعض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to فضل; and في الرزق is a ḥāl, that is, "in your state of being provided for": among you is the rich and among you the poor. (فَمَا الَّذِينَ فُضِّلُوا بِرَادِّي رِزْقِهِمْ عَلى ما مَلَكَتْ أَيْمانُهُمْ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; ما is the Ḥijāzī negative; الذين is its noun, and the clause فضلوا is a ṣila. The bāʾ is a redundant preposition, and رادي is genitive in form, and in the position of the khabar of ما. رزقهم is a muḍāf ilayhi, as a case of the maṣdar being annexed to its object. على ما is attached to رادي, and ملكت أيمانهم is a ṣila.
(فَهُمْ فِيهِ سَواءٌ) The fāʾ is a conjunction, to indicate that the equality follows upon the returning, that is, they do not return to them a return that entails equality, but only return to them a small thing. هم is a mubtadaʾ; فيه is attached to سواء; and سواء is the khabar of هم. The discussion of this eloquent concision (ījāz) will come in the section on Rhetoric. (أَفَبِنِعْمَةِ اللَّهِ يَجْحَدُونَ) An interrogative of denial and rebuke, and the fāʾ is a conjunction on an implied element, that is, "they associate others with Him, and then deny His blessing". بنعمة الله is attached to يجحدون because it includes the meaning of ingratitude (kufrān). (وَاللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِنْ أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَزْواجاً) الله is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause جعل is the khabar; لكم is attached to جعل; من أنفسكم is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of أزواجا; and أزواجا is the object of جعل. (وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِنْ أَزْواجِكُمْ بَنِينَ وَحَفَدَةً) Conjoined to what preceded, and its i'rab is the same as theirs. (وَرَزَقَكُمْ مِنَ الطَّيِّباتِ أَفَبِالْباطِلِ يُؤْمِنُونَ وَبِنِعْمَتِ اللَّهِ هُمْ يَكْفُرُونَ) ورزقكم: a past verb, a latent agent and a direct object; من الطيبات is attached to رزقكم; the hamza is for interrogative denial and rebuke, and the fāʾ is a conjunction on an implied element, that is, "they disbelieve in Allah and so believe in falsehood". وبنعمة الله is attached to يكفرون; هم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يكفرون is the khabar.

* Rhetoric:
Concision (al-ījāz):
In His saying, Exalted is He, «فهم فيه سواء» there is an eloquent concision, and an indication of the loftiest ordinances which people must follow in their worldly life so that their affairs may be set straight, the causes of enmity and quarrel may leave their hearts, and peace may prevail among them. For He, Exalted is He, informed that He made them differ in provision, but this difference does not mean preferring them over others in humanity; or it is as if He is pointing out that duty obliges you to return the surplus of what you have been given to them, until you are equal in clothing and food. It is reported from Abū Dharr al-Ghifārī that he heard the Prophet ﷺ say: «They are only your brothers, so clothe them from what you wear and feed them from what you eat.» This meaning is made more firm by the rebuke and reproach that follows, because they made distinctions among people and did not tell the classes apart. And in His saying, Exalted is He, «إلى أرذل العمر» there is another concision: to senility and the states of weakness and dotage it requires, which bring the helpless and aged person near to the first world of childhood, with the clear difference between the hope that attends childhood, with its signs that give good news of future success, and the hope for an easy life to come. As for now, he has nothing before him but to endure the states from which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to seek refuge, in his saying: «O Allah, I seek refuge in You from miserliness, laziness, the most abject old age, the punishment of the grave, and the trial of life and death.»

dervis-irab:107-111.t:
* Vocabulary:
(النفس): From the sum of the statements of the Arabic dictionaries it is taken that nafs is a verbal noun, and is also the spirit, blood (one says "he poured out his nafs", i.e. his blood), the body (one says "he is great of nafs", i.e. of body), the eye (one says "a nafs struck him", i.e. an evil eye), and a person's self; the nafs of a thing is its very self, and it is used for emphasis, so one says "he came to me, himself" and "by himself"; nafs al-amr is its reality. Nafs also means greatness, aspiration, might, pride, will, opinion, punishment and water. Nafs is feminine if the spirit is meant, as in "his nafs went out", and masculine if a person is meant, as in "I have fifteen persons (nafs)"; the plural is anfus and nufūs. One says "it is in my nafs to do something", i.e. my intention and wish is to do such-and-such; "so-and-so consults his two nafs's" means he wavers in the matter and two opinions present themselves to him, and he does not know which to hold to; "his nafs went out" and "he was generous with his nafs" are said when one dies. As for the meaning of nafs among the philosophers, it goes back to psychology, and this is not the place for it; the disagreement about it is long, and Abū al-Ṭayyib was right when he said:
تخالف الناس حتى لا اتفاق لهم ... إلا على شجب والخلف في الشجب
(People disagree until they have no agreement except on perdition, and they disagree even about perdition.)
فقيل تخلص نفس المرء سالمة ... وقيل تشرك جسم المرء في العطب
(It was said that a man's soul is delivered safe, and it was said that it shares the body in destruction.)
ومن تفكر في الدنيا ومهجته ... أقامه الفكر بين الهمّ والتعب
(And whoever reflects on the world and his own heart's blood, reflection leaves him standing between care and toil.)
From the poem of al-Raʾīs Ibn Sīnā on the soul:
It is useful to quote here chosen verses from the poem of Shaykh al-Raʾīs Abū ʿAlī ibn Sīnā on the soul:
هبطت إليك من المحل الأرفع ... ورقاء ذات تعزّز وتمنع
(There descended to you from the loftiest station a dove, proud and unapproachable.)
محجوب عن كل مقلة عارف ... وهي التي سفرت ولم تتبرقع
(Veiled from every discerning eye, though it is she who unveiled and wore no veil.) «[Translator's note: the source has «محجوب», masculine, with a feminine referent.]»
وصلت على كره إليك وربما ... كرهت فراقك وهي ذات توجع
(She reached you unwillingly, and perhaps she hated parting from you, for she is full of pain.)
أنفت وما أنست فلما واصلت ... ألفت مجاورة الغراب الأبقع
(She disdained, and was not at ease; but when she joined, she grew used to neighbouring the piebald raven.)
وأظنها نسيت عهودا بالحمى ... ومنازلا بفراقها لم تقنع
(And I think she forgot pledges in the sanctuary and abodes whose parting she did not accept.)
حتى إذا اتصلت بهاء هبوطها ... عن ميم مركزها بذات الاجرع
(Until, when she joined with the hāʾ of her descent, from the mīm of her centre, at Dhāt al-Ajraʿ,)
علقت بها ثاء الثقيل فأصبحت ... بين المعالم والطلول الخضع
(the thāʾ of the heavy clung to her, and she became, among the landmarks and the humble ruins,)
تبكي وقد ذكرت عهودا بالحمى ... بمدامع تهمي ولما تقلع
(weeping, having remembered pledges in the sanctuary, with tears that stream and have not ceased,)
وتظل ساجعة على الدمن التي ... درست بتكرار الرياح الأربع
(and she keeps cooing over the dung-heaped remains that have been effaced by the repeated visits of the four winds.)
«[Translator's note: in the source the line division of the fifth to seventh verses is disordered (the second hemistich of one verse runs into the next, and the letters ميم, هاء and ثاء are split off). The text is translated as it stands; the glosses are approximate.]»
Our discourse would grow long if we tried to explain what these verses, quoted from the splendid ʿayniyya, allude to. The sum of what he meant is that he asks: why did the soul become attached to the body? If its guide was something other than perfection, then she is wise but hidden from minds; and if its guide was perfection, why did her attachment to it not cease before perfection was attained?

* I'rab:
(ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمُ اسْتَحَبُّوا الْحَياةَ الدُّنْيا عَلَى الْآخِرَةِ) The demonstrative points to what was mentioned before of wrath and punishment. The demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is بأنهم, i.e. "established because they…", so the ب is causal; أن and its noun, and the clause استحبوا is its khabar, i.e. "they chose"; الحياة is the mafʿūl bihi and الدنيا an adjective; and على الآخرة, a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to استحبوا. (وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الْكافِرِينَ) وأن is conjoined to بأنهم; أن and its noun, and the clause لا يهدي is its khabar; القوم is the mafʿūl bihi and الكافرين an adjective of القوم. (أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ طَبَعَ اللَّهُ عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ وَسَمْعِهِمْ وَأَبْصارِهِمْ وَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْغافِلُونَ) أولئك is a mubtadaʾ and الذين its khabar; the clause طبع الله is a ṣila; على قلوبهم, a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to طبع; and سمعهم and أبصارهم are conjoined to قلوبهم. وأولئك is a mubtadaʾ; هم is a second mubtadaʾ or a separating pronoun; and الغافلون is the khabar of هم or of أولئك. (لا جَرَمَ أَنَّهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ هُمُ الْخاسِرُونَ) What was said about لا جرم has been given before; أن and its noun; في الآخرة is attached to الخاسرون; هم is a mubtadaʾ and الخاسرون its khabar, and the sentence is the khabar of أن. (ثُمَّ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لِلَّذِينَ هاجَرُوا مِنْ بَعْدِ ما فُتِنُوا ثُمَّ جاهَدُوا وَصَبَرُوا) ثم denotes order with a lapse of time, because the state of these people is far from the state of those; inna and its noun; للذين is the khabar of inna, meaning that He is their protector and helper; the clause هاجروا is a ṣila; ومن بعد is attached to هاجروا; ما is a maṣdar particle, interpreted with what follows as a maṣdar added to the adverbial, i.e. "after their trial"; ثم is a conjunction denoting lapse of time; and جاهدوا and صبروا are conjoined to هاجروا. (إِنَّ رَبَّكَ مِنْ بَعْدِها لَغَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ) inna and its noun; ومن بعدها is a ḥāl; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); غفور is the first khabar of inna and رحيم its second. The i'rab scholars have gone on at length over the i'rab of this verse and their statements have been greatly confused through their excessive care and their pursuit of the right place; their effort is appreciated, but there is no need for all that, for the speech is clear and without obscurity. (يَوْمَ تَأْتِي كُلُّ نَفْسٍ تُجادِلُ عَنْ نَفْسِها) The adverbial is attached to an omitted verb, i.e. "remember"; the clause تأتي is added to the adverbial; كل نفس is the fāʿil of تأتي; the clause تجادل is a ḥāl; and عن نفسها is attached to تجادل. The annexation of nafs to nafs is permissible although one condition of two terms in a genitive construct is that they be different from each other, because by the first nafs the human being is meant and by the second his very self; it is as though He said, "the day every human being comes disputing on behalf of his own self", i.e. making excuses for it, not caring about the affairs of anyone else. (وَتُوَفَّى كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ما عَمِلَتْ وَهُمْ لا يُظْلَمُونَ) وتوفى is conjoined to تجادل; كل نفس is the nāʾib fāʿil; ما عملت is the second object of توفى; وهم: the و is circumstantial or a conjunction, هم is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause لا يظلمون is its khabar. «[Translator's note: the source prints «متدأ» for «مبتدأ».]»

dervis-irab:73-76.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أَبْكَمُ): al-Abkam is one who was born mute, so it is more specific than the mute in general. In al-Qāmūs: «al-Bukm, vocalised, is muteness, like bakāma, or it is with incapacity of speech and dullness, or that one is born and neither speaks, nor hears, nor sees; bakima, like fariḥa, so he is abkam and bakīm, and the plural is bukm; and bakuma, like karuma, means he refrained from speaking deliberately.» Thaʿlab reported from Ibn al-Aʿrābī: «al-Abkam is one who neither hears nor sees.» On this basis he is distinguished from the mute (akhras) in that he neither understands nor is understood, whereas the mute understands by hearing or by gesture, and is understood by gesture.
(كَلٌّ): Heavy on the one who takes charge of his affairs and supports him. In al-Qāmūs and elsewhere: «It is the maṣdar of kalla yakillu (pattern taʿiba), kallan, kalla, kalālan, kulūlan, kalālatan, kulūlatan: he became weary and exhausted. Also the weak; one who has neither child nor father; the back of the knife or sword; the agent (wakīl); the idol; the calamity that befalls; the dependant (ʿayyil) and dependants (ʿiyāl); and the burden. The word kall is used for one or more, and some make the plural of masculine and feminine kulūl.»

* I'rab:
(وَيَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ ما لا يَمْلِكُ لَهُمْ رِزْقاً مِنَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ) The wāw is a conjunction; يعبدون is an imperfect verb and an agent; من دون الله is a ḥāl; ما is a direct object, and the clause لا يملك is a ṣila; رزقا is a direct object; and من السموات والأرض is an adjective of رزقا, or is attached to رزقا. (شَيْئاً وَلا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ) شيئا is a direct object of رزقا if you intend by it the maṣdar or the ism al-maṣdar (noun of the verbal noun), as in His saying, Exalted is He: «أو إطعام في يوم ذي مسغبة يتيما ...»; and if you intend by it that which is provided, then شيئا is a substitute for it, in the sense of "a little". A detailed discussion of the i'rab of شيئا, which must be known, will come in the section on Benefits. As for ولا يستطيعون, it is permissible for this clause to be conjoined to the ṣila of ما, with the report about them of lack of ability being in accordance with its meaning, because ما here is singular in form and plural in meaning; and it may be resumptive. In any case the wāw refers back to ما, and what is meant by it is their gods. (فَلا تَضْرِبُوا لِلَّهِ الْأَمْثالَ) The fāʾ is resumptive; لا is prohibitive; تضربوا is an imperfect verb in the jussive and the wāw is the agent; لله is attached to تضربوا; and الأمثال is a direct object, because striking a parable is likening one state to another, and that is incompatible with the Divine Essence. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ وَأَنْتُمْ لا تَعْلَمُونَ) إن and its noun, and the clause يعلم is the khabar; the sentence is causal. وأنتم: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), أنتم is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause لا تعلمون is the khabar. (ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا عَبْداً مَمْلُوكاً لا يَقْدِرُ عَلى شَيْءٍ) A resumptive clause to teach them how Allah strikes a parable. ضرب الله مثلا: a verb, an agent and a direct object; عبدا is a substitute for مثلا; مملوكا is an adjective; and the clause لا يقدر على شيء is a second adjective; على شيء is attached to يقدر, that is, "of disposals". (وَمَنْ رَزَقْناهُ مِنَّا رِزْقاً حَسَناً) The wāw is a conjunction, and من is conjoined to عبدا مملوكا; من is a relative noun or an indefinite noun that is described, as if it were said "and a free man whom We have provided", to correspond with عبدا; the clause رزقناه is a ṣila on the first view and an adjective on the second; نا is the agent and the ه is a direct object; منا is attached to رزقناه; رزقا is a second direct object if you intend by it that which is provided, or a mafʿūl muṭlaq if you intend the maṣdar; and حسنا is an adjective of رزقا. (فَهُوَ يُنْفِقُ مِنْهُ سِرًّا وَجَهْراً هَلْ يَسْتَوُونَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; هو is a mubtadaʾ and the clause ينفق is the khabar; منه is attached to ينفق; سرا and جهرا are two maṣdars in the accusative as mafʿūl muṭlaq, that is, "a spending in secret and in public", or they are in the accusative as ḥāl, that is, "secretly and openly". The putting of secrecy before openness indicates its superiority over it and that the reward in it is greater. هل is an interrogative particle for negation. The pronoun in يستوون is plural although two were mentioned before it, because what is meant is the kind of free men and slaves indicated by the two; the meaning is: free men and slaves are not equal. (الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لا يَعْلَمُونَ) الحمد is a mubtadaʾ and لله is the khabar; بل is a particle of turning away (iḍrāb); أكثرهم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause لا يعلمون is the khabar. He brought the informative clause to guide the servant to the obligation of thanking the Benefactor for the favours and bounties He has lavished. (وَضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا رَجُلَيْنِ) The wāw is a conjunction; ضرب الله مثلا: a verb, an agent and a direct object; and رجلين is a substitute for مثلا. (أَحَدُهُما أَبْكَمُ لا يَقْدِرُ عَلى شَيْءٍ) أحدهما is a mubtadaʾ and أبكم is its khabar, and the clause لا يقدر على شيء is an adjective of أبكم. (وَهُوَ كَلٌّ عَلى مَوْلاهُ) The wāw is circumstantial; هو is a mubtadaʾ and كل is its khabar; على مولاه is attached to كل. (أَيْنَما يُوَجِّهْهُ لا يَأْتِ بِخَيْرٍ) أينما is a jussive-governing conditional noun, in the position of the accusative as a locative adverbial, and it is attached to the verb of the protasis, as is the rule; it was also said to be attached to its apodosis, and each has an argument. Al-Raḍī said: «The governor in matā and every adverbial that has the meaning of a condition is its protasis, according to what most have said,» other than idhā; and the sound view is that the governor in it is the apodosis. Ibn al-Ḥājib gave a reason for it and said: the protasis and the requital are two clauses, and it is not valid for the apodosis to govern the conditional noun, because that would lead to their becoming one clause: for if it were an adverbial of it, it would be part of its completion, and it would not be a second clause. As for idhā, the governor in it is the requital, and the reason for that is the strength of the suggestion of annexation in idhā and its weakness in matā. Some made a distinction and said: «It is better that we distinguish and say: if idhā includes the meaning of condition, its ruling is the ruling of its sisters such as matā and the like; and if it does not include it, as in "idhā gharabat al-shams jiʾtuka" (when the sun sets I will come to you), meaning "I shall come to you at the time of sunset", the governor is the verb that is in the position of the requital, even if it is not a requital in reality, not the one in the position of the protasis, since it is a specifier of the adverbial; and its specifying it is either because it is its adjective or because it is annexed to it, and there is no third, by induction.» يوجهه is the verb of the protasis and لا is negative, and يأت is the apodosis, and بخير is attached to يأت. (هَلْ يَسْتَوِي هُوَ وَمَنْ يَأْمُرُ بِالْعَدْلِ وَهُوَ عَلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ) هل is an interrogative particle whose meaning is negation; يستوي is an imperfect verb; هو is emphasis for the latent agent; and من is conjoined to the latent agent in يستوي, and the condition is met, which is conjoining with a detached pronoun, namely the word هو. وهو is a mubtadaʾ and على صراط مستقيم is its khabar, and the nominal sentence is the ṣila of من. The counterpart of «أحدهما أبكم» was omitted, being indicated by His saying «ومن يأمر», that is, "and the other is articulate, capable, light for his master: wherever he directs him, he brings good".

* Benefits:
The difference between the maṣdar and the ism al-maṣdar:
There has been much disagreement about the i'rab of شيئا, and for this reason an extended discussion of the working of the maṣdar is needed. The difference between them is that the maṣdar is that which has a verb that conforms to it, like al-inṭilāq (going off) in inṭalaqa; and the ism al-maṣdar is a noun of the meaning that has no verb conforming to it, like al-qahqarā (retreating), for it denotes a kind of returning and has no verb derived from its wording. They sometimes also say maṣdar and ism maṣdar for two things that differ in wording, one of which is for the verb and the other for the signification with which the verb is used, such as al-ṭahūr and al-ṭuhūr, and al-akl and al-ukl: al-ṭahūr (with fatḥa) is the maṣdar and al-ṭuhūr is the name of what one purifies oneself with; al-akl is the maṣdar and al-ukl is what is eaten.
The maṣdar works as its verb works if a verb can take its place, either with the maṣdar-forming أن and the time being past or future, as in ʿajibtu min ḍarbika Zaydan amsi (I marvelled at your striking Zayd yesterday), and yuʿjibunī ḍarbuka Zaydan ghadan (your striking Zayd tomorrow pleases me); or with the maṣdar-forming ما and the time being the present only, as in yuʿjibunī ḍarbuka Zaydan al-ān, that is, "what you strike Zayd now". The working of the maṣdar when annexed is more frequent than its working when not annexed, as in «ولولا دفع الله الناس»; its working when it carries tanwīn is the analogical norm, because it is nearer to resembling the verb through its indefiniteness, as in «أو إطعام في يوم ذي مسغبة يتيما»: إطعام is a maṣdar whose agent is latent and يتيما is its object; and its working when defined by al- is rare in what is heard and weak in analogy, because it is far from resembling the verb, as in the verse:
ضعيف النكاية أعداءه ... يخال الفرار يراخي الأجل
(Weak in injuring his enemies, he imagines that flight postpones the appointed term.)
Here al-nikāya is a maṣdar joined with al-, and أعداءه is its object; the meaning is "weak is his injuring of his enemies; he thinks that fleeing from death puts the term at a distance".
As for the ism al-maṣdar, it also works like the maṣdar if it is of the mīm type, as in the verse of al-ʿArjī, and it was said al-Ḥārith ibn Khālid al-Makhzūmī:
أظلوم إن مصابكم رجلا ... أهدى السلام تحية ظلم
(O Ẓalūm, your striking a man who offered the greeting of peace as a salutation is an injustice.)
Here muṣāb is a mīmī maṣdar annexed to its agent, and رجلا is its object, and the clause أهدى السلام is an adjective of رجلا, and تحية is a mafʿūl muṭlaq. The story of this verse will come. If it is not of the mīm type, it does not work according to the Basrans, because it was originally set down for other than the maṣdar: al-ghusl is set down for that with which one washes, and al-wuḍūʾ for that with which one performs ablution. And it works according to the Kufans and a group of the Basrans, and on this is the verse of al-Quṭāmī:
أكفرا بعد رد الموت عني ... وبعد عطائك المائة الرتاعا
(Is it ingratitude, after you turned death away from me, and after your giving of the grazing hundred?)
Here ʿaṭāʾ is an ism maṣdar annexed to its agent, and المائة is its second object; as for the first, it is omitted, that is, "your giving me the hundred ar-rutāʿ", meaning al-rātiʿa, which are the camels that graze. The reality is that the sayings of the Basrans are inconsistent: some said it is permissible and some said it is forbidden.
The story of the verse of al-ʿArjī:
A slave-girl sang in the presence of al-Wāthiq some of the poetry of al-ʿArjī:
أظلوم إن مصابكم رجلا ... أهدى السلام تحية ظلم
Those present disagreed about the i'rab of رجلا: some put it in the accusative and made it the noun of inna, and some put it in the nominative as its khabar; and the slave-girl insisted that her teacher Abū ʿUthmān al-Māzinī had taught it to her with the accusative. So al-Wāthiq ordered him summoned. Abū ʿUthmān said: When I stood before him, he said: "From whom is the man?" I said: "From Māzin." He said: "From which Māzin?" I said: "From Māzin Rabīʿa." He spoke to me in the speech of my people and said: "Mā ismuka?" (for they turn the mīm into bāʾ and the bāʾ into mīm when it is at the beginning of nouns). I disliked answering him in the dialect of my people so as not to confront him with ill-nature, and said: "Bakr, O Commander of the Faithful." He grasped what I intended and was pleased with me for that. Then he said: "What do you say about the saying of the poet:
أظلوم إن مصابكم رجلا ... أهدى السلام تحية ظلم
Do you put رجلا in the nominative or the accusative?" I said: "The accusative is the correct form." He said: "Why?" I said: "Because muṣābukum is a maṣdar meaning iṣābatukum, and it is in the position of your saying 'inna ḍarbaka Zaydan ẓulm' (your striking Zayd is an injustice); so al-rajul is the object of muṣāb and is put in the accusative by it, and the proof is that the speech remains incomplete until you say ẓulm, and then it is complete." Al-Wāthiq approved of it and ordered a thousand dinars for him.

dervis-irab:112-113.t:
* I'rab:
(وَضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا قَرْيَةً كانَتْ آمِنَةً مُطْمَئِنَّةً يَأْتِيها رِزْقُها رَغَداً مِنْ كُلِّ مَكانٍ) The و is resumptive; ضرب الله مثلا is verb, agent and direct object; and قرية is a badal (substitute) for مثلا, i.e. He made the town marked by these features an example for every people upon whom Allah bestowed favours and whom the favour made arrogant, so they disbelieved. The clause كانت is an adjective of قرية; كان with its latent noun, آمنة is its khabar and مطمئنة a second khabar, and the clause يأتيها a third khabar; it is an imperfect verb with a direct object placed first, and رزقها is a delayed fāʿil; رغدا describes the maṣdar, i.e. "an abundant coming", so it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), or it has the sense of "abundant" and is a ḥāl; and من كل مكان is attached to يأتيها. (فَكَفَرَتْ بِأَنْعُمِ اللَّهِ فَأَذاقَهَا اللَّهُ لِباسَ الْجُوعِ وَالْخَوْفِ بِما كانُوا يَصْنَعُونَ) The فاء is a conjunction; كفرت is a past verb whose latent fāʿil refers to the town; and بأنعم الله is attached to كفرت. In فأذاقها the فاء is a conjunction denoting immediate sequence; أذاقها is a verb, with a direct object placed first and a delayed fāʿil; لباس الجوع والخوف is the second object; the ب is a preposition of causation; and ما is a maṣdar particle or a relative noun with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. "because of what they did" or "because of that which they used to do". (وَلَقَدْ جاءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ مِنْهُمْ فَكَذَّبُوهُ) The و is a conjunction; the lām prepares for the oath; قد is a particle of affirmation; جاءهم is a past verb with a direct object placed first and a delayed fāʿil, رسول; منهم is an adjective of رسول; فكذبوه: the فاء is a conjunction, and كذبوه is verb, agent and direct object. (فَأَخَذَهُمُ الْعَذابُ وَهُمْ ظالِمُونَ) فأخذهم is conjoined to فكذبوه; العذاب is the fāʿil; the و is circumstantial; هم is a mubtadaʾ and ظالمون the khabar, and the sentence is a ḥāl.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying, Exalted is He, «وضرب الله مثلا قرية» there are one majāz mursal (unrestricted trope) and two istiʿāra makniyya (implicit metaphors). As for the majāz mursal, it is in His saying قرية, where the people of the town are meant; the relation of the trope is locality (maḥalliyya), since the place is named and what occupies it is meant. As for the first metaphor, it is the borrowing of tasting for clothing. As for the "causing to taste", it has almost come among the Arabs to be treated as literal because of its currency in the case of afflictions: they say "so-and-so tasted misery and harm", likening what is experienced of the effect of harm and pain to what is experienced of the taste of what is bitter and repugnant. As for the clothing, the comparison with it is sound because it envelops the one who wears it. The second metaphor is the borrowing of clothing for hunger and fear, as though they had surrounded them and enveloped them as a garment envelops its wearer. The building of a metaphor on a metaphor is a wide field in which thoughts go astray, and its understanding may be blocked, as it was blocked for Ibn Sinān al-Khafājī in his criticism of al-Āmidī when he dealt with the verse of Imruʾ al-Qays:
فقلت له لما تمطى بصلبه ... وأردف أعجازا وناء بكلكل
