(I said to it, when it stretched out with its back, and followed with hindquarters and rose heavily with its chest...)
Al-Āmidī said in the Kitāb al-Muwāzana: "Whoever did not know the placing of meanings or the tropes has faulted Imruʾ al-Qays for this meaning, though it is of the utmost beauty, excellence and soundness. He only intended to describe the parts of the long night: he mentioned the stretching of its middle, the heaviness of its front in departing and setting off, and the succession of its hindquarters and its ends one after another. This in my view is orderly in covering all the attributes of the long night in its shape, and that is hardest on one who watches it and awaits its passing. So when he gave it a middle that stretches, hindquarters that follow the middle, and a front that is heavy in rising, it was fine to borrow for the middle the name 'back', and to make it stretch because of its extension, since 'stretched' and 'extended' are in one position; and it was fitting to borrow for the front the name 'chest' because of its rising. These are the closest of metaphors to the literal and the most suited here to what they were borrowed for. Likewise the saying of Zuhayr:
وعرّي أفراس الصبا ورواحله
(And the horses of youth and its mounts were stripped bare.)
Since it is the way of one with youth to be described always by saying 'he rode his steed, ran in his field, bolted against his rein' and the like, it was fine to borrow for youth the name 'horses' and to make giving it up the stripping of its horses and mounts, and this metaphor too was among the most fitting for what it was borrowed for."
Ibn Sinān al-Khafājī said in his book Sirr al-Faṣāḥa about the verse of Imruʾ al-Qays:
فقلت له لما تمطى بصلبه ... وأردف أعجازا وناء بكلكل
"What al-Āmidī mentioned is not satisfactory to the utmost; the verse of Imruʾ al-Qays is neither a good metaphor nor a bad one, but a middling one. Al-Āmidī has stated plainly that Imruʾ al-Qays, when he gave the night an extended middle, borrowed for it the name 'back' and made it stretch because of its extension, and where he gave it a first part and a last part he borrowed for it a hindquarter and a chest. All of this is fine only in parts together: mentioning the back is fine only for the sake of the hindquarter and the middle, the stretching for the sake of the back, and the chest for the sum of that: a metaphor built on another metaphor." This is what the two men said about a metaphor built on another metaphor. Ibn Sinān, for all his eminence in rhetoric, overlooked the verse of the Qur'an; otherwise he would not have allowed himself to condemn this kind of metaphor.
It is related that Ibn al-Rāwandī the heretic said to Ibn al-Aʿrābī, the imam of language and literature: "Can clothing be tasted?" Ibn al-Aʿrābī said to him: "No harm, you nasnās (ape-like creature): suppose Muḥammad was not a prophet, was he not an Arab?" It was as if he had attacked the verse on the ground that what is fitting would have been to say "so Allah clothed it in the garment of hunger" or "so Allah made it taste the taste of hunger", and Ibn al-Aʿrābī replied to him. The scholars of rhetoric have answered that this is from the tajrīd (stripping) of the metaphor: he borrowed clothing for what a person fears of certain events, such as hunger and fear, because it envelops him as a garment envelops the wearer, then mentioned the attribute suited to the thing borrowed for, namely hunger and fear, because the use of tasting for the experience of hunger and fear came among them to be treated as literal; they say "so-and-so tasted misery and harm", and "another made him taste it". So the metaphor was stripped; had He said "so it clothed it", it would have been marshalled (murashshaḥa). It is said: although the marshalling of a metaphor is considered fine from the side of hyperbole, stripping has a preference in that the side of the thing borrowed for is observed, so the speech gains in clarity.

dervis-irab:114-117.t:
* I'rab:
(فَكُلُوا مِمَّا رَزَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ حَلالًا طَيِّباً) The فاء is the eloquent fāʾ (fāʾ faṣīḥa), i.e. "when the state of those who disbelieved and what their affair came to has become clear to you, then stop what you are doing, desist from ingratitude for favours, and eat and drink". ومما is attached to كلوا; the clause رزقكم is a ṣila; حلالا is a ḥāl, and you may also make it a mafʿūl bihi of كلوا; and طيبا is an adjective.
(وَاشْكُرُوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ إِيَّاهُ تَعْبُدُونَ) واشكروا نعمة الله is an imperative verb, agent and direct object; إن is conditional and كنتم is the protasis; كان and its noun; إياه is a direct object placed first for تعبدون; and the clause تعبدون is the khabar of كنتم. (إِنَّما حَرَّمَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَيْتَةَ وَالدَّمَ وَلَحْمَ الْخِنْزِيرِ وَما أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ بِهِ) إنما is a restrictive particle and the thing restricted; حرم is a verb with a latent fāʿil; عليكم, a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to حرم; الميتة is the mafʿūl bihi; الدم and الخنزير are conjoined to الميتة; وما is also conjoined; the clause أهل is a ṣila; لغير الله is a ḥāl; and به is attached to أهل. This verse has been dealt with before.
(فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ غَيْرَ باغٍ وَلا عادٍ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ) The فاء is the fāʾ of ramification (tafrīʿiyya); من is a conditional noun, jussive-governing, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ; اضطر is a passive past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis, its nāʾib fāʿil latent and referring to من; غير باغ is a ḥāl; ولا عاد is conjoined to باغ; the فاء is the connecting fāʾ; inna and its noun; غفور is its first khabar and رحيم its second; and the sentence is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis.
(وَلا تَقُولُوا لِما تَصِفُ أَلْسِنَتُكُمُ الْكَذِبَ هذا حَلالٌ وَهذا حَرامٌ لِتَفْتَرُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ) لا is prohibitive; تقولوا is an imperfect verb jussive by لا and the و is the fāʿil. In ولما تصف the lām is a preposition; ما is a maṣdar particle, which together with what follows is in the position of a genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تقولوا; ألسنتكم is the fāʿil of تصف and الكذب the object of تصف; and the clause هذا حلال is the content of what is said. The meaning is then "do not say 'this is lawful and this is unlawful' because your tongues describe falsehood", i.e. because they are accustomed to it and it runs on them; that is, do not make lawful or unlawful on account of a statement your tongues utter, which is a rejected statement that no proof supports. وهذا حرام is conjoined to هذا حلال; ولتفتروا is a badal from His saying لما تصف; وعلى الله is attached to تفتروا; and الكذب is the mafʿūl bihi of لتفتروا. It is also possible that الكذب be accusative as the object of تقولوا, with the clause هذا حلال a badal of it; ما would then be a relative noun, i.e. "do not say the falsehood about what your tongues describe, saying 'this is unlawful and this is lawful'". Both analyses are sound and permissible. Ibn Hishām cited this verse in al-Mughnī, and his words are: It was said regarding «ولا تقولوا لما تصف ألسنتكم الكذب» and «كما أرسلنا فيكم رسولا منكم» that الكذب is a badal of the omitted object of تصف, i.e. لما تصفه, and likewise رسولا, on the basis that ما in «كما» is a relative noun; this is refuted by the fact that it applies ما to a single person among those who have intellect, and the apparent view is that ما is a restrictive particle, and still clearer is that it is a maṣdar particle, so as to keep the kāf working as a genitive. It was also said of الكذب that it is the object of تقولوا, and the two clauses after it are a badal of it, i.e. "do not say the falsehood about what your tongues describe of cattle as lawful or unlawful"; and the lām is either of an omitted verb, i.e. "then you would say falsehood", or of نصف, with ما a maṣdar particle and the two clauses quoted speech, i.e. "do not make lawful and unlawful merely on a statement your tongues utter". The meaning of attributing falsehood to the tongues will come in the section on rhetoric. (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَفْتَرُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ لا يُفْلِحُونَ) inna and its noun; the clause يفترون is a ṣila; على الله is attached to يفترون; الكذب is the object of يفترون; and the clause لا يفلحون is the khabar of inna. (مَتاعٌ قَلِيلٌ وَلَهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ)
متاع is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "that deed which is their habit is an enjoyment of little benefit", or a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "they have an enjoyment"; قليل is an adjective of متاع; ولهم is a predicate placed first, عذاب a delayed mubtadaʾ, and أليم an adjective of عذاب.

* Rhetoric:
The description of the tongues as describing falsehood is a clear Arabic expression for hyperbole: because the tongues find falsehood agreeable, and it runs over them and recurs constantly in what they utter, it is as if they describe it and embody it for the hearer. Of this kind is their saying "her face describes beauty" and "her eye suggests enchantment". Or it is as if falsehood were something unknown which they must explain to people, uncovering its hidden parts. It is thus a majāz ʿaqlī (rational trope).

dervis-irab:77-82.t:
* Vocabulary:
(ظَعْنِكُمْ): Your travel. It is said ẓaʿana yaẓʿanu (pattern fataḥa), ẓaʿnan, ẓaʿanan, ẓuʿūnan and maẓʿanan: he journeyed and departed. The poet said:
أقاطن قوم سلمى أم نووا ظعنا ... إن يظعنوا فعجيب عيش من قطنا
(Are Salmā's people residents, or have they intended to depart? If they depart, wondrous is the life of those who stay.)
The rule is: every word on the pattern faʿl whose middle letter is a guttural may have its middle letter given sukūn, such as baḥr, naḥr, nahr, shaʿr and shahr. Ibn Durustawayh said in his commentary on al-Faṣīḥ: «The people of the language and most of the grammarians say: every word whose second letter is a guttural may take sukūn or fatḥa. The adept ones said: that is not correct; rather these are words with two dialects, so whoever of the Arabs gives sukūn does not give fatḥa, and whoever gives fatḥa does not give sukūn except in poetic necessity. The proof of that is that the like has come from them in much speech in which there is no guttural at all, such as al-qabḍ and al-qabaḍ, in which both fatḥa and sukūn have come.» He said: «And among what shows the falsity of what they held is that four dialects have come for al-naṭʿ; if it were because of the guttural letters, these four would be permissible in al-shaʿr, al-nahr and everything with any guttural letter in it.» He said: «Among those with two aspects whose second letter is a guttural: al-shaʿr and al-shaʿar, al-nahr and al-nahar, al-ṣakhr and al-ṣakhar, al-baʿr and al-baʿar, al-ẓaʿn and al-ẓaʿan, al-dahb and al-daʾab, al-faḥm and al-faḥam, and al-saḥr and al-saḥar for the lung. And among those with two aspects whose second letter is not a guttural: nashz of the earth and nashaz, meaning raised ground; a ṣadʿ and ṣadaʿ man, light of flesh; the night of al-nafr and al-nafar; saṭr and saṭar; qadr and qadar; lafẓ and lafaẓ; shamʿ and shamaʿ; naṭʿ and naṭaʿ; ghadhl and ghadhal; ṭard and ṭarad and ṭurd; ghabn and ghabān; dark and darak; and shabḥ and shabaḥ for the person.» And this is explicit that the way of that is hearing (samāʿ, reliance on reported usage).
(أَثاثاً): al-Athāth is the large goods of the house. Its origin is from athatha, that is, it was dense and abundant, and from it comes shaʿr athīth, meaning abundant and thick. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
وفرع يزين المتن أسود فاحم ... أثيث كقنو النخلة المتعثكل
(And a lock of hair that adorns the back, black and jet, thick like the cluster of a date-palm heavy with fruit.)
Al-Khalīl said: «al-Athāth and al-matāʿ are one, and He combined them because of the difference in their words.» If you say: there must be a difference between al-athāth and al-matāʿ for the mention of the conjunctive wāw to be correct, since conjunction requires distinctness, what is this difference? I say: al-athāth is what is abundant of the house's equipment and needs, so it includes all kinds of property, and al-matāʿ is what is benefited from in the house specifically; thus the difference between the two words is evident.
(أكنان): The plural of kinn, which is that in which one takes shelter, of houses hewn in the mountains, caves and cavities. In al-Mukhtār: «al-Kinn is a covering, and the plural is aknān. Exalted is He said: "وجعل لكم من الجبال أكنانا". And al-akinna are coverings. Exalted is He said: "وجعلنا على قلوبهم أكنة"; the singular is kinān. Al-Kisāʾī said: kanna l-shayʾ means he covered it, and its verb pattern is radda.» The mention of al-akinna has already preceded.
(سَرابِيلَ): They are shirts and clothes made of wool, linen and cotton. From it is the saying of Labīd:
الحمد لله إذ لم يأتني أجلي ... حتى اكتسيت من الإسلام سربالا
(Praise be to Allah that my appointed time did not come to me until I put on a garment of Islam.)

* I'rab:
(وَلِلَّهِ غَيْبُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَما أَمْرُ السَّاعَةِ إِلَّا كَلَمْحِ الْبَصَرِ أَوْ هُوَ أَقْرَبُ) The wāw is resumptive; لله is a fronted khabar and غيب السموات والأرض is a delayed mubtadaʾ. The wāw is a conjunction; ما is negative; أمر is a mubtadaʾ and الساعة is a muḍāf ilayhi; إلا is a particle of restriction; وكلمح البصر is its khabar; أو is a conjunction; هو is a mubtadaʾ and أقرب is its khabar.
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ) إن and its noun; على كل شيء is attached to قدير; and قدير is the khabar of inna. (وَاللَّهُ أَخْرَجَكُمْ مِنْ بُطُونِ أُمَّهاتِكُمْ) الله is a mubtadaʾ and the clause أخرجكم is the khabar; and من بطون أمهاتكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أخرجكم.
(لا تَعْلَمُونَ شَيْئاً) The clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the kāf, that is, "not knowing anything"; and شيئا is a direct object. (وَجَعَلَ لَكُمُ السَّمْعَ وَالْأَبْصارَ وَالْأَفْئِدَةَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ) وجعل is conjoined to أخرجكم, and the agent is latent, its implied form being "He". لكم is in the place of the second object of جعل, and السمع is its first object; الأبصار and الأفئدة are conjoined to it; لعل and its noun, and the clause تشكرون is its khabar.
(أَلَمْ يَرَوْا إِلَى الطَّيْرِ مُسَخَّراتٍ فِي جَوِّ السَّماءِ) The hamza is for confirmatory interrogation; لم is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; يروا is an imperfect verb jussive by لم and the wāw is the agent; إلى الطير is attached to يروا; مسخرات is a ḥāl, that is, made subservient to flight by the wings that were created for them and the suitable means for it; and في جو السماء is attached to مسخرات, that is, for soaring in the direction of height and the upper air. And (ما يُمْسِكُهُنَّ إِلَّا اللَّهُ) The clause is circumstantial; ما is negative; يمسكهن: a verb, a latent agent and a direct object; إلا is a particle of restriction; and الله is the agent. (إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآياتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ) إن and its fronted khabar, the shifted lām, and آيات is its delayed noun; لقوم is an adjective of آيات and the clause يؤمنون is an adjective of قوم. (وَاللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِنْ بُيُوتِكُمْ سَكَناً) والله is a mubtadaʾ and the clause جعل is the khabar; its first object is سكنا and its second object is one of the two prepositional phrases, and the other is a ḥāl, because it was an adjective of سكنا and was put before it. When جعل means "created", one of the two prepositional phrases is attached to it and it is content with one object; this has already been pointed out. (وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِنْ جُلُودِ الْأَنْعامِ بُيُوتاً تَسْتَخِفُّونَها يَوْمَ ظَعْنِكُمْ وَيَوْمَ إِقامَتِكُمْ) وجعل لكم من جلود الأنعام بيوتا: the i'rab of its counterpart has preceded. What is meant by houses here is the tents and structures of leather and hides, such as tents and the like; the clause تستخفونها is an adjective of بيوتا; the adverbial يوم ظعنكم is attached to تستخفونها; and يوم إقامتكم is conjoined to يوم ظعنكم.
(وَمِنْ أَصْوافِها وَأَوْبارِها وَأَشْعارِها أَثاثاً وَمَتاعاً إِلى حِينٍ) ومن أصوافها is conjoined to من جلود الأنعام, and أثاثا is conjoined to بيوتا, that is, "and He made for you from their wool furnishings", so it is a case of conjoining a preposition and its genitive noun and an accusative to the like; ومتاعا is conjoined to أثاثا, and إلى حين is attached to متاعا or is an adjective of it. (وَاللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِمَّا خَلَقَ ظِلالًا) Its i'rab has preceded. (وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِنَ الْجِبالِ أَكْناناً)
Its i'rab has also preceded. (وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ سَرابِيلَ تَقِيكُمُ الْحَرَّ) The clause تقيكم الحر is an adjective of سرابيل, and the conjoined element is omitted because it is known, that is, "and the cold". (وَسَرابِيلَ تَقِيكُمْ بَأْسَكُمْ) وسرابيل is conjoined to the first سرابيل and the clause تقيكم is an adjective; تقيكم is an imperfect verb with a latent agent, the kāf being its first object and بأسكم its second object; what is meant by it is coats of mail and cuirasses. (كَذلِكَ يُتِمُّ نِعْمَتَهُ عَلَيْكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُسْلِمُونَ) كذلك is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, and this has often preceded; يتم نعمته: a verb, a latent agent and a direct object; لعل and its noun, and the clause تسلمون is its khabar. (فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَإِنَّما عَلَيْكَ الْبَلاغُ الْمُبِينُ) The fāʾ is resumptive and إن is conditional; تولوا is the verb of the protasis, and its origin is tatawallaw, so one of the two tāʾs was dropped; it may also be a past verb, in which case there is an iltifāt in the speech, and this is perhaps preferable. The apodosis of إن is omitted, that is, "then there is no blame upon you", and the fāʾ is causal; إنما is a particle of restriction, a kāffa (preventer) and makfūfa (prevented); عليك البلاغ is a fronted khabar and a delayed mubtadaʾ; and المبين is an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
The meaning of the simile (tashbīh) here is tamthīl (representation), that is, since the Hour is bound to come, it was made, in nearness, like the twinkling of an eye. Al-lamḥ is looking quickly, and it needs a time in which the pupil turns toward what is seen, and every time is divisible. Al-Zajjāj said: «He did not mean that the Hour comes in the twinkling of an eye; he described only the speed of the power to bring it, because He says to a thing "Be", and it is.» It was said: the meaning is that it is so with Allah, even if it is not of this description with creatures.

dervis-irab:118-123.t:
* I'rab:
(وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ هادُوا حَرَّمْنا ما قَصَصْنا عَلَيْكَ مِنْ قَبْلُ) وعلى الذين is attached to حرمنا; هادوا is the ṣila of الذين; ما is the mafʿūl bihi; قصصنا is a ṣila; وعليك is attached to قصصنا; and ومن قبل is attached to حرمنا. Reference has already been made to what was forbidden specifically to the Jews, in His saying, Exalted is He: «وعلى الذين هادوا حرمنا كل ذي ظفر» to the end of the verse, in Sūrat al-Anʿām. (وَما ظَلَمْناهُمْ وَلكِنْ كانُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ) The و is a conjunction; ما is negative; ظلمناهم is verb, agent and direct object; the و is circumstantial; ولكن is the lightened form, inoperative, and so a particle of rectification (istidrāk); كانوا is kāna with its noun; أنفسهم is a direct object placed first for يظلمون; and the clause يظلمون is the khabar of كانوا. (ثُمَّ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لِلَّذِينَ عَمِلُوا السُّوءَ بِجَهالَةٍ ثُمَّ تابُوا مِنْ بَعْدِ ذلِكَ وَأَصْلَحُوا) ثم is a conjunction denoting lapse of time; inna and its noun; وللذين is its khabar, i.e. "forgiving to those who"; عملوا is a ṣila; السوء is the mafʿūl bihi; وبجهالة is in the position of a ḥāl from the و, i.e. "they did evil in ignorance"; ثم تابوا is conjoined to عملوا; ومن بعد is attached to تابوا; ذلك is added to بعد; and وأصلحوا is conjoined to تابوا.
(إِنَّ رَبَّكَ مِنْ بَعْدِها لَغَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ) inna and its noun; ومن بعدها is attached to غفور; the lām is the shifted lām; غفور is the khabar of inna and رحيم a second khabar. (إِنَّ إِبْراهِيمَ كانَ أُمَّةً قانِتاً لِلَّهِ حَنِيفاً وَلَمْ يَكُ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ) inna and its noun; the clause كان is its khabar; the noun of كان is latent, its implied form being "he", i.e. Ibrāhīm; and أمة is the khabar of كان, i.e. he was by himself a community in his own right, because there came together in him of the attributes of perfection what comes together in a community. Abū Nuwās's saying is true of him:
ليس على الله بمستنكر ... أن يجمع العالم في واحد
(It is nothing for Allah to find strange, that He should gather the world in one.)
قانتا is a second khabar of كان; لله is attached to قانتا; and حنيفا is a third khabar. ولم يك: لم is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; يك is an imperfect verb jussive by لم, its sign of jussive being sukūn, the nūn having been dropped for lightness, as has been discussed in the section on the peculiarities of kāna; the noun of يك is latent, its implied form being "he"; and من المشركين is the khabar of يك. (شاكِراً لِأَنْعُمِهِ اجْتَباهُ وَهَداهُ إِلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ) شاكرا is a fourth khabar of كان; ولأنعمه is attached to شاكرا; the clause اجتباه is a fifth khabar; وهداه is conjoined to اجتباه; والى صراط, a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to هداه; and مستقيم is an adjective of صراط.
(وَآتَيْناهُ فِي الدُّنْيا حَسَنَةً وَإِنَّهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ لَمِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ) It is conjoined to what preceded, by way of iltifāt (turning) from the third person to the first person, for greater concern for his standing. آتيناه is verb, agent and direct object; في الدنيا, a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was an adjective of حسنة; and حسنة is the second object. وإنه is inna and its noun; وفي الآخرة is attached to an omitted ḥāl; the lām is the shifted lām; and من الصالحين is the khabar of inna. (ثُمَّ أَوْحَيْنا إِلَيْكَ أَنِ اتَّبِعْ مِلَّةَ إِبْراهِيمَ حَنِيفاً وَما كانَ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ) ثم is a conjunction, and أوحينا is verb and agent. Its being conjoined with ثم, which indicates lapse of time and distance, hints at the lofty standing and high rank of Muḥammad ﷺ, and that the greatest of the favours given to Ibrāhīm was Muḥammad's following his law. وإليك is attached to أوحينا. In أن اتبع, أن is explicative (mufassira) or a maṣdar particle, in which case it is accusative by removal of the preposition; ملة إبراهيم is the object of اتبع; and حنيفا is a ḥāl from إبراهيم (the discussion of a ḥāl coming from the muḍāf ilayhi will come later). The و is a conjunction, ما is negative, كان has a latent noun, and من المشركين is its khabar.

* Benefits:
A ḥāl coming from the muḍāf ilayhi:
A ḥāl comes from the muḍāf ilayhi under three conditions: 1- that the muḍāf be a part of the muḍāf ilayhi, as in «ونزعنا ما في صدورهم من غل إخوانا», where إخوانا is a ḥāl from the muḍāf ilayhi, which is the pronoun, the breasts being a part of it; and as in «أيحب أحدكم أن يأكل لحم أخيه ميتا فكرهتموه», where ميتا is a ḥāl from الأخ, the muḍāf ilayhi of اللحم, the flesh being a part of the brother. 2- or like a part of it, as in this verse: حنيفا is a ḥāl from إبراهيم, the muḍāf ilayhi of الملة, and the milla is like a part of him in that it is sound to drop the muḍāf and put the muḍāf ilayhi in its place, since if one said واتبع إبراهيم it would be correct. 3- that the muḍāf be an operator on the ḥāl, such as being a maṣdar or an attribute, as in «إليه مرجعكم جميعا», where جميعا is a ḥāl from the kāf and mīm, the muḍāf ilayhi of مرجع, and مرجع is a maṣdar mīmī that operates, putting the ḥāl in the accusative.

dervis-irab:124-128.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّما جُعِلَ السَّبْتُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ اخْتَلَفُوا فِيهِ) إنما is a restrictive particle and the thing restricted; جعل is a passive past verb and السبت the nāʾib fāʿil; على الذين, a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to جعل, and so is in the position of the second object; the clause اختلفوا is a ṣila; and فيه is attached to اختلفوا. It has been mentioned before that the Jews opposed their prophet Mūsā, when he commanded them to honour Friday by devoting themselves to worship on it and leaving their occupations; they said, "We do not want it", and chose the Sabbath, so it was made hard for them. (وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَيَحْكُمُ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ فِيما كانُوا فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ) The و is a conjunction or resumptive; inna and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām; the clause يحكم is the khabar of inna; بينهم is attached to يحكم, as is the adverbial, which is يوم القيامة; فيما is attached to an omitted ḥāl; the clause كانوا is a ṣila; فيه is attached to يختلفون; and the clause يختلفون is the khabar of كانوا.
(ادْعُ إِلى سَبِيلِ رَبِّكَ بِالْحِكْمَةِ وَالْمَوْعِظَةِ الْحَسَنَةِ) ادع is an imperative verb whose latent fāʿil is "you"; the object is omitted, i.e. "the people"; والى سبيل ربك is attached to ادع; بالحكمة is a ḥāl, i.e. "connected with it"; and الموعظة الحسنة is conjoined to الحكمة. (وَجادِلْهُمْ بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ) وجادلهم is conjoined to ادع; the هاء is the mafʿūl bihi; بالتي is attached to ادع; هي is a mubtadaʾ and أحسن the khabar, and the nominal sentence is the ṣila of التي. (إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ ضَلَّ عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِالْمُهْتَدِينَ) inna and its noun; هو is a mubtadaʾ and أعلم the khabar, and the sentence is the khabar of inna; بمن is attached to أعلم; the clause ضل is a ṣila; وعن سبيله is attached to ضل; هو is a mubtadaʾ and أعلم the khabar; and بالمهتدين is attached to أعلم. (وَإِنْ عاقَبْتُمْ فَعاقِبُوا بِمِثْلِ ما عُوقِبْتُمْ بِهِ) The و is resumptive; إن is conditional; عاقبتم is a past verb, the ت being the fāʿil, in the position of a jussive as the protasis. In فعاقبوا the فاء is the connecting fāʾ; عاقبوا is an imperative verb and agent; بمثل, a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to عاقبوا; ما is a muḍāf ilayhi; the clause عوقبتم is a ṣila; به is attached to عوقبتم; and the clause فعاقبوا is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis.
(وَلَئِنْ صَبَرْتُمْ لَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لِلصَّابِرِينَ) The lām prepares for the oath; إن is conditional and صبرتم is in the position of a jussive as the protasis; the lām occurs in the apodosis of the oath because it precedes, as has been discussed before; هو is a mubtadaʾ and خير the khabar; and للصابرين is attached to خير.
(وَاصْبِرْ وَما صَبْرُكَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ وَلا تَحْزَنْ عَلَيْهِمْ) In واصبر the و is resumptive and اصبر is an imperative verb with a latent fāʿil. In وما صبرك the و is circumstantial, ما is negative, صبرك is a mubtadaʾ, إلا is a particle of restriction, and بالله is the khabar; the و is a conjunction, لا is prohibitive, تحزن is an imperfect verb jussive by لا, and عليهم is attached to تحزن. (وَلا تَكُ فِي ضَيْقٍ مِمَّا يَمْكُرُونَ) The و is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; تك is an imperfect verb jussive by لا, its sign of jussive being the sukūn implied on the nūn which was dropped for lightness; the noun of تك is latent, its implied form being "you"; في ضيق is the khabar of تك; ومما is an adjective of ضيق; and the clause يمكرون is a ṣila.
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ مُحْسِنُونَ) inna and its noun; مع is an adverbial of place attached to an omitted khabar; الذين is the muḍāf ilayhi; اتقوا is a ṣila; والذين is conjoined to الذين; هم is a mubtadaʾ and محسنون the khabar, and the sentence is a ṣila.

* Rhetoric:
The closing verses of Sūrat al-Naḥl:
His saying, Exalted is He, «ولا تك في ضيق»: it may be from reversed speech (kalām maqlūb), because narrowness (ḍayq) is an attribute that is in a person and the person is not in it; or it may be meant that there is a simile in the speech, narrowness having been likened to a thing that surrounds a person. This is among the marvels of expression and the comprehensive words. Hence it is related of Ibrāhīm ibn Ḥayyān that when he was dying it was said to him, "Make a bequest." He said: "A bequest is from property, and I have no property, but I bequeath to you the closing verses of Sūrat al-Naḥl."

dervis-irab:83-86.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يُسْتَعْتَبُونَ): They are asked to be pleased (yustarḍawna). The expressions of the exegetes differ about it, so let us return to the books of the language. It is said in al-Mukhtār: «ʿataba ʿalayhi means he was angry with him, and its verb pattern is ḍaraba and naṣara; also maʿtaban with fatḥa on the tāʾ; and al-taʿattub is like al-ʿatb, and the noun is al-maʿtaba with fatḥa or kasra on the tāʾ. Al-Khalīl said: al-ʿitāb is speaking with familiarity and recalling displeasure. ʿātabahu muʿātabatan and ʿitāban; and aʿtabahu means he pleased him after having wronged him, and the noun from it is al-ʿutbā. Istaʿtaba and aʿtaba are alike in meaning. Istaʿtaba also means he asked to be pleased: you say istaʿtabahu fa-aʿtabahu, that is, he asked him to be pleased and he pleased him.» And in al-Asās: «istaʿtabahu means he asked him to be pleased: "وما بعد الموت مستعتب" ("and after death there is no pleasing"). Between them is an aʿtūba if they reproach one another. You say: I heard from her an aʿtūba, it was nothing but a marvel (aʿjūba). And "your reproach is the sword"; and "I reproached grey hair". Al-Nābigha said:
على حين عاتبت المشيب على الصبا ... وقلت: ألمّا أصح والشيب وازع
(At the time when I reproached grey hair for youthful folly and said: have I not yet become sober, while grey hair is a restrainer?)
that is, I said to grey hair: how ugly of you to be inclined to folly. And ʿalā is a complement of ʿātabtu, as you say ʿātabtuhu ʿalā l-dhanb (I reproached him for the sin).»
(نَبْعَثُ): We send. In al-Qāmūs and elsewhere: baʿathahu yabʿathuhu (pattern fataḥa), baʿthan and tibʿāthan means he sent him alone, and baʿatha bihi means he sent him with another. By this the correctness of Abū l-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī in his saying becomes clear:
فآجرك الإله على عليل ... بعثت إلى المسيح به طبيبا
(So may the Lord reward you for an invalid for whom you sent a physician to the Messiah.)
Al-Ṣāḥib erred in his criticism of this verse, because he made baʿatha transitive with bi- on the pretext that baʿatha takes a rational being directly and a non-rational one with bi-. His bias against Abū l-Ṭayyib turned him away from reflecting on the story of the verse. For al-Wāḥidī mentioned in his book: «I heard the Shaykh Karīm ibn al-Faḍl say: I heard my father Abū Bishr, the chief judge, say: Abū l-Ḥusayn al-Shāmī, nicknamed al-Mushawwaq, recited to me; he said: I was with al-Mutanabbī when the agent of ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Sayyār ibn Mukram came, and he loved poetry (al-ramy, as written in the source). When he came in to him he recited to him some feeble verses. So al-Mutanabbī composed his splendid ode in praise of ʿAlī ibn Mukram, whose opening is:
ضروب الناس عشاق ضروبا ... فأعذرهم أشفهم حبيبا
(Kinds of people are lovers of kinds; the most excusable of them is the one whose beloved is most healing.)
In it he describes himself with verses of unending beauty, which we record in what follows:
أعزمي طال هذا الليل فانظر ... أمنك الصبح يفرق أن يئوبا
(O my resolve, this night has grown long, so look: does the dawn fear returning because of you?)
كأن الفجر حبّ مستزار ... يراعي من دجنته رقيبا
(As if the dawn were a beloved who is visited, watching in its gloom for a spy.)
كأن نجومه حلي عليه ... وقد حذيت قوائمه الجبوبا
(As if its stars were jewels upon it, while its legs have been shod with the earth.)
كأن الجو قاسى ما أقاسي ... فصار سواده فيه شحوبا
(As if the air suffered what I suffer, so its blackness became pallor in it.)
كأن دجاه يجذبها سهادي ... فليس تغيب إلا أن تغيبا
(As if my sleeplessness were pulling its darkness, so that it does not set unless it is made to set.)
أقلب فيه أجفاني كأني ... أعد به على الدهر ألذ نوبا
(I turn my eyelids in it as if I were counting against Time its most pleasurable turns.)
وما ليل بأطول من نهار ... يظل بلحظ حسادي مشوبا
(And no night is longer than a day that remains mixed with the glances of my enviers.)
وما موت بأبغض من حياة ... أرى لهم معي فيها نصيبا
(And no death is more hateful than a life in which I see them having a share with me.)
Then he turns to the praise of ʿAlī ibn Mukram and alludes to the story of his agent, the feeble poet:
تيممني وكيلك مادحا لي ... وأنشدني من الشعر الغريبا
(Your agent made for me, praising me, and recited to me strange poetry.)
فآجرك الإله على عليل ... بعثت إلى المسيح به طبيبا
(So may the Lord reward you for an invalid for whom you sent a physician to the Messiah.)
And he expressed him by a non-rational thing (the bi- construction), because he made baʿth transitive by the preposition; or he was among the gifts that were sent to him, but a disagreeable gift, as he says:
ولست بمنكر منك الهدايا ... ولكن زدتني فيها أديبا
(I do not disown gifts from you, but you have added to me in them a man of letters.)
As for the verses of the agent, they are trivial and metrically incorrect, which is why we passed them over.»

* I'rab:
(يَعْرِفُونَ نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ ثُمَّ يُنْكِرُونَها وَأَكْثَرُهُمُ الْكافِرُونَ) يعرفون نعمة الله: يعرفون is an imperfect verb and the wāw is the agent, and نعمة الله is a direct object. ثم is a conjunction of delay; ينكرونها is conjoined to يعرفون, and he conjoined with ثم to indicate that their denial is a thing far-fetched after the availability of the proofs of recognition. وأكثرهم: the wāw is circumstantial, أكثرهم is a mubtadaʾ and الكافرون is its khabar, or the reverse, that is, they used to recognise and then deviate. (وَيَوْمَ نَبْعَثُ مِنْ كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ شَهِيداً) The adverbial is attached to an omitted element, "mention", and the clause نبعث is annexed to the adverbial; من كل أمة is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of شهيدا; and شهيدا is a direct object. (ثُمَّ لا يُؤْذَنُ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَلا هُمْ يُسْتَعْتَبُونَ) ثم is a conjunction of delay; لا is negative; يؤذن is a passive imperfect verb and للذين is attached to it. Opinions differ about this permission, and the soundest is that they will not be permitted to make excuses, especially as it has a parallel in the Qur'an, namely His saying «ولا يؤذن لهم فيعتذرون». ولا: the wāw is a conjunction and لا is negative; هم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يستعتبون is the khabar. He conjoined with ثم only because of the length of the period whose outcome was their being prevented from speaking. (وَإِذا رَأَى الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا الْعَذابَ) The wāw is a conjunction; إذا is a future adverbial including the meaning of a condition; the clause رأى is annexed to the adverbial; الذين is the agent of رأى, and the clause ظلموا is a ṣila; العذاب is a direct object; and the fāʾ links the apodosis of إذا. (فَلا يُخَفَّفُ عَنْهُمْ وَلا هُمْ يُنْظَرُونَ) The fāʾ links the apodosis of إذا; لا is negative; يخفف is a passive imperfect verb, and the deputy agent is latent, that is, "the punishment"; لا is a conjunction; هم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause ينظرون is the khabar. (وَإِذا رَأَى الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا شُرَكاءَهُمْ) The like of it has preceded; and شركاءهم is the object of رأى. (قالُوا رَبَّنا هؤُلاءِ شُرَكاؤُنَا الَّذِينَ كُنَّا نَدْعُوا مِنْ دُونِكَ) The clause قالوا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of إذا; ربنا is a vocative, a muḍāf from which the vocative particle has been omitted; هؤلاء is a mubtadaʾ and شركاؤنا is the khabar; الذين is an adjective of شركاؤنا and the clause كنا is a ṣila; كان and its noun, and the clause ندعو is the khabar of كنا; and من دونك is a ḥāl from the omitted object of ندعو, that is, "we called them and worshipped them besides You".
(فَأَلْقَوْا إِلَيْهِمُ الْقَوْلَ إِنَّكُمْ لَكاذِبُونَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; ألقوا is a verb and an agent, and it is the partners; إليهم is attached to ألقوا; القول is a direct object; إنكم لكاذبون: inna and its noun, the shifted lām and its khabar, and the clause is the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

dervis-irab:53-60.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تَجْئَرُونَ): you supplicate humbly. Al-juʾār, on the pattern of al-zukām, is raising the voice in supplication and appeal for help. Al-Aʿshā said, describing a monk:
يراوح من صلوات المليك طورا سجودا وطورا جؤارا
(He alternates in the prayers to the King, at times in prostration and at times in loud supplication.)
Al-murāwaḥa in work is moving from one state to another, and do not let the precision of this description escape you. Before it:
وما آبلي على هيكل ... بناه وصلب فيه وصارا
(Nor is the Ābilī monk at a temple that he built, in which he set a cross and images.)
The Ābilī is the monk, relating to Ābil, who is the custodian of the church; and ṣallaba means he drew the cross. In al-Qāmūs: "jaʾara (like manaʿa), jaʾran and juʾāran (on the pattern of ghurāb): he raised his voice in supplication, entreated and cried for help; of a cow or bull, it bellowed; of vegetation, jaʾran: it grew tall; of the land, its vegetation grew tall."
(ظَلَّ) here means "became", and it is not in its usual sense of indicating remaining in the daytime in the state predicated of its noun; on either reading it is an incomplete verb (kāna's sister), and its maṣdar is al-ẓulūl. It is also permissible to keep it in its original meaning, which is a thing's being characterised by some attribute in the daytime only, because circumstances are alike at night, i.e. "he spends the whole span of his day grieved, his face dark from dejection and shame before people."
(كَظِيمٌ): filled with rage against the female. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "kaẓamtu al-ghayẓa kaẓman (like ḍaraba) and kuẓūman: you held back what was in yourself of it, in forbearance or rage. In the Revelation: ﴿والكاظمين الغيظ﴾. Sometimes one says kaẓamtu ʿalā al-ghayẓ and kaẓamanī al-ghayẓ, so I am kaẓīm and makẓūm. And the camel kaẓama kuẓūman: it did not chew the cud."
(هُونٍ): abasement and humiliation. Al-Yazīdī said: al-hūn is abasement in the dialect of Quraysh. Abū ʿUbayd related the same from al-Kisāʾī, and al-Kisāʾī related that it is affliction and hardship. Al-Khansāʾ said:
نهين النفوس وهون النفو ... س يوم الكريهة أبقى لها
(We hold our souls cheap, and holding souls cheap on the day of battle is what preserves them the more.)

* I'rab:
(وَما بِكُمْ مِنْ نِعْمَةٍ فَمِنَ اللَّهِ) ما is conditional, in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; the protasis verb is omitted; بكم is attached to the omitted protasis verb; and من نعمة is a ḥāl from the conditional noun, while Abū al-Baqāʾ preferred that it be a ḥāl from the pronoun in the preposition and its genitive noun; the fāʾ is the connector of the apodosis; and من الله is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, the implied form being "it is from Allah", and the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, and the omitted protasis verb together with the apodosis is in the position of nominative as the khabar of ما. It is also permissible that ما be a relative noun, a mubtadaʾ, the preposition and its genitive noun being its ṣila, and the khabar being His words فمن الله, the fāʾ being a connector because the relative contains the sense of the condition, the implied form being "whatever has settled upon you". More discussion of the omission of the protasis verb and the apodosis will come under Benefits. (ثُمَّ إِذا مَسَّكُمُ الضُّرُّ فَإِلَيْهِ تَجْئَرُونَ) ثم is a conjunction; إذا is a future adverb containing the sense of the condition, attached to the apodosis تجأرون; the clause مسكم is annexed to the adverb; مسكم is a verb with a fronted direct object; الضر is a postponed agent; the fāʾ is a connector; واليه is attached to تجأرون; تجأرون is an imperfect verb and agent; and the clause فإليه تجأرون has no position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (ثُمَّ إِذا كَشَفَ الضُّرَّ عَنْكُمْ إِذا فَرِيقٌ مِنْكُمْ بِرَبِّهِمْ يُشْرِكُونَ) ثم is a conjunction; the first إذا is a future adverb containing the sense of the condition, attached to what is contained in the second إذا of the sense of surprise; and it is not permissible that the operator in إذا be the apodosis, because what comes after the sudden إذا does not operate on what precedes it; the clause كشف is annexed; الضر is a direct object; عنكم is attached to كشف; and the second إذا is a sudden one with no position, and it has been discussed before; فريق is a mubtadaʾ, and it is allowable to begin with it because it is qualified by His words منهم; بربهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يشركون; and the clause يشركون is the khabar of فريق. It is strange that Abū al-Baqāʾ blundered by analogising the sudden إذا to the conditional إذا, saying "فريق is the agent of an omitted verb", and this collapses from its foundation. (لِيَكْفُرُوا بِما آتَيْناهُمْ فَتَمَتَّعُوا فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ) ليكفروا: the lām is the lām of purpose (taʿlīl), and يكفروا is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied أن after the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يشركون, i.e. their association is caused by their disbelief in their Lord. The lām may also be the lām of consequence (ṣayrūra or ʿāqiba), i.e. the end result of their associating others with Allah is their disbelief in the favour, which is the removal of harm from them; in that case what is attached to ليكفروا is an omitted khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; بما is attached to يكفروا; the clause آتيناهم is a ṣila; فتمتعوا is a clause governed by an omitted saying, i.e. "Say to them, Muḥammad: enjoy yourselves"; فسوف تعلمون: the fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ; سوف is a particle of futurity; and تعلمون is a verb and agent, whose object is omitted, its implied form being "the consequence of that". (وَيَجْعَلُونَ لِما لا يَعْلَمُونَ نَصِيباً مِمَّا رَزَقْناهُمْ) It is conjoined to what precedes; يجعلون is an imperfect verb and agent; لما is attached to يجعلون; the clause لا يعلمون is a ṣila of ما; and the pronoun in يعلمون refers to the polytheists, and the returning pronoun is omitted, to be implied as "that they harm and do not benefit"; or you may make it refer to the idols, indicated by ما, i.e. things not described as having knowledge, which do not perceive whether they have been given a share in their livestock and crops or not; نصيبا is the object of يجعلون; مما is an adjective of نصيبا; and the clause رزقناهم is a ṣila. (تَاللَّهِ لَتُسْئَلُنَّ عَمَّا كُنْتُمْ تَفْتَرُونَ) The tāʾ is the tāʾ of oath that governs the genitive; the Glorious Name is genitive by the tāʾ of oath, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "my oath"; the lām occurs in the answer of the oath; تسألن is an imperfect verb nominative, its sign of nominative being the presence of the nūn, which has been omitted because of the succession of identical letters, and the wāw, omitted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the agent; the doubled nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis; parallels to this parsing have gone before; عما is attached to تسألن; the clause كنتم is a ṣila; and the clause تفترون is the khabar of كنتم. (وَيَجْعَلُونَ لِلَّهِ الْبَناتِ سُبْحانَهُ وَلَهُمْ ما يَشْتَهُونَ) ويجعلون is conjoined to what precedes; لله is attached to يجعلون; البنات is the object of يجعلون; سبحانه is accusative as a maṣdar of an omitted verb, and the clause is parenthetical because it is in the sense of a verb, and it occurs in the midst of the discourse, because His words, the Exalted, ولهم ما يشتهون are conjoined to His words لله البنات in the opinion of al-Zamakhsharī and al-Farrāʾ; ولهم is a fronted khabar; ما is a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause يشتهون is a ṣila; some of them parsed ما as in the position of accusative [Translator's note: the text reads "an implied verb", presumably meaning the object of an implied verb]; and the clause ولهم ما يشتهون is either resumptive or a ḥāl. You may also conjoin ما to البنات and لهم to لله, making it a case of conjoining single words, and this is the opinion of al-Zamakhsharī and al-Farrāʾ; Abū Ḥayyān followed them up, saying: "They overlooked a rule of grammar, which is that when a verb takes a pronoun as its agent and a pronoun in the accusative follows it, the verb may not make it accusative unless it belongs to the chapter of ẓanna and its sisters among the verbs of the heart, or to faqada and ʿadima, so it is permissible to say 'Zayd ẓannahu qāʾiman', meaning he thought himself standing; but if you said 'Zayd ḍarabahu', putting in ḍaraba a nominative pronoun referring to Zayd while it also governs the accusative pronoun, it would not be permissible, and the genitive pronoun is treated like the accusative, so if you said 'Zayd ghaḍiba ʿalayhi' it would not be permissible, just as 'Zayd ḍarabahu' is not; hence it is impossible that their saying لهم be attached to يجعلون."
(وَإِذا بُشِّرَ أَحَدُهُمْ بِالْأُنْثى ظَلَّ وَجْهُهُ مُسْوَدًّا وَهُوَ كَظِيمٌ) The wāw is a ḥāl from the pronoun of يجعلون, i.e. how do they find it palatable to ascribe daughters to Him, the Exalted, while this is their own condition; إذا is a future adverb containing the sense of the condition; the clause بشر أحدهم is annexed to the adverb; بالأنثى is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to بشر; the clause ظل has no position; وجهه is the noun of ظل; مسودا is its khabar; the wāw is also a ḥāl; وهو is a mubtadaʾ; كظيم is a khabar; and the clause is a nested ḥāl. What is meant is not the blackness that is the opposite of whiteness, but a metonymy using blackness for the change and dejection that result from grief; the Arabs say of everyone who meets something disagreeable "his face has turned black with grief and sorrow", as al-Zajjāj said. Al-Māwardī said: rather, what is meant is blackness of colour in truth, and he said that it is the saying of the majority. The first is preferable, since it is known by experience that one who is angry, sad and grieved undergoes in his colour only a mere change and an appearance of dejection and gloom, not true blackness. (يَتَوارى مِنَ الْقَوْمِ مِنْ سُوءِ ما بُشِّرَ بِهِ) The clause يتوارى is a ḥāl from the pronoun in كظيم; من القوم is attached to it; and من سوء is attached to it also, the first being for the beginning of the action and the second for the cause; ما is a relative noun annexed to سوء; and the clause بشر به is a ṣila, that is, the female and her evil according to their beliefs, that she is exposed to seduction and they fear for her fornication and the fact that she does not earn. (أَيُمْسِكُهُ عَلى هُونٍ أَمْ يَدُسُّهُ فِي التُّرابِ) The hamza is interrogative; the interrogative clause يمسكه is governed by an omitted something that is a ḥāl from the agent of يتوارى, i.e. "he hides, bewildered, hesitating, wavering between certainty and doubt: shall he keep her, bearing the humiliation, or bury her alive?"; يمسكه is an imperfect verb, latent agent and direct object; على هون is a ḥāl from the latent agent or from the direct object; أم is a conjunction; ويدسه is conjoined to يمسكه; في التراب is attached to يدسه; and the masculine in يمسكه and يدسه, although it refers to the female, is out of regard for the word.
(أَلا ساءَ ما يَحْكُمُونَ) ألا is a particle of alert; ساء is a past verb to express censure; ما is an indefinite noun, accusative as tamyīz, or a relative as the agent of ساء, and the clause يحكمون is a ṣila; you may also make it maṣdariyya, with the interpreted maṣdar the agent, i.e. "evil is their judgement".
(لِلَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ مَثَلُ السَّوْءِ وَلِلَّهِ الْمَثَلُ الْأَعْلى وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ) للذين is a fronted khabar; the clause لا يؤمنون is a ṣila; بالآخرة is attached to يؤمنون; مثل السوء is a postponed mubtadaʾ; ولله المثل الأعلى is conjoined to what precedes; وهو is a mubtadaʾ; العزيز is a first khabar; and الحكيم is a second khabar.

* Benefits:
Omission of the protasis verb and its apodosis:
What is known from the conditional may be omitted if the particle is إن joined to the negative لا, as in the saying of al-Aḥwaṣ addressing Maṭar, who was ugly in form and had under him a handsome wife:
فطلّقها فلست لها بكفء ... وإلّا يعل مفرقك الحسام
(Divorce her, for you are no match for her; and if not, the sword will rise over the parting of your hair.)
He omitted the protasis verb because his words «فطلقها» point to it and left its apodosis, i.e. "and if you do not divorce her, it will rise". Because of these conditions some exegetes prevented parsing «وما بكم من نعمة فمن الله» as conditional and were content to make it relative; but the grammarians reported that these conditions are not binding, since one of the two may be missing, either إن or the association with لا, and both may be missing together. The first is what Ibn al-Anbārī related in al-Inṣāf from the Arabs: "man yusallim ʿalayka fa-sallim ʿalayhi, wa-man lā fa-lā taʿbaʾ bihi", i.e. "and whoever does not greet you, take no notice of him". Al-Shāṭibī said: this is an explicit text for permissibility. The second is as in «وإن امرأة خافت من بعلها», where the protasis is omitted although the association of إن with لا is absent. The third is as in the line:
متى تؤخذوا قسرا بظنة عامر ... ولم ينج إلا في الصفاد يزيد
(Whenever you are seized by force on suspicion concerning ʿĀmir, while Yazīd escaped only in fetters.)
i.e. "whenever you are overtaken you will be seized", so the protasis was omitted with both conditions absent. It is also permissible to omit what is known of the apodosis of a past-tense condition, as in «فإن استطعت أن تبتغي نفقا في الأرض أو سلما في السماء فتأتيهم بآية»: فإن استطعت is a condition whose apodosis is omitted because the speech indicates it, the implied form being "so do it", and the second condition with its apodosis is the apodosis of the first condition. The meaning is: if you are able to find a passage beneath the earth through which you may pass and so bring them a sign, or a ladder by which you may ascend to the sky and descend from it with a sign, then do it. The detail of that will come in its places.
Here is the wording of Ibn Hishām in al-Mughnī. He said, in discussing the conditional ما: "It has been permitted in «وما بكم من نعمة فمن الله», on the basis that the original is 'whatever there is' (wa-mā yakun), and then the protasis verb was omitted, as in the line:
إن العقل في أموالنا لا نضق بها ... ذراعا وإن صبرا فنصبر للصبر
(As for the blood-money in our wealth, we do not become narrow in arm over it; and if it be patience, we will be patient for patience's sake.)
i.e. 'if it is the blood-money' and 'if we are to be confined by confinement'. The more probable view in the verse is that it is relative and that the fāʾ enters the khabar, not that it is conditional with the fāʾ entering the apodosis."

dervis-irab:61-64.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مُفْرَطُونَ): passive participle of afraṭa, i.e. he hastened. One says: afraṭtu fulānan and farraṭtuhu fī ṭalab al-māʾ when you sent him ahead. It was also said: forgotten, abandoned, from afraṭtu fulānan khalfī when you left him behind and forgot him. In al-Mukhtār: "faraṭa al-qawm: he preceded them to the water, so he is a fāriṭ and the plural is furrāṭ on the pattern of kitāb (its type is naṣara); afraṭahu: he left him, and from it comes His words, the Exalted, «وأنهم مفرطون», i.e. abandoned in the Fire, forgotten; and afraṭa fī al-amr: he exceeded the limit in it." In al-Qāmūs: "afraṭa fulānan: he left him, preceded him, exceeded the limit and was hasty in the matter; and «وأنهم مفرطون» means forgotten, abandoned in the Fire, or sent ahead, hastened into it."
In the hadith, from Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "I am your forerunner (faraṭ) at the Pool; whoever passes by me drinks, and whoever drinks will never be thirsty. Some people will come to me whom I know and who know me, then a barrier will be set between me and them." Al-Quṭāmī said:
فاستعجلونا وكانوا من صحابتنا ... كما تعجل فراط لورّاد
(They hurried us, and they were among our companions, as forerunners hurry for those coming to the water.)

* I'rab:
(وَلَوْ يُؤاخِذُ اللَّهُ النَّاسَ بِظُلْمِهِمْ ما تَرَكَ عَلَيْها مِنْ دَابَّةٍ) The wāw is resumptive; لو is conditional; يؤاخذ الله الناس is an imperfect verb, agent and direct object; بظلمهم: the bāʾ is a preposition of causation, i.e. because of their wrongdoing, attached to يؤاخذ; the clause ما ترك has no position; ترك is a verb with a latent agent; عليها is attached to an omitted ḥāl because it was an adjective of دابة; من is a redundant preposition; and دابة is genitive in form and a direct object in position; the pronoun refers to the earth, even though it was not mentioned, for the mention of people and the mention of the creature indicate it, since all of them rest upon the earth.
(وَلكِنْ يُؤَخِّرُهُمْ إِلى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى) The wāw is a conjunction; لكن is a particle of rectification, inoperative because it is the lightened form; يؤخرهم is an imperfect verb, latent agent and direct object; إلى أجل is attached to يؤخرهم; and مسمى is an adjective, i.e. appointed. (فَإِذا جاءَ أَجَلُهُمْ لا يَسْتَأْخِرُونَ ساعَةً وَلا يَسْتَقْدِمُونَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction or resumptive; إذا is a future adverb containing the sense of the condition; the clause جاء أجلهم is annexed to the adverb; the clause لا يستأخرون has no position; ساعة is an adverb attached to يستأخرون; and ولا يستقدمون is conjoined to لا يستأخرون; reference has gone before, in a similar verse, to the meaning of لا يستأخرون ولا يستقدمون. (وَيَجْعَلُونَ لِلَّهِ ما يَكْرَهُونَ وَتَصِفُ أَلْسِنَتُهُمُ الْكَذِبَ) ويجعلون is an imperfect verb and agent; لله is attached to يجعلون; ما is the object of يجعلون; the clause يكرهون is a ṣila; and تصف ألسنتهم الكذب is an imperfect verb, agent and direct object, and the lie has been explained by His words: (أَنَّ لَهُمُ الْحُسْنى) so أن and what is in its scope are a substitute for الكذب, a total substitute (badal al-kull min al-kull); لهم is the fronted khabar of أن; and الحسنى is its postponed noun. (لا جَرَمَ أَنَّ لَهُمُ النَّارَ وَأَنَّهُمْ مُفْرَطُونَ) The discussion of لا جرم has gone before; أن with its fronted khabar and postponed noun; and وإنهم مفرطون is conjoined to أن لهم النار. (تَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا إِلى أُمَمٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ) The tāʾ is the tāʾ of oath and the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the implied oath verb; the lām occurs in the answer of the oath; qad is a particle of certainty; أرسلنا is a verb and agent; إلى أمم is attached to أرسلنا; and من قبلك is an adjective. (فَزَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الشَّيْطانُ أَعْمالَهُمْ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; زين is a past verb; لهم is attached to زين; الشيطان is the agent; and أعمالهم is the direct object. (فَهُوَ وَلِيُّهُمُ الْيَوْمَ وَلَهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; هو is a mubtadaʾ; وليهم is a khabar; اليوم is an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl if you intend to narrate the future state or this world, or attached to وليهم if you intend to narrate the past state in which Satan was adorning their deeds for them, with وليهم in the sense of their helper and supporter; لهم is a fronted khabar; عذاب is a postponed mubtadaʾ; and أليم is an adjective. (وَما أَنْزَلْنا عَلَيْكَ الْكِتابَ إِلَّا لِتُبَيِّنَ لَهُمُ الَّذِي اخْتَلَفُوا فِيهِ) The wāw is a conjunction; ما is negative; أنزلنا is a verb and agent; عليك is attached to أنزلنا; الكتاب is a direct object; إلا is a particle of restriction; لتبين: the lām is the lām of purpose, and what it governs is attached to أنزلنا in the sense of purpose. The object of purpose (mafʿūl li-ajlihi) is made genitive with the lām only because its agent differs from the agent of the verb, since the one who sent down is Allah and the one who makes clear is the Prophet. (وَهُدىً وَرَحْمَةً لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ) هدى and رحمة are conjoined to the position of لتبين, and both are accusative as objects of purpose because their agent is the same as the agent of the verb, since the Guide and the Merciful is Allah, as He is the One who sent down; لقوم is an adjective or attached to the maṣdar; and the clause يؤمنون is an adjective of قوم.

* Benefits:
An important discussion of the fāʾ of succession (fāʾ al-taʿqīb):
What is known of the conjunctive fāʾ is that it is for conjunction with succession, but not immediate succession; rather it is for succession as is sound either rationally or customarily. Hence it is sound to say "I entered Basra and then Baghdad" even if much time lay between them, but the entering of the latter followed the entering of the former as far as possible, meaning that he did not stay in Wāsiṭ, for example, for a year or a long period, but traversed the stages after Basra and did not settle in any of them with a stay that takes him out of the bounds of travel until he entered Baghdad. This is what the people of the language and the people of uṣūl say, and the fāʾ is not for true immediacy, whose meaning is that this happens after this without separation or time. Do you not see His words, the Exalted, «فإذا جاء أجلهم»: the coming of their term is delayed from the deferral. Parallels to this will come.

dervis-irab:87-90.t:
* I'rab:
(وَأَلْقَوْا إِلَى اللَّهِ يَوْمَئِذٍ السَّلَمَ) The wāw is a conjunction; ألقوا is a verb and an agent, and it is the disbelievers; إلى الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ألقوا; يومئذ is an adverbial annexed to a similar adverbial, and the tanwīn is a compensation for a clause, and examples of this have often passed; السلم is a direct object. (وَضَلَّ عَنْهُمْ ما كانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; ضل is a past verb and عنهم is attached to it; ما is the agent of ضل and the clause كانوا is a ṣila; كان and its noun, and the clause يفترون is the khabar of كانوا. (الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ زِدْناهُمْ عَذاباً فَوْقَ الْعَذابِ بِما كانُوا يُفْسِدُونَ) الذين is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause زدناهم, and the clause كفروا is a ṣila; وصدوا عن سبيل الله is conjoined to كفروا. زدناهم: a verb, an agent and a direct object; عذابا is a second direct object; فوق العذاب is an adverbial attached to an omitted adjective of عذابا; بما is attached to زدناهم, and the bāʾ is causal, and ما is maṣdar-forming, that is, "because of their turning away and their corruption"; and كان and its noun, and the clause يفسدون is its khabar.
(وَيَوْمَ نَبْعَثُ فِي كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ شَهِيداً عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ أَنْفُسِهِمْ) The adverbial is attached to an omitted element, its implied form being "mention"; this clause has been repeated as hyperbole in threat and warning. The clause نبعث is annexed to the adverbial; في كل أمة is attached to نبعث; شهيدا is a direct object; عليهم is attached to شهيدا; and من أنفسهم is an adjective of شهيدا. (وَجِئْنا بِكَ شَهِيداً عَلى هؤُلاءِ) وجئنا: the wāw is a conjunction and جئنا is a verb and an agent; بك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to جئنا; شهيدا is a ḥāl; and على هؤلاء is attached to شهيدا.
(وَنَزَّلْنا عَلَيْكَ الْكِتابَ تِبْياناً لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَهُدىً وَرَحْمَةً وَبُشْرى لِلْمُسْلِمِينَ) ونزلنا is conjoined to جئنا and نا is the agent; عليك is attached to نزلنا; الكتاب is a direct object; تبيانا is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi or a ḥāl, that is, "making clear"; لكل شيء is attached to تبيانا; هدى, رحمة and بشرى are conjoined to تبيانا; and للمسلمين is attached to بشرى, and it is attached in meaning to the other preceding maṣdars.
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُ بِالْعَدْلِ وَالْإِحْسانِ وَإِيتاءِ ذِي الْقُرْبى) إن and its noun, and the clause يأمر is the khabar of inna; بالعدل is attached to يأمر; الإحسان is conjoined to العدل, and likewise إيتاء; and ذي القربى is annexed to إيتاء. (وَيَنْهى عَنِ الْفَحْشاءِ وَالْمُنْكَرِ وَالْبَغْيِ يَعِظُكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ) وينهى is conjoined to يأمر and the agent is latent; عن الفحشاء is attached to ينهى and what follows is conjoined to it; the clause يعظكم is a ḥāl from the agent of يأمر and ينهى; and لعل and its noun, and the clause تذكرون, that is, tatadhakkarūn, is its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
The scholars of rhetoric and the exegetes all agreed that this verse is the most comprehensive verse in the Qur'an for good and evil, namely His saying, Exalted is He: «إن الله يأمر بالعدل والإحسان إلخ». ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, the righteous caliph, ordered its recitation in place of the cursing of Imam ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib that used to follow the Friday sermons, and because of it ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn became a Muslim. It is reported that the Prophet ﷺ recited it to al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, who said to him: "O son of my brother, repeat it." So the Prophet ﷺ repeated its recitation to him, and he said to him: "It has sweetness, it has charm, its top is fruitful and its bottom is abundant, and it is not the speech of a human being."
In reality it contains varieties of rhetoric, which we explain in what follows:
1- Concision (al-ījāz): At the beginning of the verse He commanded every good deed, then after that forbade every evil deed, and concluded the verse with the most eloquent admonitions, framing that in the most concise expressions.
2- Soundness of division (ṣiḥḥat al-taqsīm): He covered in it all divisions of the meaning, so that no good deed remains that does not fall within the scope of the command, and no evil deed remains that does not fall within the range of the prohibition. He put the mention of justice first because it is obligatory and followed it with benevolence because it is recommended, so that the arrangement of the speech might fall in the finest order. He coupled them in the command because the obligatory is not free of some defect and shortcoming which the recommended and supererogatory make good. And He singled out the kinsfolk for mention after their inclusion in the generality of those whom one is commanded to treat with justice and benevolence, to show the excellence of the kinsfolk and the excellence of the reward upon it.
3- Verbal antithesis (ṭibāq) and contrast (muqābala): between "commands" and "forbids", between justice, benevolence and giving to kinsfolk, and between indecency, wrongdoing and oppression.
4- Beauty of arrangement (ḥusn al-nasaq): in the ordering of the clauses and their conjoining one with another as is fitting, where He put justice first and conjoined benevolence to it, since benevolence is a general noun and giving to kinsfolk is specific, so it is as if it were a kind of that genus; then He brought the clause of command first and conjoined the clause of prohibition to it.
5- Tasḥīm (the opening indicates the end): because the beginning of the speech points to its end, as the beginning of a "striped" verse points to its end.
6- Beauty of exposition (ḥusn al-bayān): because the one who hears the wording of the verse does not hesitate in understanding its meaning, as it is free of obscurity in its wording and points to its meaning clearly by the nearest and easiest ways, and the intelligent and the dull are equal in understanding it.
7- Harmony (al-iʾtilāf): because every word is such that no other can take its place.
8- Equivalence (al-musāwāt): because the words of the speech are moulds for its meanings, neither exceeding them nor falling short of them.
9- Firm placing of the rhyme-ending (tamkīn al-fāṣila): because the closing of the verse sits settled in its place, firm in its resting place, its meaning connected to what precedes up to the beginning of the speech; and because admonition is not good except after the charge of making the command and prohibition clear; and because whichever word you remove from the words of the verse, the meaning is plainly disturbed by its removal and clearly diminished.

dervis-irab:91-93.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تَوْكِيدِها): Their ratification. Al-Tawkīd is the maṣdar of wakkada yuwakkidu with wāw, and in it is another dialect, akkada yuʾakkidu with hamza, and its meaning is strengthening. This is like their saying warrakhtu l-kitāb and arrakhtuhu (I dated the book); the hamza is not a replacement for a wāw, as some claimed, because the two usages in the two roots are equal, so claiming that one of them is the origin is no better than the other.
(أَنْكاثاً): The plural of nikth, with kasra on the nūn, which is that whose twisting has been undone. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «nakatha l-rajulu l-ʿahd nakthan (pattern qatala) means he broke it and cast it aside, so it was undone (intakatha), like naqaḍahu fa-ntaqaḍa; and nakatha l-kisāʾ and others means he also unravelled it. And al-nikth, with kasra, is what is unravelled in order to be spun a second time, and the plural is ankāth, like ḥiml and aḥmāl.» And in al-Qāmūs: «al-Nikth, with kasra, is what is unravelled of cloaks and tents to be spun a second time, and its plural is ankāth. It is said: ḥablun nikthun and ankāthun, that is, an unravelled rope (mankūth).»
(دَخَلًا): Corruption and treachery (daghal). In al-Ṣiḥāḥ: «al-Daghal, vocalised, is corruption, like al-dakhal.» In the dictionaries: «al-Dakhal is a defect.» In al-Qāmūs and al-Tāj: «al-Dakhal, with two fatḥas, is the corruption that enters a person in intellect or body; deceit; a flaw in lineage; and people who ascribe themselves to those they are not of. Among the strange things about the letters dāl and khāʾ is that they do not come together except to point to corruption or darkness: al-dakh and al-dukh, with fatḥa or ḍamma on the dāl, is smoke, and enough for you is its darkness and dinginess. A Bedouin woman said to her husband, who had grown old:
لا خير في الشيخ إذا ما اجلخا ... وسال غرب عينه ولخا
وكان أكلا قاعدا وشخا ... تحت رواق البيت يغشى الدخا
وانثنت الرجل فصارت فخا ... وصار وصل الغانيات أخا
(There is no good in an old man when he grows bent, and the tear-duct of his eye runs and is gummed; when he is an eater, sitting, passing water under the awning of the tent, enveloped in smoke; when his leg is bent and becomes a snare, and the favour of fair women becomes for him a brother's [mere kinship].)
And dakhara means he became abased and small, and adkharahu means he abased him. Dakhisa l-ḥāfir, with kasra on the khāʾ, means the hoof was struck by the disease of al-dakhas, with sukūn on the khāʾ, which is a swelling in the hoof; and al-dukhas, with ḍamma on the dāl and sukūn on the khāʾ, is a creature of the sea. Al-Dakhīs is the entangled part of pasture; and when it is entangled it nears blackness and large number, and the plump flesh. Tadākhalat al-umūr means the affairs became confused and resembled each other. And al-dakhl, with fatḥa on the dāl and sukūn on the khāʾ, is what comes in to you of your wealth, and its opposite is al-kharj (expenditure); it is a corruption for its owner unless he pays its zakāh and what follows from it, and from it the income tax was named. Dukhla (with the three vowels on the dāl) of a man is his inner part, hidden in the darkness of concealment. Al-Dakhīl is one who has entered a people and ascribed himself to them but is not of them, so he is in confusion about his affair and is seldom righteous; and "a dakhīl disease" means one entering the depths of the body; and every foreign word that has been brought into the speech of the Arabs. Dakhamahu means he pushed him with disturbance. Dakhkhana l-ṭaʿām wa-l-laḥm and the like means smoke reached it while it was cooked or grilled, so the smell of smoke overcame its taste, so it is dakhin. Al-Dakhan, with two fatḥas, is rancour, corruption, and a change of mind, religion and lineage. It is said: "I will not make peace with him on a dakhan", that is, on deceit and corruption. Al-Dukhiyy, with fatḥa on the shaddated dāl, is darkness, and a dukhyāʾ night is dark. And this is among the wonders of languages.»
(أَرْبى): More numerous in number and more abundant in wealth.

* I'rab:
(وَأَوْفُوا بِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ إِذا عاهَدْتُمْ) The wāw is a conjunction; أوفوا is an imperative verb and an agent; بعهد الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أوفوا; إذا is a future adverbial including the meaning of a condition; and the clause عاهدتم is annexed to the adverbial. (وَلا تَنْقُضُوا الْأَيْمانَ بَعْدَ تَوْكِيدِها وَقَدْ جَعَلْتُمُ اللَّهَ عَلَيْكُمْ كَفِيلًا) The wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; تنقضوا is an imperfect verb jussive by لا and the wāw is the agent; الأيمان is a direct object; بعد is an adverbial attached to تنقضوا; توكيدها is a muḍāf ilayhi; the wāw is circumstantial and the clause is a ḥāl from the agent of تنقضوا; قد is a particle of certainty; جعلتم الله: a verb, an agent and a direct object; عليكم is attached to كفيلا; and كفيلا is a second direct object of جعلتم. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ ما تَفْعَلُونَ) The i'rab of its like has often preceded. (وَلا تَكُونُوا كَالَّتِي نَقَضَتْ غَزْلَها مِنْ بَعْدِ قُوَّةٍ أَنْكاثاً) The wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive and تكونوا is jussive by it; كان and its noun, and the kāf is its khabar; the clause نقضت is a ṣila; غزلها is a direct object; من بعد قوة is a ḥāl from the agent of نقضت or from its object, that is, "making it firm" or "made firm"; and أنكاثا is accusative by an omitted verb, that is, "and so she made it ankāth", or because نقضت is made to include the meaning of "she turned into", in which case it is a second object. Al-Zajjāj allowed another aspect for it, namely accusative as a maṣdar, because the meaning of naqaḍat is nakathat, so it agrees in meaning with its governor. It was also said that it is a ḥāl from غزلها, that is, "unravelled". The story of this woman will come in the section on Benefits. (تَتَّخِذُونَ أَيْمانَكُمْ دَخَلًا بَيْنَكُمْ أَنْ تَكُونَ أُمَّةٌ هِيَ أَرْبى مِنْ أُمَّةٍ) The clause تتخذون is a ḥāl from the pronoun of تكونوا, that is, "do not be like her, taking your oaths as a means of deceit"; تتخذون is an imperfect verb and an agent; أيمانكم is a first direct object and دخلا is a second direct object; بينكم is an adjective of دخلا; أن and what is within its scope is an interpreted maṣdar in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl li-ajlihi, that is, "for fear that there should be"; أمة is the noun of تكون, هي is a mubtadaʾ and أربى its khabar, and the clause is the khabar of تكون; and من أمة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أربى. They used to make alliances with allies and cut agreements and covenants, and when they found others more numerous and mightier in side, they broke the alliance of the former and allied with the latter.
(إِنَّما يَبْلُوكُمُ اللَّهُ بِهِ وَلَيُبَيِّنَنَّ لَكُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ ما كُنْتُمْ فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ) إنما is a kāffa and makfūfa, and it is for restriction; يبلوكم الله: a verb, a fronted object and a delayed agent; به is attached to يبلوكم. وليبيننّ: the wāw is a conjunction, the lām is the preparatory lām of the oath, and يبينّ is an imperfect verb indeclinable on fatḥa because of the obligatory attachment of the heavy nūn of emphasis; لكم is attached to يبينن; يوم القيامة is an adverbial attached to an omitted ḥāl; ما is a direct object; كنتم is a ṣila, being kāna and its noun; فيه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تختلفون; and the clause تختلفون is the khabar of كنتم. (وَلَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ لَجَعَلَكُمْ أُمَّةً واحِدَةً) The wāw is a conjunction; لو is conditional; شاء الله is a verb and an agent; the lām occurs in the apodosis of لو; جعلكم is a verb, a latent agent and a first direct object; أمة is a second direct object; and واحدة is an adjective. (وَلكِنْ يُضِلُّ مَنْ يَشاءُ وَيَهْدِي مَنْ يَشاءُ) The wāw is circumstantial; لكن is a particle of rectification, inoperative because it has been lightened; يضل is an imperfect verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "He"; من is a direct object and يشاء is a ṣila; and ويهدي من يشاء is conjoined to what preceded. (وَلَتُسْئَلُنَّ عَمَّا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; the lām is the preparatory lām of the oath; تسألن is an imperfect verb that is declined, because the nūn did not directly attach to it, so it is nominative, and the sign of its nominative is the presence of the nūn that has been omitted because of the succession of similar letters; the wāw, omitted because of the meeting of two sukūns, is the deputy agent; the doubled nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis; عما is attached to تسألن; and the clause كنتم تعملون is the khabar of كنتم.

* Benefits:
History reports that a foolish woman named Rayṭa bint Saʿd ibn Taymī, of Mecca, took a spindle about a cubit long, a hook like a finger and a great whorl proportionate to it, and she would spin, she and her maidservants, from the morning until noon, then order them and they would unravel what they had spun. So the speech is a representational simile (tashbīh tamthīlī) in unrestricted form (mursal), and the thing likened to is specified.
